125// This helper class can be used to mock out Google Test failure reporting
126// so that we can test Google Test or code that builds on Google Test.
127//
128// An object of this class appends a TestPartResult object to the
129// TestPartResultArray object given in the constructor whenever a Google Test
130// failure is reported. It can either intercept only failures that are
131// generated in the same thread that created this object or it can intercept
132// all generated failures. The scope of this mock object can be controlled with
133// the second argument to the two arguments constructor.
134class GTEST_API_ ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter
135 : public TestPartResultReporterInterface {
136 public:
137 // The two possible mocking modes of this object.
138 enum InterceptMode {
139 INTERCEPT_ONLY_CURRENT_THREAD, // Intercepts only thread local failures.
140 INTERCEPT_ALL_THREADS // Intercepts all failures.
141 };
142
143 // The c'tor sets this object as the test part result reporter used
144 // by Google Test. The 'result' parameter specifies where to report the
145 // results. This reporter will only catch failures generated in the current
146 // thread. DEPRECATED
147 explicit ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter(TestPartResultArray* result);
148
149 // Same as above, but you can choose the interception scope of this object.
150 ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter(InterceptMode intercept_mode,
151 TestPartResultArray* result);
152
153 // The d'tor restores the previous test part result reporter.
154 virtual ~ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter();
155
156 // Appends the TestPartResult object to the TestPartResultArray
157 // received in the constructor.
158 //
159 // This method is from the TestPartResultReporterInterface
160 // interface.
161 virtual void ReportTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& result);
162 private:
163 void Init();
164
165 const InterceptMode intercept_mode_;
166 TestPartResultReporterInterface* old_reporter_;
167 TestPartResultArray* const result_;
168
169 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter);
170};

174// A helper class for implementing EXPECT_FATAL_FAILURE() and
175// EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE(). Its destructor verifies that the given
176// TestPartResultArray contains exactly one failure that has the given
177// type and contains the given substring. If that's not the case, a
178// non-fatal failure will be generated.
179class GTEST_API_ SingleFailureChecker {
180 public:
181 // The constructor remembers the arguments.
182 SingleFailureChecker(const TestPartResultArray* results,
183 TestPartResult::Type type, const std::string& substr);
184 ~SingleFailureChecker();
185 private:
186 const TestPartResultArray* const results_;
187 const TestPartResult::Type type_;
188 const std::string substr_;
189
190 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(SingleFailureChecker);
191};

199// A set of macros for testing Google Test assertions or code that's expected
200// to generate Google Test fatal failures. It verifies that the given
201// statement will cause exactly one fatal Google Test failure with 'substr'
202// being part of the failure message.
203//
204// There are two different versions of this macro. EXPECT_FATAL_FAILURE only
205// affects and considers failures generated in the current thread and
206// EXPECT_FATAL_FAILURE_ON_ALL_THREADS does the same but for all threads.
207//
208// The verification of the assertion is done correctly even when the statement
209// throws an exception or aborts the current function.
210//
211// Known restrictions:
212// - 'statement' cannot reference local non-static variables or
213// non-static members of the current object.
214// - 'statement' cannot return a value.
215// - You cannot stream a failure message to this macro.
216//
217// Note that even though the implementations of the following two
218// macros are much alike, we cannot refactor them to use a common
219// helper macro, due to some peculiarity in how the preprocessor
220// works. The AcceptsMacroThatExpandsToUnprotectedComma test in
221// gtest_unittest.cc will fail to compile if we do that.
222#define EXPECT_FATAL_FAILURE(statement, substr) \
223 do { \
224 class GTestExpectFatalFailureHelper {\
225 public:\
226 static void Execute() { statement; }\
227 };\
228 ::testing::TestPartResultArray gtest_failures;\
229 ::testing::internal::SingleFailureChecker gtest_checker(\
230 &gtest_failures, ::testing::TestPartResult::kFatalFailure, (substr));\
231 {\
232 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter gtest_reporter(\
233 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter:: \
234 INTERCEPT_ONLY_CURRENT_THREAD, &gtest_failures);\
235 GTestExpectFatalFailureHelper::Execute();\
236 }\
237 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
238
239#define EXPECT_FATAL_FAILURE_ON_ALL_THREADS(statement, substr) \
240 do { \
241 class GTestExpectFatalFailureHelper {\
242 public:\
243 static void Execute() { statement; }\
244 };\
245 ::testing::TestPartResultArray gtest_failures;\
246 ::testing::internal::SingleFailureChecker gtest_checker(\
247 &gtest_failures, ::testing::TestPartResult::kFatalFailure, (substr));\
248 {\
249 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter gtest_reporter(\
250 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter:: \
251 INTERCEPT_ALL_THREADS, &gtest_failures);\
252 GTestExpectFatalFailureHelper::Execute();\
253 }\
254 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
255
256// A macro for testing Google Test assertions or code that's expected to
257// generate Google Test non-fatal failures. It asserts that the given
258// statement will cause exactly one non-fatal Google Test failure with 'substr'
259// being part of the failure message.
260//
261// There are two different versions of this macro. EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE only
262// affects and considers failures generated in the current thread and
263// EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE_ON_ALL_THREADS does the same but for all threads.
264//
265// 'statement' is allowed to reference local variables and members of
266// the current object.
267//
268// The verification of the assertion is done correctly even when the statement
269// throws an exception or aborts the current function.
270//
271// Known restrictions:
272// - You cannot stream a failure message to this macro.
273//
274// Note that even though the implementations of the following two
275// macros are much alike, we cannot refactor them to use a common
276// helper macro, due to some peculiarity in how the preprocessor
277// works. If we do that, the code won't compile when the user gives
278// EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE() a statement that contains a macro that
279// expands to code containing an unprotected comma. The
280// AcceptsMacroThatExpandsToUnprotectedComma test in gtest_unittest.cc
281// catches that.
282//
283// For the same reason, we have to write
284// if (::testing::internal::AlwaysTrue()) { statement; }
285// instead of
286// GTEST_SUPPRESS_UNREACHABLE_CODE_WARNING_BELOW_(statement)
287// to avoid an MSVC warning on unreachable code.
288#define EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE(statement, substr) \
289 do {\
290 ::testing::TestPartResultArray gtest_failures;\
291 ::testing::internal::SingleFailureChecker gtest_checker(\
292 &gtest_failures, ::testing::TestPartResult::kNonFatalFailure, \
293 (substr));\
294 {\
295 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter gtest_reporter(\
296 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter:: \
297 INTERCEPT_ONLY_CURRENT_THREAD, &gtest_failures);\
298 if (::testing::internal::AlwaysTrue()) { statement; }\
299 }\
300 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
301
302#define EXPECT_NONFATAL_FAILURE_ON_ALL_THREADS(statement, substr) \
303 do {\
304 ::testing::TestPartResultArray gtest_failures;\
305 ::testing::internal::SingleFailureChecker gtest_checker(\
306 &gtest_failures, ::testing::TestPartResult::kNonFatalFailure, \
307 (substr));\
308 {\
309 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter gtest_reporter(\
310 ::testing::ScopedFakeTestPartResultReporter::INTERCEPT_ALL_THREADS, \
311 &gtest_failures);\
312 if (::testing::internal::AlwaysTrue()) { statement; }\
313 }\
314 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
315

533// Parses a string for an Int32 flag, in the form of "--flag=value".
534//
535// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns

537GTEST_API_ bool ParseInt32Flag(

540// Returns a random seed in range [1, kMaxRandomSeed] based on the
541// given --gtest_random_seed flag value.
542inline int GetRandomSeedFromFlag(Int32 random_seed_flag) {
543 const unsigned int raw_seed = (random_seed_flag == 0) ?
544 static_cast<unsigned int>(GetTimeInMillis()) :
545 static_cast<unsigned int>(random_seed_flag);
546
547 // Normalizes the actual seed to range [1, kMaxRandomSeed] such that
548 // it's easy to type.
549 const int normalized_seed =
550 static_cast<int>((raw_seed - 1U) %
551 static_cast<unsigned int>(kMaxRandomSeed)) + 1;
552 return normalized_seed;
553}
554
555// Returns the first valid random seed after 'seed'. The behavior is
556// undefined if 'seed' is invalid. The seed after kMaxRandomSeed is
557// considered to be 1.
558inline int GetNextRandomSeed(int seed) {
559 GTEST_CHECK_(1 <= seed && seed <= kMaxRandomSeed)
560 << "Invalid random seed " << seed << " - must be in [1, "
561 << kMaxRandomSeed << "].";
562 const int next_seed = seed + 1;
563 return (next_seed > kMaxRandomSeed) ? 1 : next_seed;
564}

566// This class saves the values of all Google Test flags in its c'tor, and
567// restores them in its d'tor.
568class GTestFlagSaver {
569 public:
570 // The c'tor.
571 GTestFlagSaver() {
572 also_run_disabled_tests_ = GTEST_FLAG(also_run_disabled_tests);
573 break_on_failure_ = GTEST_FLAG(break_on_failure);
574 catch_exceptions_ = GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions);
575 color_ = GTEST_FLAG(color);
576 death_test_style_ = GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style);
577 death_test_use_fork_ = GTEST_FLAG(death_test_use_fork);
578 filter_ = GTEST_FLAG(filter);
579 param_filter_ = GTEST_FLAG(param_filter);
580 internal_run_death_test_ = GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test);
581 list_tests_ = GTEST_FLAG(list_tests);
582 output_ = GTEST_FLAG(output);
583 print_time_ = GTEST_FLAG(print_time);
584 print_utf8_ = GTEST_FLAG(print_utf8);
585 random_seed_ = GTEST_FLAG(random_seed);
586 repeat_ = GTEST_FLAG(repeat);
587 shuffle_ = GTEST_FLAG(shuffle);
588 stack_trace_depth_ = GTEST_FLAG(stack_trace_depth);
589 stream_result_to_ = GTEST_FLAG(stream_result_to);
590 throw_on_failure_ = GTEST_FLAG(throw_on_failure);
591 }
592
593 // The d'tor is not virtual. DO NOT INHERIT FROM THIS CLASS.
594 ~GTestFlagSaver() {
595 GTEST_FLAG(also_run_disabled_tests) = also_run_disabled_tests_;
596 GTEST_FLAG(break_on_failure) = break_on_failure_;
597 GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions) = catch_exceptions_;
598 GTEST_FLAG(color) = color_;
599 GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) = death_test_style_;
600 GTEST_FLAG(death_test_use_fork) = death_test_use_fork_;
601 GTEST_FLAG(filter) = filter_;
602 GTEST_FLAG(param_filter) = param_filter_;
603 GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test) = internal_run_death_test_;
604 GTEST_FLAG(list_tests) = list_tests_;
605 GTEST_FLAG(output) = output_;
606 GTEST_FLAG(print_time) = print_time_;
607 GTEST_FLAG(print_utf8) = print_utf8_;
608 GTEST_FLAG(random_seed) = random_seed_;
609 GTEST_FLAG(repeat) = repeat_;
610 GTEST_FLAG(shuffle) = shuffle_;
611 GTEST_FLAG(stack_trace_depth) = stack_trace_depth_;
612 GTEST_FLAG(stream_result_to) = stream_result_to_;
613 GTEST_FLAG(throw_on_failure) = throw_on_failure_;
614 }

639// Converts a Unicode code point to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.

641// wide enough to contain a code point.

643// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) it will be converted
644// to "(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)".

647// Converts a wide string to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.

649// UTF-16 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 2 (on Windows, Cygwin, Symbian OS)
650// UTF-32 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 4 (on Linux)
651// Parameter str points to a null-terminated wide string.
652// Parameter num_chars may additionally limit the number
653// of wchar_t characters processed. -1 is used when the entire string
654// should be processed.
655// If the string contains code points that are not valid Unicode code points
656// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) they will be output
657// as '(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)'. If the string is in UTF16 encoding
658// and contains invalid UTF-16 surrogate pairs, values in those pairs
659// will be encoded as individual Unicode characters from Basic Normal Plane.
660GTEST_API_ std::string WideStringToUtf8(const wchar_t* str, int num_chars);

690// STL container utilities.
691
692// Returns the number of elements in the given container that satisfy
693// the given predicate.
694template <class Container, typename Predicate>
695inline int CountIf(const Container& c, Predicate predicate) {
696 // Implemented as an explicit loop since std::count_if() in libCstd on
697 // Solaris has a non-standard signature.
698 int count = 0;
699 for (typename Container::const_iterator it = c.begin(); it != c.end(); ++it) {
700 if (predicate(*it))
701 ++count;
702 }
703 return count;
704}
705
706// Applies a function/functor to each element in the container.
707template <class Container, typename Functor>
708void ForEach(const Container& c, Functor functor) {
709 std::for_each(c.begin(), c.end(), functor);
710}
711
712// Returns the i-th element of the vector, or default_value if i is not
713// in range [0, v.size()).
714template <typename E>
715inline E GetElementOr(const std::vector<E>& v, int i, E default_value) {
716 return (i < 0 || i >= static_cast<int>(v.size())) ? default_value : v[i];
717}
718
719// Performs an in-place shuffle of a range of the vector's elements.
720// 'begin' and 'end' are element indices as an STL-style range;
721// i.e. [begin, end) are shuffled, where 'end' == size() means to
722// shuffle to the end of the vector.
723template <typename E>
724void ShuffleRange(internal::Random* random, int begin, int end,
725 std::vector<E>* v) {
726 const int size = static_cast<int>(v->size());
727 GTEST_CHECK_(0 <= begin && begin <= size)
728 << "Invalid shuffle range start " << begin << ": must be in range [0, "
729 << size << "].";
730 GTEST_CHECK_(begin <= end && end <= size)
731 << "Invalid shuffle range finish " << end << ": must be in range ["
732 << begin << ", " << size << "].";
733
734 // Fisher-Yates shuffle, from
735 // http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher-Yates_shuffle
736 for (int range_width = end - begin; range_width >= 2; range_width--) {
737 const int last_in_range = begin + range_width - 1;
738 const int selected = begin + random->Generate(range_width);
739 std::swap((*v)[selected], (*v)[last_in_range]);
740 }
741}
742
743// Performs an in-place shuffle of the vector's elements.
744template <typename E>
745inline void Shuffle(internal::Random* random, std::vector<E>* v) {
746 ShuffleRange(random, 0, static_cast<int>(v->size()), v);
747}

775// Class UnitTestOptions.

778// specifies when running the tests. It has only static members.

781// environment variable or a command line flag. E.g. you can set the
782// test filter using either GTEST_FILTER or --gtest_filter. If both
783// the variable and the flag are present, the latter overrides the
784// former.
785class GTEST_API_ UnitTestOptions {
786 public:
787 // Functions for processing the gtest_output flag.

793 // default (test_detail.xml in the original working directory) if
794 // none was explicitly specified.

797 // Functions for processing the gtest_filter flag.
798
799 // Returns true iff the wildcard pattern matches the string. The
800 // first ':' or '\0' character in pattern marks the end of it.
801 //
802 // This recursive algorithm isn't very efficient, but is clear and
803 // works well enough for matching test names, which are short.
804 static bool PatternMatchesString(const char *pattern, const char *str);
805
806 // Returns true iff the user-specified filter matches the test case
807 // name and the test name.
808 static bool FilterMatchesTest(const std::string &test_case_name,

811#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
812 // Function for supporting the gtest_catch_exception flag.
813
814 // Returns EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER if Google Test should handle the
815 // given SEH exception, or EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH otherwise.
816 // This function is useful as an __except condition.
817 static int GTestShouldProcessSEH(DWORD exception_code);
818#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
819
820 // Returns true if "name" matches the ':' separated list of glob-style
821 // filters in "filter".
822 static bool MatchesFilter(const std::string& name, const char* filter);

829// The role interface for getting the OS stack trace as a string.
830class OsStackTraceGetterInterface {
831 public:
832 OsStackTraceGetterInterface() {}
833 virtual ~OsStackTraceGetterInterface() {}
834
835 // Returns the current OS stack trace as an std::string. Parameters:
836 //
837 // max_depth - the maximum number of stack frames to be included
838 // in the trace.
839 // skip_count - the number of top frames to be skipped; doesn't count
840 // against max_depth.
841 virtual std::string CurrentStackTrace(int max_depth, int skip_count) = 0;
842
843 // UponLeavingGTest() should be called immediately before Google Test calls
844 // user code. It saves some information about the current stack that
845 // CurrentStackTrace() will use to find and hide Google Test stack frames.
846 virtual void UponLeavingGTest() = 0;
847
848 // This string is inserted in place of stack frames that are part of
849 // Google Test's implementation.
850 static const char* const kElidedFramesMarker;
851
852 private:
853 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(OsStackTraceGetterInterface);
854};
855
856// A working implementation of the OsStackTraceGetterInterface interface.
857class OsStackTraceGetter : public OsStackTraceGetterInterface {
858 public:
859 OsStackTraceGetter() {}
860
861 virtual std::string CurrentStackTrace(int max_depth, int skip_count);
862 virtual void UponLeavingGTest();
863
864 private:
865#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
866 Mutex mutex_; // Protects all internal state.
867
868 // We save the stack frame below the frame that calls user code.
869 // We do this because the address of the frame immediately below
870 // the user code changes between the call to UponLeavingGTest()
871 // and any calls to the stack trace code from within the user code.
872 void* caller_frame_ = nullptr;
873#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
874
875 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(OsStackTraceGetter);
876};

1051 // type_param: the name of the test's type parameter, or NULL if
1052 // this is not a typed or a type-parameterized test.
1053 // set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test case
1054 // tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test case

1060 // Adds a TestInfo to the unit test.
1061 //
1062 // Arguments:
1063 //
1064 // set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test case
1065 // tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test case
1066 // test_info: the TestInfo object
1067 void AddTestInfo(Test::SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc,
1068 Test::TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc,
1069 TestInfo* test_info) {
1070#if OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
1071 // In order to support thread-safe death tests, we need to
1072 // remember the original working directory when the test program
1073 // was first invoked. We cannot do this in RUN_ALL_TESTS(), as
1074 // the user may have changed the current directory before calling
1075 // RUN_ALL_TESTS(). Therefore we capture the current directory in
1076 // AddTestInfo(), which is called to register a TEST or TEST_F
1077 // before main() is reached.
1078 if (original_working_dir_.IsEmpty()) {
1079 original_working_dir_.Set(FilePath::GetCurrentDir());
1080 GTEST_CHECK_(!original_working_dir_.IsEmpty())
1081 << "Failed to get the current working directory.";
1082 }
1083#endif
1084
1085 GetTestCase(test_info->test_case_name(),
1086 test_info->type_param(),
1087 set_up_tc,
1088 tear_down_tc)->AddTestInfo(test_info);
1089 }

1382// Attempts to parse a string into a positive integer pointed to by the
1383// number parameter. Returns true if that is possible.
1384// GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST implies that we have ::std::string, so we can use
1385// it here.
1386template <typename Integer>
1387bool ParseNaturalNumber(const ::std::string& str, Integer* number) {
1388 // Fail fast if the given string does not begin with a digit;
1389 // this bypasses strtoXXX's "optional leading whitespace and plus
1390 // or minus sign" semantics, which are undesirable here.
1391 if (str.empty() || !IsDigit(str[0])) {
1392 return false;
1393 }
1394 errno = 0;
1395
1396 char* end;
1397 // BiggestConvertible is the largest integer type that system-provided
1398 // string-to-number conversion routines can return.
1399
1400# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !defined(__GNUC__)
1401
1402 // MSVC and C++ Builder define __int64 instead of the standard long long.
1403 typedef unsigned __int64 BiggestConvertible;
1404 const BiggestConvertible parsed = _strtoui64(str.c_str(), &end, 10);
1405
1406# else
1407
1408 typedef unsigned long long BiggestConvertible; // NOLINT
1409 const BiggestConvertible parsed = strtoull(str.c_str(), &end, 10);
1410
1411# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !defined(__GNUC__)
1412
1413 const bool parse_success = *end == '\0' && errno == 0;
1414
1415 // FIXME: Convert this to compile time assertion when it is
1416 // available.
1417 GTEST_CHECK_(sizeof(Integer) <= sizeof(parsed));
1418
1419 const Integer result = static_cast<Integer>(parsed);
1420 if (parse_success && static_cast<BiggestConvertible>(result) == parsed) {
1421 *number = result;
1422 return true;
1423 }
1424 return false;
1425}
1426#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST

1452#if GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
1453
1454// Streams test results to the given port on the given host machine.
1455class StreamingListener : public EmptyTestEventListener {
1456 public:
1457 // Abstract base class for writing strings to a socket.
1458 class AbstractSocketWriter {
1459 public:
1460 virtual ~AbstractSocketWriter() {}
1461
1462 // Sends a string to the socket.
1463 virtual void Send(const std::string& message) = 0;
1464
1465 // Closes the socket.
1466 virtual void CloseConnection() {}
1467
1468 // Sends a string and a newline to the socket.
1469 void SendLn(const std::string& message) { Send(message + "\n"); }
1470 };
1471
1472 // Concrete class for actually writing strings to a socket.
1473 class SocketWriter : public AbstractSocketWriter {
1474 public:
1475 SocketWriter(const std::string& host, const std::string& port)
1476 : sockfd_(-1), host_name_(host), port_num_(port) {
1477 MakeConnection();
1478 }
1479
1480 virtual ~SocketWriter() {
1481 if (sockfd_ != -1)
1482 CloseConnection();
1483 }
1484
1485 // Sends a string to the socket.
1486 virtual void Send(const std::string& message) {
1487 GTEST_CHECK_(sockfd_ != -1)
1488 << "Send() can be called only when there is a connection.";
1489
1490 const int len = static_cast<int>(message.length());
1491 if (write(sockfd_, message.c_str(), len) != len) {
1492 GTEST_LOG_(WARNING)
1493 << "stream_result_to: failed to stream to "
1494 << host_name_ << ":" << port_num_;
1495 }
1496 }
1497
1498 private:
1499 // Creates a client socket and connects to the server.
1500 void MakeConnection();
1501
1502 // Closes the socket.
1503 void CloseConnection() {
1504 GTEST_CHECK_(sockfd_ != -1)
1505 << "CloseConnection() can be called only when there is a connection.";
1506
1507 close(sockfd_);
1508 sockfd_ = -1;
1509 }
1510
1511 int sockfd_; // socket file descriptor
1512 const std::string host_name_;
1513 const std::string port_num_;
1514
1515 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(SocketWriter);
1516 }; // class SocketWriter
1517
1518 // Escapes '=', '&', '%', and '\n' characters in str as "%xx".
1519 static std::string UrlEncode(const char* str);
1520
1521 StreamingListener(const std::string& host, const std::string& port)
1522 : socket_writer_(new SocketWriter(host, port)) {
1523 Start();
1524 }
1525
1526 explicit StreamingListener(AbstractSocketWriter* socket_writer)
1527 : socket_writer_(socket_writer) { Start(); }
1528
1529 void OnTestProgramStart(const UnitTest& /* unit_test */) {
1530 SendLn("event=TestProgramStart");
1531 }
1532
1533 void OnTestProgramEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test) {
1534 // Note that Google Test current only report elapsed time for each
1535 // test iteration, not for the entire test program.
1536 SendLn("event=TestProgramEnd&passed=" + FormatBool(unit_test.Passed()));
1537
1538 // Notify the streaming server to stop.
1539 socket_writer_->CloseConnection();
1540 }
1541
1542 void OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& /* unit_test */, int iteration) {
1543 SendLn("event=TestIterationStart&iteration=" +
1544 StreamableToString(iteration));
1545 }
1546
1547 void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test, int /* iteration */) {
1548 SendLn("event=TestIterationEnd&passed=" +
1549 FormatBool(unit_test.Passed()) + "&elapsed_time=" +
1550 StreamableToString(unit_test.elapsed_time()) + "ms");
1551 }
1552
1553 void OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& test_case) {
1554 SendLn(std::string("event=TestCaseStart&name=") + test_case.name());
1555 }
1556
1557 void OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& test_case) {
1558 SendLn("event=TestCaseEnd&passed=" + FormatBool(test_case.Passed())
1559 + "&elapsed_time=" + StreamableToString(test_case.elapsed_time())
1560 + "ms");
1561 }
1562
1563 void OnTestStart(const TestInfo& test_info) {
1564 SendLn(std::string("event=TestStart&name=") + test_info.name());
1565 }
1566
1567 void OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& test_info) {
1568 SendLn("event=TestEnd&passed=" +
1569 FormatBool((test_info.result())->Passed()) +
1570 "&elapsed_time=" +
1571 StreamableToString((test_info.result())->elapsed_time()) + "ms");
1572 }
1573
1574 void OnTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& test_part_result) {
1575 const char* file_name = test_part_result.file_name();
1576 if (file_name == NULL)
1577 file_name = "";
1578 SendLn("event=TestPartResult&file=" + UrlEncode(file_name) +
1579 "&line=" + StreamableToString(test_part_result.line_number()) +
1580 "&message=" + UrlEncode(test_part_result.message()));
1581 }
1582
1583 private:
1584 // Sends the given message and a newline to the socket.
1585 void SendLn(const std::string& message) { socket_writer_->SendLn(message); }
1586
1587 // Called at the start of streaming to notify the receiver what
1588 // protocol we are using.
1589 void Start() { SendLn("gtest_streaming_protocol_version=1.0"); }
1590
1591 std::string FormatBool(bool value) { return value ? "1" : "0"; }
1592
1593 const scoped_ptr<AbstractSocketWriter> socket_writer_;
1594
1595 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(StreamingListener);
1596}; // class StreamingListener
1597
1598#endif // GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_

1668static FILE* OpenFileForWriting(const std::string& output_file) {
1669 FILE* fileout = NULL;

1671 FilePath output_dir(output_file_path.RemoveFileName());

1673 if (output_dir.CreateDirectoriesRecursively()) {
1674 fileout = posix::FOpen(output_file.c_str(), "w");
1675 }
1676 if (fileout == NULL) {
1677 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Unable to open file \"" << output_file << "\"";

1679 return fileout;

1826// Generates a random number from [0, range), using a Linear
1827// Congruential Generator (LCG). Crashes if 'range' is 0 or greater
1828// than kMaxRange.
1829UInt32 Random::Generate(UInt32 range) {
1830 // These constants are the same as are used in glibc's rand(3).
1831 // Use wider types than necessary to prevent unsigned overflow diagnostics.
1832 state_ = static_cast<UInt32>(1103515245ULL*state_ + 12345U) % kMaxRange;
1833
1834 GTEST_CHECK_(range > 0)
1835 << "Cannot generate a number in the range [0, 0).";
1836 GTEST_CHECK_(range <= kMaxRange)
1837 << "Generation of a number in [0, " << range << ") was requested, "
1838 << "but this can only generate numbers in [0, " << kMaxRange << ").";
1839
1840 // Converting via modulus introduces a bit of downward bias, but
1841 // it's simple, and a linear congruential generator isn't too good
1842 // to begin with.
1843 return state_ % range;
1844}

1851// Iterates over a vector of TestCases, keeping a running sum of the
1852// results of calling a given int-returning method on each.
1853// Returns the sum.
1854static int SumOverTestCaseList(const std::vector<TestCase*>& case_list,
1855 int (TestCase::*method)() const) {
1856 int sum = 0;
1857 for (size_t i = 0; i < case_list.size(); i++) {
1858 sum += (case_list[i]->*method)();
1859 }
1860 return sum;
1861}

1933// Functions for processing the gtest_output flag.
1934
1935// Returns the output format, or "" for normal printed output.
1936std::string UnitTestOptions::GetOutputFormat() {
1937 const char* const gtest_output_flag = GTEST_FLAG(output).c_str();
1938 const char* const colon = strchr(gtest_output_flag, ':');
1939 return (colon == NULL) ?
1940 std::string(gtest_output_flag) :
1941 std::string(gtest_output_flag, colon - gtest_output_flag);
1942}
1943
1944// Returns the name of the requested output file, or the default if none
1945// was explicitly specified.
1946std::string UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile() {
1947 const char* const gtest_output_flag = GTEST_FLAG(output).c_str();
1948
1949 std::string format = GetOutputFormat();
1950 if (format.empty())
1951 format = std::string(kDefaultOutputFormat);
1952
1953 const char* const colon = strchr(gtest_output_flag, ':');
1954 if (colon == NULL)
1955 return internal::FilePath::MakeFileName(
1956 internal::FilePath(
1957 UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir()),
1958 internal::FilePath(kDefaultOutputFile), 0,
1959 format.c_str()).string();
1960
1961 internal::FilePath output_name(colon + 1);
1962 if (!output_name.IsAbsolutePath())
1963 // FIXME: on Windows \some\path is not an absolute
1964 // path (as its meaning depends on the current drive), yet the
1965 // following logic for turning it into an absolute path is wrong.
1966 // Fix it.
1967 output_name = internal::FilePath::ConcatPaths(
1968 internal::FilePath(UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir()),
1969 internal::FilePath(colon + 1));
1970
1971 if (!output_name.IsDirectory())
1972 return output_name.string();
1973
1974 internal::FilePath result(internal::FilePath::GenerateUniqueFileName(
1975 output_name, internal::GetCurrentExecutableName(),
1976 GetOutputFormat().c_str()));
1977 return result.string();
1978}

1980// Returns true iff the wildcard pattern matches the string. The
1981// first ':' or '\0' character in pattern marks the end of it.
1982//
1983// This recursive algorithm isn't very efficient, but is clear and
1984// works well enough for matching test names, which are short.
1985bool UnitTestOptions::PatternMatchesString(const char *pattern,
1986 const char *str) {
1987 switch (*pattern) {
1988 case '\0':
1989 case ':': // Either ':' or '\0' marks the end of the pattern.
1990 return *str == '\0';
1991 case '?': // Matches any single character.
1992 return *str != '\0' && PatternMatchesString(pattern + 1, str + 1);
1993 case '*': // Matches any string (possibly empty) of characters.
1994 return (*str != '\0' && PatternMatchesString(pattern, str + 1)) ||
1995 PatternMatchesString(pattern + 1, str);
1996 default: // Non-special character. Matches itself.
1997 return *pattern == *str &&
1998 PatternMatchesString(pattern + 1, str + 1);
1999 }
2000}
2001
2002bool UnitTestOptions::MatchesFilter(
2003 const std::string& name, const char* filter) {
2004 const char *cur_pattern = filter;
2005 for (;;) {
2006 if (PatternMatchesString(cur_pattern, name.c_str())) {
2007 return true;
2008 }
2009
2010 // Finds the next pattern in the filter.
2011 cur_pattern = strchr(cur_pattern, ':');
2012
2013 // Returns if no more pattern can be found.
2014 if (cur_pattern == NULL) {
2015 return false;
2016 }
2017
2018 // Skips the pattern separater (the ':' character).
2019 cur_pattern++;
2020 }
2021}
2022
2023// Returns true iff the user-specified filter matches the test case
2024// name and the test name.
2025bool UnitTestOptions::FilterMatchesTest(const std::string &test_case_name,
2026 const std::string &test_name) {
2027 const std::string& full_name = test_case_name + "." + test_name.c_str();
2028
2029 // Split --gtest_filter at '-', if there is one, to separate into
2030 // positive filter and negative filter portions
2031 const char* const p = GTEST_FLAG(filter).c_str();
2032 const char* const dash = strchr(p, '-');
2033 std::string positive;
2034 std::string negative;
2035 if (dash == NULL) {
2036 positive = GTEST_FLAG(filter).c_str(); // Whole string is a positive filter
2037 negative = "";
2038 } else {
2039 positive = std::string(p, dash); // Everything up to the dash
2040 negative = std::string(dash + 1); // Everything after the dash
2041 if (positive.empty()) {
2042 // Treat '-test1' as the same as '*-test1'
2043 positive = kUniversalFilter;
2044 }
2045 }
2046
2047 // A filter is a colon-separated list of patterns. It matches a
2048 // test if any pattern in it matches the test.
2049 return (MatchesFilter(full_name, positive.c_str()) &&
2050 !MatchesFilter(full_name, negative.c_str()));
2051}

2053#if GTEST_HAS_SEH
2054// Returns EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER if Google Test should handle the
2055// given SEH exception, or EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH otherwise.
2056// This function is useful as an __except condition.
2057int UnitTestOptions::GTestShouldProcessSEH(DWORD exception_code) {
2058 // Google Test should handle a SEH exception if:
2059 // 1. the user wants it to, AND
2060 // 2. this is not a breakpoint exception, AND
2061 // 3. this is not a C++ exception (VC++ implements them via SEH,
2062 // apparently).
2063 //
2064 // SEH exception code for C++ exceptions.
2065 // (see http://support.microsoft.com/kb/185294 for more information).
2066 const DWORD kCxxExceptionCode = 0xe06d7363;
2067
2068 bool should_handle = true;
2069
2070 if (!GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions))
2071 should_handle = false;
2072 else if (exception_code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT)
2073 should_handle = false;
2074 else if (exception_code == kCxxExceptionCode)
2075 should_handle = false;
2076
2077 return should_handle ? EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER : EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
2078}
2079#endif // GTEST_HAS_SEH

2151// This predicate-formatter checks that 'results' contains a test part
2152// failure of the given type and that the failure message contains the
2153// given substring.
2154static AssertionResult HasOneFailure(const char* /* results_expr */,
2155 const char* /* type_expr */,
2156 const char* /* substr_expr */,
2157 const TestPartResultArray& results,
2158 TestPartResult::Type type,
2159 const std::string& substr) {
2160 const std::string expected(type == TestPartResult::kFatalFailure ?
2161 "1 fatal failure" :
2162 "1 non-fatal failure");
2163 Message msg;
2164 if (results.size() != 1) {
2165 msg << "Expected: " << expected << "\n"
2166 << " Actual: " << results.size() << " failures";
2167 for (int i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
2168 msg << "\n" << results.GetTestPartResult(i);
2169 }
2170 return AssertionFailure() << msg;
2171 }
2172
2173 const TestPartResult& r = results.GetTestPartResult(0);
2174 if (r.type() != type) {
2175 return AssertionFailure() << "Expected: " << expected << "\n"
2176 << " Actual:\n"
2177 << r;
2178 }
2179
2180 if (strstr(r.message(), substr.c_str()) == NULL) {
2181 return AssertionFailure() << "Expected: " << expected << " containing \""
2182 << substr << "\"\n"
2183 << " Actual:\n"
2184 << r;
2185 }
2186
2187 return AssertionSuccess();
2188}

2310// specifies the number of top frames to be skipped, which doesn't
2311// count against the number of frames to be included.
2312//
2313// For example, if Foo() calls Bar(), which in turn calls
2314// CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(1), Foo() will be included in the
2315// trace but Bar() and CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop() won't.
2316std::string UnitTestImpl::CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(int skip_count) {
2317 return os_stack_trace_getter()->CurrentStackTrace(
2318 static_cast<int>(GTEST_FLAG(stack_trace_depth)),

2321 // itself.
2322 ); // NOLINT

2325// Returns the current time in milliseconds.
2326TimeInMillis GetTimeInMillis() {
2327#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || defined(__BORLANDC__)
2328 // Difference between 1970-01-01 and 1601-01-01 in milliseconds.
2329 // http://analogous.blogspot.com/2005/04/epoch.html
2330 const TimeInMillis kJavaEpochToWinFileTimeDelta =
2331 static_cast<TimeInMillis>(116444736UL) * 100000UL;
2332 const DWORD kTenthMicrosInMilliSecond = 10000;
2333
2334 SYSTEMTIME now_systime;
2335 FILETIME now_filetime;
2336 ULARGE_INTEGER now_int64;
2337 // FIXME: Shouldn't this just use
2338 // GetSystemTimeAsFileTime()?
2339 GetSystemTime(&now_systime);
2340 if (SystemTimeToFileTime(&now_systime, &now_filetime)) {
2341 now_int64.LowPart = now_filetime.dwLowDateTime;
2342 now_int64.HighPart = now_filetime.dwHighDateTime;
2343 now_int64.QuadPart = (now_int64.QuadPart / kTenthMicrosInMilliSecond) -
2344 kJavaEpochToWinFileTimeDelta;
2345 return now_int64.QuadPart;
2346 }
2347 return 0;
2348#elif GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_HAS_GETTIMEOFDAY_
2349 __timeb64 now;
2350
2351 // MSVC 8 deprecates _ftime64(), so we want to suppress warning 4996
2352 // (deprecated function) there.
2353 // FIXME: Use GetTickCount()? Or use
2354 // SystemTimeToFileTime()
2355 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_DEPRECATED_PUSH_()
2356 _ftime64(&now);
2357 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_DEPRECATED_POP_()
2358
2359 return static_cast<TimeInMillis>(now.time) * 1000 + now.millitm;
2360#elif GTEST_HAS_GETTIMEOFDAY_
2361 struct timeval now;
2362 gettimeofday(&now, NULL);
2363 return static_cast<TimeInMillis>(now.tv_sec) * 1000 + now.tv_usec / 1000;
2364#else
2365# error "Don't know how to get the current time on your system."
2366#endif
2367}

2371// class String.

2373#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
2374// Creates a UTF-16 wide string from the given ANSI string, allocating
2375// memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
2376// value using delete[]. Returns the wide string, or NULL if the
2377// input is NULL.
2378LPCWSTR String::AnsiToUtf16(const char* ansi) {
2379 if (!ansi) return NULL;
2380 const int length = strlen(ansi);
2381 const int unicode_length =
2382 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, ansi, length,
2383 NULL, 0);
2384 WCHAR* unicode = new WCHAR[unicode_length + 1];
2385 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, ansi, length,
2386 unicode, unicode_length);
2387 unicode[unicode_length] = 0;
2388 return unicode;
2389}
2390
2391// Creates an ANSI string from the given wide string, allocating
2392// memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
2393// value using delete[]. Returns the ANSI string, or NULL if the
2394// input is NULL.
2395const char* String::Utf16ToAnsi(LPCWSTR utf16_str) {
2396 if (!utf16_str) return NULL;
2397 const int ansi_length =
2398 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, utf16_str, -1,
2399 NULL, 0, NULL, NULL);
2400 char* ansi = new char[ansi_length + 1];
2401 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, utf16_str, -1,
2402 ansi, ansi_length, NULL, NULL);
2403 ansi[ansi_length] = 0;
2404 return ansi;
2405}
2406
2407#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
2408
2409// Compares two C strings. Returns true iff they have the same content.
2410//
2411// Unlike strcmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A NULL
2412// C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
2413// including the empty string.
2414bool String::CStringEquals(const char * lhs, const char * rhs) {
2415 if ( lhs == NULL ) return rhs == NULL;
2416
2417 if ( rhs == NULL ) return false;
2418
2419 return strcmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
2420}

2423
2424// Converts an array of wide chars to a narrow string using the UTF-8
2425// encoding, and streams the result to the given Message object.
2426static void StreamWideCharsToMessage(const wchar_t* wstr, size_t length,
2427 Message* msg) {
2428 for (size_t i = 0; i != length; ) { // NOLINT
2429 if (wstr[i] != L'\0') {
2430 *msg << WideStringToUtf8(wstr + i, static_cast<int>(length - i));
2431 while (i != length && wstr[i] != L'\0')
2432 i++;
2433 } else {
2434 *msg << '\0';
2435 i++;
2436 }
2437 }
2438}
2439
2440#endif // GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING || GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_WSTRING
2441
2442void SplitString(const ::std::string& str, char delimiter,
2443 ::std::vector< ::std::string>* dest) {
2444 ::std::vector< ::std::string> parsed;
2445 ::std::string::size_type pos = 0;
2446 while (::testing::internal::AlwaysTrue()) {
2447 const ::std::string::size_type colon = str.find(delimiter, pos);
2448 if (colon == ::std::string::npos) {
2449 parsed.push_back(str.substr(pos));
2450 break;
2451 } else {
2452 parsed.push_back(str.substr(pos, colon - pos));
2453 pos = colon + 1;
2454 }
2455 }
2456 dest->swap(parsed);
2457}

2461// Constructs an empty Message.
2462// We allocate the stringstream separately because otherwise each use of
2463// ASSERT/EXPECT in a procedure adds over 200 bytes to the procedure's
2464// stack frame leading to huge stack frames in some cases; gcc does not reuse
2465// the stack space.
2466Message::Message() : ss_(new ::std::stringstream) {
2467 // By default, we want there to be enough precision when printing
2468 // a double to a Message.
2469 *ss_ << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<double>::digits10 + 2);

2520
2521// Returns the assertion's negation. Used with EXPECT/ASSERT_FALSE.
2522AssertionResult AssertionResult::operator!() const {
2523 AssertionResult negation(!success_);
2524 if (message_.get() != NULL)
2525 negation << *message_;
2526 return negation;
2527}
2528
2529// Makes a successful assertion result.
2530AssertionResult AssertionSuccess() {
2531 return AssertionResult(true);
2532}
2533
2534// Makes a failed assertion result.
2535AssertionResult AssertionFailure() {
2536 return AssertionResult(false);
2537}
2538
2539// Makes a failed assertion result with the given failure message.
2540// Deprecated; use AssertionFailure() << message.
2541AssertionResult AssertionFailure(const Message& message) {
2542 return AssertionFailure() << message;
2543}

2547namespace edit_distance {
2548std::vector<EditType> CalculateOptimalEdits(const std::vector<size_t>& left,
2549 const std::vector<size_t>& right) {
2550 std::vector<std::vector<double> > costs(
2551 left.size() + 1, std::vector<double>(right.size() + 1));
2552 std::vector<std::vector<EditType> > best_move(
2553 left.size() + 1, std::vector<EditType>(right.size() + 1));
2554
2555 // Populate for empty right.
2556 for (size_t l_i = 0; l_i < costs.size(); ++l_i) {
2557 costs[l_i][0] = static_cast<double>(l_i);
2558 best_move[l_i][0] = kRemove;
2559 }
2560 // Populate for empty left.
2561 for (size_t r_i = 1; r_i < costs[0].size(); ++r_i) {
2562 costs[0][r_i] = static_cast<double>(r_i);
2563 best_move[0][r_i] = kAdd;
2564 }
2565
2566 for (size_t l_i = 0; l_i < left.size(); ++l_i) {
2567 for (size_t r_i = 0; r_i < right.size(); ++r_i) {
2568 if (left[l_i] == right[r_i]) {
2569 // Found a match. Consume it.
2570 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = costs[l_i][r_i];
2571 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kMatch;
2572 continue;
2573 }
2574
2575 const double add = costs[l_i + 1][r_i];
2576 const double remove = costs[l_i][r_i + 1];
2577 const double replace = costs[l_i][r_i];
2578 if (add < remove && add < replace) {
2579 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = add + 1;
2580 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kAdd;
2581 } else if (remove < add && remove < replace) {
2582 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = remove + 1;
2583 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kRemove;
2584 } else {
2585 // We make replace a little more expensive than add/remove to lower
2586 // their priority.
2587 costs[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = replace + 1.00001;
2588 best_move[l_i + 1][r_i + 1] = kReplace;
2589 }
2590 }
2591 }
2592
2593 // Reconstruct the best path. We do it in reverse order.
2594 std::vector<EditType> best_path;
2595 for (size_t l_i = left.size(), r_i = right.size(); l_i > 0 || r_i > 0;) {
2596 EditType move = best_move[l_i][r_i];
2597 best_path.push_back(move);
2598 l_i -= move != kAdd;
2599 r_i -= move != kRemove;
2600 }
2601 std::reverse(best_path.begin(), best_path.end());
2602 return best_path;
2603}

2607// Helper class to convert string into ids with deduplication.
2608class InternalStrings {
2609 public:
2610 size_t GetId(const std::string& str) {
2611 IdMap::iterator it = ids_.find(str);
2612 if (it != ids_.end()) return it->second;
2613 size_t id = ids_.size();
2614 return ids_[str] = id;
2615 }
2616
2617 private:
2618 typedef std::map<std::string, size_t> IdMap;
2619 IdMap ids_;
2620};
2621
2622} // namespace
2623
2624std::vector<EditType> CalculateOptimalEdits(
2625 const std::vector<std::string>& left,
2626 const std::vector<std::string>& right) {
2627 std::vector<size_t> left_ids, right_ids;
2628 {
2629 InternalStrings intern_table;
2630 for (size_t i = 0; i < left.size(); ++i) {
2631 left_ids.push_back(intern_table.GetId(left[i]));
2632 }
2633 for (size_t i = 0; i < right.size(); ++i) {
2634 right_ids.push_back(intern_table.GetId(right[i]));
2635 }
2636 }
2637 return CalculateOptimalEdits(left_ids, right_ids);
2638}

2640namespace {
2641
2642// Helper class that holds the state for one hunk and prints it out to the
2643// stream.
2644// It reorders adds/removes when possible to group all removes before all
2645// adds. It also adds the hunk header before printint into the stream.
2646class Hunk {
2647 public:
2648 Hunk(size_t left_start, size_t right_start)
2649 : left_start_(left_start),
2650 right_start_(right_start),
2651 adds_(),
2652 removes_(),
2653 common_() {}
2654
2655 void PushLine(char edit, const char* line) {
2656 switch (edit) {
2657 case ' ':
2658 ++common_;
2659 FlushEdits();
2660 hunk_.push_back(std::make_pair(' ', line));
2661 break;
2662 case '-':
2663 ++removes_;
2664 hunk_removes_.push_back(std::make_pair('-', line));
2665 break;
2666 case '+':
2667 ++adds_;
2668 hunk_adds_.push_back(std::make_pair('+', line));
2669 break;
2670 }
2671 }
2672
2673 void PrintTo(std::ostream* os) {
2674 PrintHeader(os);
2675 FlushEdits();
2676 for (std::list<std::pair<char, const char*> >::const_iterator it =
2677 hunk_.begin();
2678 it != hunk_.end(); ++it) {
2679 *os << it->first << it->second << "\n";
2680 }
2681 }
2682
2683 bool has_edits() const { return adds_ || removes_; }
2684
2685 private:
2686 void FlushEdits() {
2687 hunk_.splice(hunk_.end(), hunk_removes_);
2688 hunk_.splice(hunk_.end(), hunk_adds_);
2689 }
2690
2691 // Print a unified diff header for one hunk.
2692 // The format is
2693 // "@@ -<left_start>,<left_length> +<right_start>,<right_length> @@"
2694 // where the left/right parts are omitted if unnecessary.
2695 void PrintHeader(std::ostream* ss) const {
2696 *ss << "@@ ";
2697 if (removes_) {
2698 *ss << "-" << left_start_ << "," << (removes_ + common_);
2699 }
2700 if (removes_ && adds_) {
2701 *ss << " ";
2702 }
2703 if (adds_) {
2704 *ss << "+" << right_start_ << "," << (adds_ + common_);
2705 }
2706 *ss << " @@\n";
2707 }
2708
2709 size_t left_start_, right_start_;
2710 size_t adds_, removes_, common_;
2711 std::list<std::pair<char, const char*> > hunk_, hunk_adds_, hunk_removes_;
2712};
2713
2714} // namespace
2715
2716// Create a list of diff hunks in Unified diff format.
2717// Each hunk has a header generated by PrintHeader above plus a body with
2718// lines prefixed with ' ' for no change, '-' for deletion and '+' for
2719// addition.
2720// 'context' represents the desired unchanged prefix/suffix around the diff.
2721// If two hunks are close enough that their contexts overlap, then they are
2722// joined into one hunk.
2723std::string CreateUnifiedDiff(const std::vector<std::string>& left,
2724 const std::vector<std::string>& right,
2725 size_t context) {
2726 const std::vector<EditType> edits = CalculateOptimalEdits(left, right);
2727
2728 size_t l_i = 0, r_i = 0, edit_i = 0;
2729 std::stringstream ss;
2730 while (edit_i < edits.size()) {
2731 // Find first edit.
2732 while (edit_i < edits.size() && edits[edit_i] == kMatch) {
2733 ++l_i;
2734 ++r_i;
2735 ++edit_i;
2736 }
2737
2738 // Find the first line to include in the hunk.
2739 const size_t prefix_context = std::min(l_i, context);
2740 Hunk hunk(l_i - prefix_context + 1, r_i - prefix_context + 1);
2741 for (size_t i = prefix_context; i > 0; --i) {
2742 hunk.PushLine(' ', left[l_i - i].c_str());
2743 }
2744
2745 // Iterate the edits until we found enough suffix for the hunk or the input
2746 // is over.
2747 size_t n_suffix = 0;
2748 for (; edit_i < edits.size(); ++edit_i) {
2749 if (n_suffix >= context) {
2750 // Continue only if the next hunk is very close.
2751 std::vector<EditType>::const_iterator it = edits.begin() + edit_i;
2752 while (it != edits.end() && *it == kMatch) ++it;
2753 if (it == edits.end() || (it - edits.begin()) - edit_i >= context) {
2754 // There is no next edit or it is too far away.
2755 break;
2756 }
2757 }
2758
2759 EditType edit = edits[edit_i];
2760 // Reset count when a non match is found.
2761 n_suffix = edit == kMatch ? n_suffix + 1 : 0;
2762
2763 if (edit == kMatch || edit == kRemove || edit == kReplace) {
2764 hunk.PushLine(edit == kMatch ? ' ' : '-', left[l_i].c_str());
2765 }
2766 if (edit == kAdd || edit == kReplace) {
2767 hunk.PushLine('+', right[r_i].c_str());
2768 }
2769
2770 // Advance indices, depending on edit type.
2771 l_i += edit != kAdd;
2772 r_i += edit != kRemove;
2773 }
2774
2775 if (!hunk.has_edits()) {
2776 // We are done. We don't want this hunk.
2777 break;
2778 }
2779
2780 hunk.PrintTo(&ss);
2781 }
2782 return ss.str();
2783}

2789// The string representation of the values received in EqFailure() are already
2790// escaped. Split them on escaped '\n' boundaries. Leave all other escaped
2791// characters the same.
2792std::vector<std::string> SplitEscapedString(const std::string& str) {
2793 std::vector<std::string> lines;
2794 size_t start = 0, end = str.size();
2795 if (end > 2 && str[0] == '"' && str[end - 1] == '"') {
2796 ++start;
2797 --end;
2798 }
2799 bool escaped = false;
2800 for (size_t i = start; i + 1 < end; ++i) {
2801 if (escaped) {
2802 escaped = false;
2803 if (str[i] == 'n') {
2804 lines.push_back(str.substr(start, i - start - 1));
2805 start = i + 1;
2806 }
2807 } else {
2808 escaped = str[i] == '\\';
2809 }
2810 }
2811 lines.push_back(str.substr(start, end - start));
2812 return lines;
2813}

2816
2817// Constructs and returns the message for an equality assertion
2818// (e.g. ASSERT_EQ, EXPECT_STREQ, etc) failure.
2819//
2820// The first four parameters are the expressions used in the assertion
2821// and their values, as strings. For example, for ASSERT_EQ(foo, bar)
2822// where foo is 5 and bar is 6, we have:
2823//
2824// lhs_expression: "foo"
2825// rhs_expression: "bar"
2826// lhs_value: "5"
2827// rhs_value: "6"
2828//
2829// The ignoring_case parameter is true iff the assertion is a
2830// *_STRCASEEQ*. When it's true, the string "Ignoring case" will
2831// be inserted into the message.
2832AssertionResult EqFailure(const char* lhs_expression,
2833 const char* rhs_expression,
2834 const std::string& lhs_value,
2835 const std::string& rhs_value,
2836 bool ignoring_case) {
2837 Message msg;
2838 msg << "Expected equality of these values:";
2839 msg << "\n " << lhs_expression;
2840 if (lhs_value != lhs_expression) {
2841 msg << "\n Which is: " << lhs_value;
2842 }
2843 msg << "\n " << rhs_expression;
2844 if (rhs_value != rhs_expression) {
2845 msg << "\n Which is: " << rhs_value;
2846 }
2847
2848 if (ignoring_case) {
2849 msg << "\nIgnoring case";
2850 }
2851
2852 if (!lhs_value.empty() && !rhs_value.empty()) {
2853 const std::vector<std::string> lhs_lines =
2854 SplitEscapedString(lhs_value);
2855 const std::vector<std::string> rhs_lines =
2856 SplitEscapedString(rhs_value);
2857 if (lhs_lines.size() > 1 || rhs_lines.size() > 1) {
2858 msg << "\nWith diff:\n"
2859 << edit_distance::CreateUnifiedDiff(lhs_lines, rhs_lines);
2860 }
2861 }
2862
2863 return AssertionFailure() << msg;
2864}
2865
2866// Constructs a failure message for Boolean assertions such as EXPECT_TRUE.
2867std::string GetBoolAssertionFailureMessage(
2868 const AssertionResult& assertion_result,
2869 const char* expression_text,
2870 const char* actual_predicate_value,
2871 const char* expected_predicate_value) {
2872 const char* actual_message = assertion_result.message();
2873 Message msg;
2874 msg << "Value of: " << expression_text
2875 << "\n Actual: " << actual_predicate_value;
2876 if (actual_message[0] != '\0')
2877 msg << " (" << actual_message << ")";
2878 msg << "\nExpected: " << expected_predicate_value;
2879 return msg.GetString();
2880}

2882// Helper function for implementing ASSERT_NEAR.
2883AssertionResult DoubleNearPredFormat(const char* expr1,
2884 const char* expr2,
2885 const char* abs_error_expr,
2886 double val1,
2887 double val2,
2888 double abs_error) {
2889 const double diff = fabs(val1 - val2);
2890 if (diff <= abs_error) return AssertionSuccess();
2891
2892 // FIXME: do not print the value of an expression if it's
2893 // already a literal.
2894 return AssertionFailure()
2895 << "The difference between " << expr1 << " and " << expr2
2896 << " is " << diff << ", which exceeds " << abs_error_expr << ", where\n"
2897 << expr1 << " evaluates to " << val1 << ",\n"
2898 << expr2 << " evaluates to " << val2 << ", and\n"
2899 << abs_error_expr << " evaluates to " << abs_error << ".";
2900}

2903// Helper template for implementing FloatLE() and DoubleLE().
2904template <typename RawType>
2905AssertionResult FloatingPointLE(const char* expr1,
2906 const char* expr2,
2907 RawType val1,
2908 RawType val2) {
2909 // Returns success if val1 is less than val2,
2910 if (val1 < val2) {
2911 return AssertionSuccess();
2912 }
2913
2914 // or if val1 is almost equal to val2.
2915 const FloatingPoint<RawType> lhs(val1), rhs(val2);
2916 if (lhs.AlmostEquals(rhs)) {
2917 return AssertionSuccess();
2918 }
2919
2920 // Note that the above two checks will both fail if either val1 or
2921 // val2 is NaN, as the IEEE floating-point standard requires that
2922 // any predicate involving a NaN must return false.
2923
2924 ::std::stringstream val1_ss;
2925 val1_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
2926 << val1;
2927
2928 ::std::stringstream val2_ss;
2929 val2_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
2930 << val2;
2931
2932 return AssertionFailure()
2933 << "Expected: (" << expr1 << ") <= (" << expr2 << ")\n"
2934 << " Actual: " << StringStreamToString(&val1_ss) << " vs "
2935 << StringStreamToString(&val2_ss);
2936}

2940// Asserts that val1 is less than, or almost equal to, val2. Fails
2941// otherwise. In particular, it fails if either val1 or val2 is NaN.
2942AssertionResult FloatLE(const char* expr1, const char* expr2,
2943 float val1, float val2) {
2944 return internal::FloatingPointLE<float>(expr1, expr2, val1, val2);
2945}
2946
2947// Asserts that val1 is less than, or almost equal to, val2. Fails
2948// otherwise. In particular, it fails if either val1 or val2 is NaN.
2949AssertionResult DoubleLE(const char* expr1, const char* expr2,
2950 double val1, double val2) {
2951 return internal::FloatingPointLE<double>(expr1, expr2, val1, val2);
2952}

3072// Helper functions for implementing IsSubString() and IsNotSubstring().
3073
3074// This group of overloaded functions return true iff needle is a
3075// substring of haystack. NULL is considered a substring of itself
3076// only.
3077
3078bool IsSubstringPred(const char* needle, const char* haystack) {
3079 if (needle == NULL || haystack == NULL)
3080 return needle == haystack;
3081
3082 return strstr(haystack, needle) != NULL;
3083}
3084
3085bool IsSubstringPred(const wchar_t* needle, const wchar_t* haystack) {
3086 if (needle == NULL || haystack == NULL)
3087 return needle == haystack;
3088
3089 return wcsstr(haystack, needle) != NULL;
3090}
3091
3092// StringType here can be either ::std::string or ::std::wstring.
3093template <typename StringType>
3094bool IsSubstringPred(const StringType& needle,
3095 const StringType& haystack) {
3096 return haystack.find(needle) != StringType::npos;
3097}
3098
3099// This function implements either IsSubstring() or IsNotSubstring(),
3100// depending on the value of the expected_to_be_substring parameter.
3101// StringType here can be const char*, const wchar_t*, ::std::string,
3102// or ::std::wstring.
3103template <typename StringType>
3104AssertionResult IsSubstringImpl(
3105 bool expected_to_be_substring,
3106 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3107 const StringType& needle, const StringType& haystack) {
3108 if (IsSubstringPred(needle, haystack) == expected_to_be_substring)
3109 return AssertionSuccess();
3110
3111 const bool is_wide_string = sizeof(needle[0]) > 1;
3112 const char* const begin_string_quote = is_wide_string ? "L\"" : "\"";
3113 return AssertionFailure()
3114 << "Value of: " << needle_expr << "\n"
3115 << " Actual: " << begin_string_quote << needle << "\"\n"
3116 << "Expected: " << (expected_to_be_substring ? "" : "not ")
3117 << "a substring of " << haystack_expr << "\n"
3118 << "Which is: " << begin_string_quote << haystack << "\"";
3119}

3121} // namespace
3122
3123// IsSubstring() and IsNotSubstring() check whether needle is a
3124// substring of haystack (NULL is considered a substring of itself
3125// only), and return an appropriate error message when they fail.
3126
3127AssertionResult IsSubstring(
3128 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3129 const char* needle, const char* haystack) {
3130 return IsSubstringImpl(true, needle_expr, haystack_expr, needle, haystack);
3131}
3132
3133AssertionResult IsSubstring(
3134 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3135 const wchar_t* needle, const wchar_t* haystack) {
3136 return IsSubstringImpl(true, needle_expr, haystack_expr, needle, haystack);
3137}
3138
3139AssertionResult IsNotSubstring(
3140 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3141 const char* needle, const char* haystack) {
3142 return IsSubstringImpl(false, needle_expr, haystack_expr, needle, haystack);
3143}
3144
3145AssertionResult IsNotSubstring(
3146 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3147 const wchar_t* needle, const wchar_t* haystack) {
3148 return IsSubstringImpl(false, needle_expr, haystack_expr, needle, haystack);
3149}
3150
3151AssertionResult IsSubstring(
3152 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,
3153 const ::std::string& needle, const ::std::string& haystack) {
3154 return IsSubstringImpl(true, needle_expr, haystack_expr, needle, haystack);
3155}
3156
3157AssertionResult IsNotSubstring(
3158 const char* needle_expr, const char* haystack_expr,

3183// Helper function for IsHRESULT{SuccessFailure} predicates
3184AssertionResult HRESULTFailureHelper(const char* expr,
3185 const char* expected,
3186 long hr) { // NOLINT
3187# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_TV_TITLE
3188
3189 // Windows CE doesn't support FormatMessage.
3190 const char error_text[] = "";
3191
3192# else
3193
3194 // Looks up the human-readable system message for the HRESULT code
3195 // and since we're not passing any params to FormatMessage, we don't
3196 // want inserts expanded.
3197 const DWORD kFlags = FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM |
3198 FORMAT_MESSAGE_IGNORE_INSERTS;
3199 const DWORD kBufSize = 4096;
3200 // Gets the system's human readable message string for this HRESULT.
3201 char error_text[kBufSize] = { '\0' };
3202 DWORD message_length = ::FormatMessageA(kFlags,
3203 0, // no source, we're asking system
3204 hr, // the error
3205 0, // no line width restrictions
3206 error_text, // output buffer
3207 kBufSize, // buf size
3208 NULL); // no arguments for inserts
3209 // Trims tailing white space (FormatMessage leaves a trailing CR-LF)
3210 for (; message_length && IsSpace(error_text[message_length - 1]);
3211 --message_length) {
3212 error_text[message_length - 1] = '\0';
3213 }
3214
3215# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
3216
3217 const std::string error_hex("0x" + String::FormatHexInt(hr));
3218 return ::testing::AssertionFailure()
3219 << "Expected: " << expr << " " << expected << ".\n"
3220 << " Actual: " << error_hex << " " << error_text << "\n";
3221}
3222
3223} // namespace
3224
3225AssertionResult IsHRESULTSuccess(const char* expr, long hr) { // NOLINT
3226 if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
3227 return AssertionSuccess();
3228 }
3229 return HRESULTFailureHelper(expr, "succeeds", hr);
3230}
3231
3232AssertionResult IsHRESULTFailure(const char* expr, long hr) { // NOLINT
3233 if (FAILED(hr)) {
3234 return AssertionSuccess();
3235 }
3236 return HRESULTFailureHelper(expr, "fails", hr);
3237}

3241// Utility functions for encoding Unicode text (wide strings) in
3242// UTF-8.
3243
3244// A Unicode code-point can have up to 21 bits, and is encoded in UTF-8
3245// like this:
3246//
3247// Code-point length Encoding
3248// 0 - 7 bits 0xxxxxxx
3249// 8 - 11 bits 110xxxxx 10xxxxxx
3250// 12 - 16 bits 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
3251// 17 - 21 bits 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
3252
3253// The maximum code-point a one-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
3254const UInt32 kMaxCodePoint1 = (static_cast<UInt32>(1) << 7) - 1;
3255
3256// The maximum code-point a two-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
3257const UInt32 kMaxCodePoint2 = (static_cast<UInt32>(1) << (5 + 6)) - 1;
3258
3259// The maximum code-point a three-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
3260const UInt32 kMaxCodePoint3 = (static_cast<UInt32>(1) << (4 + 2*6)) - 1;
3261
3262// The maximum code-point a four-byte UTF-8 sequence can represent.
3263const UInt32 kMaxCodePoint4 = (static_cast<UInt32>(1) << (3 + 3*6)) - 1;
3264
3265// Chops off the n lowest bits from a bit pattern. Returns the n
3266// lowest bits. As a side effect, the original bit pattern will be
3267// shifted to the right by n bits.
3268inline UInt32 ChopLowBits(UInt32* bits, int n) {
3269 const UInt32 low_bits = *bits & ((static_cast<UInt32>(1) << n) - 1);
3270 *bits >>= n;
3271 return low_bits;
3272}
3273
3274// Converts a Unicode code point to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.
3275// code_point parameter is of type UInt32 because wchar_t may not be
3276// wide enough to contain a code point.
3277// If the code_point is not a valid Unicode code point
3278// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) it will be converted
3279// to "(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)".
3280std::string CodePointToUtf8(UInt32 code_point) {
3281 if (code_point > kMaxCodePoint4) {
3282 return "(Invalid Unicode 0x" + String::FormatHexInt(code_point) + ")";
3283 }
3284
3285 char str[5]; // Big enough for the largest valid code point.
3286 if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint1) {
3287 str[1] = '\0';
3288 str[0] = static_cast<char>(code_point); // 0xxxxxxx
3289 } else if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint2) {
3290 str[2] = '\0';
3291 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3292 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xC0 | code_point); // 110xxxxx
3293 } else if (code_point <= kMaxCodePoint3) {
3294 str[3] = '\0';
3295 str[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3296 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3297 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xE0 | code_point); // 1110xxxx
3298 } else { // code_point <= kMaxCodePoint4
3299 str[4] = '\0';
3300 str[3] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3301 str[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3302 str[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ChopLowBits(&code_point, 6)); // 10xxxxxx
3303 str[0] = static_cast<char>(0xF0 | code_point); // 11110xxx
3304 }
3305 return str;
3306}
3307
3308// The following two functions only make sense if the system
3309// uses UTF-16 for wide string encoding. All supported systems
3310// with 16 bit wchar_t (Windows, Cygwin, Symbian OS) do use UTF-16.
3311
3312// Determines if the arguments constitute UTF-16 surrogate pair
3313// and thus should be combined into a single Unicode code point
3314// using CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair.
3315inline bool IsUtf16SurrogatePair(wchar_t first, wchar_t second) {
3316 return sizeof(wchar_t) == 2 &&
3317 (first & 0xFC00) == 0xD800 && (second & 0xFC00) == 0xDC00;
3318}
3319
3320// Creates a Unicode code point from UTF16 surrogate pair.
3321inline UInt32 CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair(wchar_t first,
3322 wchar_t second) {
3323 const UInt32 mask = (1 << 10) - 1;
3324 return (sizeof(wchar_t) == 2) ?
3325 (((first & mask) << 10) | (second & mask)) + 0x10000 :
3326 // This function should not be called when the condition is
3327 // false, but we provide a sensible default in case it is.
3328 static_cast<UInt32>(first);
3329}
3330
3331// Converts a wide string to a narrow string in UTF-8 encoding.
3332// The wide string is assumed to have the following encoding:
3333// UTF-16 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 2 (on Windows, Cygwin, Symbian OS)
3334// UTF-32 if sizeof(wchar_t) == 4 (on Linux)
3335// Parameter str points to a null-terminated wide string.
3336// Parameter num_chars may additionally limit the number
3337// of wchar_t characters processed. -1 is used when the entire string
3338// should be processed.
3339// If the string contains code points that are not valid Unicode code points
3340// (i.e. outside of Unicode range U+0 to U+10FFFF) they will be output
3341// as '(Invalid Unicode 0xXXXXXXXX)'. If the string is in UTF16 encoding
3342// and contains invalid UTF-16 surrogate pairs, values in those pairs
3343// will be encoded as individual Unicode characters from Basic Normal Plane.
3344std::string WideStringToUtf8(const wchar_t* str, int num_chars) {
3345 if (num_chars == -1)
3346 num_chars = static_cast<int>(wcslen(str));
3347
3348 ::std::stringstream stream;
3349 for (int i = 0; i < num_chars; ++i) {
3350 UInt32 unicode_code_point;
3351
3352 if (str[i] == L'\0') {
3353 break;
3354 } else if (i + 1 < num_chars && IsUtf16SurrogatePair(str[i], str[i + 1])) {
3355 unicode_code_point = CreateCodePointFromUtf16SurrogatePair(str[i],
3356 str[i + 1]);
3357 i++;
3358 } else {
3359 unicode_code_point = static_cast<UInt32>(str[i]);
3360 }
3361
3362 stream << CodePointToUtf8(unicode_code_point);
3363 }
3364 return StringStreamToString(&stream);
3365}
3366
3367// Converts a wide C string to an std::string using the UTF-8 encoding.
3368// NULL will be converted to "(null)".
3369std::string String::ShowWideCString(const wchar_t * wide_c_str) {
3370 if (wide_c_str == NULL) return "(null)";
3371
3372 return internal::WideStringToUtf8(wide_c_str, -1);
3373}

3375// Compares two wide C strings. Returns true iff they have the same
3376// content.
3377//
3378// Unlike wcscmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A NULL
3379// C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
3380// including the empty string.
3381bool String::WideCStringEquals(const wchar_t * lhs, const wchar_t * rhs) {
3382 if (lhs == NULL) return rhs == NULL;
3383
3384 if (rhs == NULL) return false;
3385
3386 return wcscmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
3387}

3389// Helper function for *_STREQ on wide strings.
3390AssertionResult CmpHelperSTREQ(const char* lhs_expression,
3391 const char* rhs_expression,
3392 const wchar_t* lhs,
3393 const wchar_t* rhs) {
3394 if (String::WideCStringEquals(lhs, rhs)) {
3395 return AssertionSuccess();
3396 }
3397
3398 return EqFailure(lhs_expression,
3399 rhs_expression,
3400 PrintToString(lhs),
3401 PrintToString(rhs),
3402 false);
3403}

3405// Helper function for *_STRNE on wide strings.
3406AssertionResult CmpHelperSTRNE(const char* s1_expression,
3407 const char* s2_expression,
3408 const wchar_t* s1,
3409 const wchar_t* s2) {
3410 if (!String::WideCStringEquals(s1, s2)) {
3411 return AssertionSuccess();
3412 }
3413
3414 return AssertionFailure() << "Expected: (" << s1_expression << ") != ("
3415 << s2_expression << "), actual: "
3416 << PrintToString(s1)
3417 << " vs " << PrintToString(s2);
3418}

3420// Compares two C strings, ignoring case. Returns true iff they have
3421// the same content.
3422//
3423// Unlike strcasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A
3424// NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
3425// including the empty string.
3426bool String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(const char * lhs, const char * rhs) {
3427 if (lhs == NULL)
3428 return rhs == NULL;
3429 if (rhs == NULL)
3430 return false;
3431 return posix::StrCaseCmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
3432}
3433
3434 // Compares two wide C strings, ignoring case. Returns true iff they
3435 // have the same content.
3436 //
3437 // Unlike wcscasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s).
3438 // A NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL wide C string,
3439 // including the empty string.
3440 // NB: The implementations on different platforms slightly differ.
3441 // On windows, this method uses _wcsicmp which compares according to LC_CTYPE
3442 // environment variable. On GNU platform this method uses wcscasecmp
3443 // which compares according to LC_CTYPE category of the current locale.
3444 // On MacOS X, it uses towlower, which also uses LC_CTYPE category of the
3445 // current locale.
3446bool String::CaseInsensitiveWideCStringEquals(const wchar_t* lhs,
3447 const wchar_t* rhs) {
3448 if (lhs == NULL) return rhs == NULL;
3449
3450 if (rhs == NULL) return false;
3451
3452#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
3453 return _wcsicmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
3454#elif GTEST_OS_LINUX && !GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID
3455 return wcscasecmp(lhs, rhs) == 0;
3456#else
3457 // Android, Mac OS X and Cygwin don't define wcscasecmp.
3458 // Other unknown OSes may not define it either.
3459 wint_t left, right;
3460 do {
3461 left = towlower(*lhs++);
3462 right = towlower(*rhs++);
3463 } while (left && left == right);
3464 return left == right;
3465#endif // OS selector
3466}
3467
3468// Returns true iff str ends with the given suffix, ignoring case.
3469// Any string is considered to end with an empty suffix.
3470bool String::EndsWithCaseInsensitive(
3471 const std::string& str, const std::string& suffix) {
3472 const size_t str_len = str.length();
3473 const size_t suffix_len = suffix.length();
3474 return (str_len >= suffix_len) &&
3475 CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(str.c_str() + str_len - suffix_len,
3476 suffix.c_str());
3477}

3480std::string String::FormatIntWidth2(int value) {
3481 std::stringstream ss;

3486// Formats an int value as "%X".
3487std::string String::FormatHexInt(int value) {

3493// Formats a byte as "%02X".
3494std::string String::FormatByte(unsigned char value) {
3495 std::stringstream ss;
3496 ss << std::setfill('0') << std::setw(2) << std::hex << std::uppercase
3497 << static_cast<unsigned int>(value);
3498 return ss.str();
3499}

3501// Converts the buffer in a stringstream to an std::string, converting NUL
3502// bytes to "\\0" along the way.
3503std::string StringStreamToString(::std::stringstream* ss) {
3504 const ::std::string& str = ss->str();
3505 const char* const start = str.c_str();
3506 const char* const end = start + str.length();
3507
3508 std::string result;
3509 result.reserve(2 * (end - start));
3510 for (const char* ch = start; ch != end; ++ch) {
3511 if (*ch == '\0') {
3512 result += "\\0"; // Replaces NUL with "\\0";
3513 } else {
3514 result += *ch;
3515 }
3516 }
3517
3518 return result;
3519}

3521// Appends the user-supplied message to the Google-Test-generated message.
3522std::string AppendUserMessage(const std::string& gtest_msg,
3523 const Message& user_msg) {
3524 // Appends the user message if it's non-empty.
3525 const std::string user_msg_string = user_msg.GetString();
3526 if (user_msg_string.empty()) {
3527 return gtest_msg;
3528 }
3529
3530 return gtest_msg + "\n" + user_msg_string;
3531}

3575// Adds a test property to the list. If a property with the same key as the
3576// supplied property is already represented, the value of this test_property
3577// replaces the old value for that key.
3578void TestResult::RecordProperty(const std::string& xml_element,
3579 const TestProperty& test_property) {
3580 if (!ValidateTestProperty(xml_element, test_property)) {
3581 return;
3582 }
3583 internal::MutexLock lock(&test_properites_mutex_);
3584 const std::vector<TestProperty>::iterator property_with_matching_key =
3585 std::find_if(test_properties_.begin(), test_properties_.end(),
3586 internal::TestPropertyKeyIs(test_property.key()));
3587 if (property_with_matching_key == test_properties_.end()) {
3588 test_properties_.push_back(test_property);
3589 return;
3590 }
3591 property_with_matching_key->SetValue(test_property.value());
3592}

3594// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testsuites> element of XML
3595// output.
3596static const char* const kReservedTestSuitesAttributes[] = {
3597 "disabled",
3598 "errors",
3599 "failures",
3600 "name",
3601 "random_seed",
3602 "tests",
3603 "time",
3604 "timestamp"
3605};
3606
3607// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testsuite> element of XML
3608// output.
3609static const char* const kReservedTestSuiteAttributes[] = {
3610 "disabled",
3611 "errors",
3612 "failures",
3613 "name",
3614 "tests",
3615 "time"
3616};
3617
3618// The list of reserved attributes used in the <testcase> element of XML output.
3619static const char* const kReservedTestCaseAttributes[] = {
3620 "classname", "name", "status", "time",
3621 "type_param", "value_param", "file", "line"};
3622
3623template <int kSize>
3624std::vector<std::string> ArrayAsVector(const char* const (&array)[kSize]) {
3625 return std::vector<std::string>(array, array + kSize);
3626}
3627
3628static std::vector<std::string> GetReservedAttributesForElement(
3629 const std::string& xml_element) {
3630 if (xml_element == "testsuites") {
3631 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuitesAttributes);
3632 } else if (xml_element == "testsuite") {
3633 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestSuiteAttributes);
3634 } else if (xml_element == "testcase") {
3635 return ArrayAsVector(kReservedTestCaseAttributes);
3636 } else {
3637 GTEST_CHECK_(false) << "Unrecognized xml_element provided: " << xml_element;
3638 }
3639 // This code is unreachable but some compilers may not realizes that.
3640 return std::vector<std::string>();
3641}
3642
3643static std::string FormatWordList(const std::vector<std::string>& words) {
3644 Message word_list;
3645 for (size_t i = 0; i < words.size(); ++i) {
3646 if (i > 0 && words.size() > 2) {
3647 word_list << ", ";
3648 }
3649 if (i == words.size() - 1) {
3650 word_list << "and ";
3651 }
3652 word_list << "'" << words[i] << "'";
3653 }
3654 return word_list.GetString();
3655}
3656
3657static bool ValidateTestPropertyName(
3658 const std::string& property_name,
3659 const std::vector<std::string>& reserved_names) {
3660 if (std::find(reserved_names.begin(), reserved_names.end(), property_name) !=
3661 reserved_names.end()) {
3662 ADD_FAILURE() << "Reserved key used in RecordProperty(): " << property_name
3663 << " (" << FormatWordList(reserved_names)
3664 << " are reserved by " << GTEST_NAME_ << ")";
3665 return false;
3666 }
3667 return true;
3668}
3669
3670// Adds a failure if the key is a reserved attribute of the element named
3671// xml_element. Returns true if the property is valid.
3672bool TestResult::ValidateTestProperty(const std::string& xml_element,
3673 const TestProperty& test_property) {
3674 return ValidateTestPropertyName(test_property.key(),
3675 GetReservedAttributesForElement(xml_element));
3676}

3781// Google Test requires all tests in the same test case to use the same test
3782// fixture class. This function checks if the current test has the
3783// same fixture class as the first test in the current test case. If
3784// yes, it returns true; otherwise it generates a Google Test failure and
3785// returns false.
3786bool Test::HasSameFixtureClass() {
3787 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
3788 const TestCase* const test_case = impl->current_test_case();
3789
3790 // Info about the first test in the current test case.
3791 const TestInfo* const first_test_info = test_case->test_info_list()[0];
3792 const internal::TypeId first_fixture_id = first_test_info->fixture_class_id_;
3793 const char* const first_test_name = first_test_info->name();
3794
3795 // Info about the current test.
3796 const TestInfo* const this_test_info = impl->current_test_info();
3797 const internal::TypeId this_fixture_id = this_test_info->fixture_class_id_;
3798 const char* const this_test_name = this_test_info->name();
3799
3800 if (this_fixture_id != first_fixture_id) {
3801 // Is the first test defined using TEST?
3802 const bool first_is_TEST = first_fixture_id == internal::GetTestTypeId();
3803 // Is this test defined using TEST?
3804 const bool this_is_TEST = this_fixture_id == internal::GetTestTypeId();
3805
3806 if (first_is_TEST || this_is_TEST) {
3807 // Both TEST and TEST_F appear in same test case, which is incorrect.
3808 // Tell the user how to fix this.
3809
3810 // Gets the name of the TEST and the name of the TEST_F. Note
3811 // that first_is_TEST and this_is_TEST cannot both be true, as
3812 // the fixture IDs are different for the two tests.
3813 const char* const TEST_name =
3814 first_is_TEST ? first_test_name : this_test_name;
3815 const char* const TEST_F_name =
3816 first_is_TEST ? this_test_name : first_test_name;
3817
3818 ADD_FAILURE()
3819 << "All tests in the same test case must use the same test fixture\n"
3820 << "class, so mixing TEST_F and TEST in the same test case is\n"
3821 << "illegal. In test case " << this_test_info->test_case_name()
3822 << ",\n"
3823 << "test " << TEST_F_name << " is defined using TEST_F but\n"
3824 << "test " << TEST_name << " is defined using TEST. You probably\n"
3825 << "want to change the TEST to TEST_F or move it to another test\n"
3826 << "case.";
3827 } else {
3828 // Two fixture classes with the same name appear in two different
3829 // namespaces, which is not allowed. Tell the user how to fix this.
3830 ADD_FAILURE()
3831 << "All tests in the same test case must use the same test fixture\n"
3832 << "class. However, in test case "
3833 << this_test_info->test_case_name() << ",\n"
3834 << "you defined test " << first_test_name
3835 << " and test " << this_test_name << "\n"
3836 << "using two different test fixture classes. This can happen if\n"
3837 << "the two classes are from different namespaces or translation\n"
3838 << "units and have the same name. You should probably rename one\n"
3839 << "of the classes to put the tests into different test cases.";
3840 }
3841 return false;
3842 }
3843
3844 return true;
3845}
