3847#if GTEST_HAS_SEH
3848
3849// Adds an "exception thrown" fatal failure to the current test. This
3850// function returns its result via an output parameter pointer because VC++
3851// prohibits creation of objects with destructors on stack in functions
3852// using __try (see error C2712).
3853static std::string* FormatSehExceptionMessage(DWORD exception_code,
3854 const char* location) {
3855 Message message;
3856 message << "SEH exception with code 0x" << std::setbase(16) <<
3857 exception_code << std::setbase(10) << " thrown in " << location << ".";
3858
3859 return new std::string(message.GetString());
3860}
3861
3862#endif // GTEST_HAS_SEH
3863
3864namespace internal {
3865
3866#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
3867
3868// Adds an "exception thrown" fatal failure to the current test.
3869static std::string FormatCxxExceptionMessage(const char* description,
3870 const char* location) {
3871 Message message;
3872 if (description != NULL) {
3873 message << "C++ exception with description \"" << description << "\"";
3874 } else {
3875 message << "Unknown C++ exception";
3876 }
3877 message << " thrown in " << location << ".";
3878
3879 return message.GetString();
3880}
3881
3882static std::string PrintTestPartResultToString(
3883 const TestPartResult& test_part_result);
3884
3885GoogleTestFailureException::GoogleTestFailureException(
3886 const TestPartResult& failure)
3887 : ::std::runtime_error(PrintTestPartResultToString(failure).c_str()) {}
3888
3889#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
3890
3891// We put these helper functions in the internal namespace as IBM's xlC
3892// compiler rejects the code if they were declared static.
3893
3894// Runs the given method and handles SEH exceptions it throws, when
3895// SEH is supported; returns the 0-value for type Result in case of an
3896// SEH exception. (Microsoft compilers cannot handle SEH and C++
3897// exceptions in the same function. Therefore, we provide a separate
3898// wrapper function for handling SEH exceptions.)
3899template <class T, typename Result>
3900Result HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
3901 T* object, Result (T::*method)(), const char* location) {
3902#if GTEST_HAS_SEH
3903 __try {
3904 return (object->*method)();
3905 } __except (internal::UnitTestOptions::GTestShouldProcessSEH( // NOLINT
3906 GetExceptionCode())) {
3907 // We create the exception message on the heap because VC++ prohibits
3908 // creation of objects with destructors on stack in functions using __try
3909 // (see error C2712).
3910 std::string* exception_message = FormatSehExceptionMessage(
3911 GetExceptionCode(), location);
3912 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
3913 *exception_message);
3914 delete exception_message;
3915 return static_cast<Result>(0);
3916 }
3917#else
3918 CV_UNUSED(location);
3919 return (object->*method)();
3920#endif // GTEST_HAS_SEH
3921}
3922
3923// Runs the given method and catches and reports C++ and/or SEH-style
3924// exceptions, if they are supported; returns the 0-value for type
3925// Result in case of an SEH exception.
3926template <class T, typename Result>
3927Result HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
3928 T* object, Result (T::*method)(), const char* location) {
3929 // NOTE: The user code can affect the way in which Google Test handles
3930 // exceptions by setting GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions), but only before
3931 // RUN_ALL_TESTS() starts. It is technically possible to check the flag
3932 // after the exception is caught and either report or re-throw the
3933 // exception based on the flag's value:
3934 //
3935 // try {
3936 // // Perform the test method.
3937 // } catch (...) {
3938 // if (GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions))
3939 // // Report the exception as failure.
3940 // else
3941 // throw; // Re-throws the original exception.
3942 // }
3943 //
3944 // However, the purpose of this flag is to allow the program to drop into
3945 // the debugger when the exception is thrown. On most platforms, once the
3946 // control enters the catch block, the exception origin information is
3947 // lost and the debugger will stop the program at the point of the
3948 // re-throw in this function -- instead of at the point of the original
3949 // throw statement in the code under test. For this reason, we perform
3950 // the check early, sacrificing the ability to affect Google Test's
3951 // exception handling in the method where the exception is thrown.
3952 if (internal::GetUnitTestImpl()->catch_exceptions()) {
3953#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
3954 try {
3955 return HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(object, method, location);
3956 } catch (const AssertionException&) { // NOLINT
3957 // This failure was reported already.
3958 } catch (const internal::GoogleTestFailureException&) { // NOLINT
3959 // This exception type can only be thrown by a failed Google
3960 // Test assertion with the intention of letting another testing
3961 // framework catch it. Therefore we just re-throw it.
3962 throw;
3963 } catch (const std::exception& e) { // NOLINT
3964 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(
3965 TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
3966 FormatCxxExceptionMessage(e.what(), location));
3967 } catch (...) { // NOLINT
3968 internal::ReportFailureInUnknownLocation(
3969 TestPartResult::kFatalFailure,
3970 FormatCxxExceptionMessage(NULL, location));
3971 }
3972 return static_cast<Result>(0);
3973#else
3974 return HandleSehExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(object, method, location);
3975#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
3976 } else {
3977 return (object->*method)();
3978 }
3979}

3981} // namespace internal

3983// Runs the test and updates the test result.
3984void Test::Run() {
3985 if (!HasSameFixtureClass()) return;
3986
3987 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
3988 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
3989 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(this, &Test::SetUp, "SetUp()");
3990 // We will run the test only if SetUp() was successful.
3991 if (!HasFatalFailure()) {
3992 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
3993 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
3994 this, &Test::TestBody, "the test body");
3995 }
3996
3997 // However, we want to clean up as much as possible. Hence we will
3998 // always call TearDown(), even if SetUp() or the test body has
3999 // failed.
4000 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
4001 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
4002 this, &Test::TearDown, "TearDown()");
4003}

4044// Creates a new TestInfo object and registers it with Google Test;
4045// returns the created object.
4046//
4047// Arguments:
4048//
4049// test_case_name: name of the test case
4050// name: name of the test
4051// type_param: the name of the test's type parameter, or NULL if
4052// this is not a typed or a type-parameterized test.
4053// value_param: text representation of the test's value parameter,
4054// or NULL if this is not a value-parameterized test.
4055// code_location: code location where the test is defined
4056// fixture_class_id: ID of the test fixture class
4057// set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test case
4058// tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test case
4059// factory: pointer to the factory that creates a test object.
4060// The newly created TestInfo instance will assume
4061// ownership of the factory object.
4062TestInfo* MakeAndRegisterTestInfo(
4063 const char* test_case_name,
4064 const char* name,
4065 const char* type_param,
4066 const char* value_param,
4067 CodeLocation code_location,
4068 TypeId fixture_class_id,
4069 SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc,
4070 TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc,
4071 TestFactoryBase* factory) {
4072 TestInfo* const test_info =
4073 new TestInfo(test_case_name, name, type_param, value_param,
4074 code_location, fixture_class_id, factory);
4075 GetUnitTestImpl()->AddTestInfo(set_up_tc, tear_down_tc, test_info);
4076 return test_info;
4077}

4079void ReportInvalidTestCaseType(const char* test_case_name,
4080 CodeLocation code_location) {
4081 Message errors;
4082 errors
4083 << "Attempted redefinition of test case " << test_case_name << ".\n"
4084 << "All tests in the same test case must use the same test fixture\n"
4085 << "class. However, in test case " << test_case_name << ", you tried\n"
4086 << "to define a test using a fixture class different from the one\n"
4087 << "used earlier. This can happen if the two fixture classes are\n"
4088 << "from different namespaces and have the same name. You should\n"
4089 << "probably rename one of the classes to put the tests into different\n"
4090 << "test cases.";
4091
4092 GTEST_LOG_(ERROR) << FormatFileLocation(code_location.file.c_str(),
4093 code_location.line)
4094 << " " << errors.GetString();
4095}

4100// A predicate that checks the test name of a TestInfo against a known

4140
4141// Creates the test object, runs it, records its result, and then
4142// deletes it.
4143void TestInfo::Run() {
4144 if (!should_run_) return;
4145
4146 // Tells UnitTest where to store test result.
4147 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
4148 impl->set_current_test_info(this);
4149
4150 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
4151
4152 // Notifies the unit test event listeners that a test is about to start.
4153 repeater->OnTestStart(*this);
4154
4155 const TimeInMillis start = internal::GetTimeInMillis();
4156
4157 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
4158
4159 // Creates the test object.
4160 Test* const test = internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
4161 factory_, &internal::TestFactoryBase::CreateTest,
4162 "the test fixture's constructor");
4163
4164 // Runs the test if the constructor didn't generate a fatal failure.
4165 // Note that the object will not be null
4166 if (!Test::HasFatalFailure()) {
4167 // This doesn't throw as all user code that can throw are wrapped into
4168 // exception handling code.
4169 test->Run();
4170 }
4171
4172 // Deletes the test object.
4173 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
4174 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
4175 test, &Test::DeleteSelf_, "the test fixture's destructor");
4176
4177 result_.set_elapsed_time(internal::GetTimeInMillis() - start);
4178
4179 // Notifies the unit test event listener that a test has just finished.
4180 repeater->OnTestEnd(*this);
4181
4182 // Tells UnitTest to stop associating assertion results to this
4183 // test.
4184 impl->set_current_test_info(NULL);
4185}

4270
4271// Runs every test in this TestCase.
4272void TestCase::Run() {
4273 if (!should_run_) return;
4274
4275 internal::UnitTestImpl* const impl = internal::GetUnitTestImpl();
4276 impl->set_current_test_case(this);
4277
4278 TestEventListener* repeater = UnitTest::GetInstance()->listeners().repeater();
4279
4280 repeater->OnTestCaseStart(*this);
4281 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
4282 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
4283 this, &TestCase::RunSetUpTestCase, "SetUpTestCase()");
4284
4285 const internal::TimeInMillis start = internal::GetTimeInMillis();
4286 for (int i = 0; i < total_test_count(); i++) {
4287 GetMutableTestInfo(i)->Run();
4288 }
4289 elapsed_time_ = internal::GetTimeInMillis() - start;
4290
4291 impl->os_stack_trace_getter()->UponLeavingGTest();
4292 internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
4293 this, &TestCase::RunTearDownTestCase, "TearDownTestCase()");
4294
4295 repeater->OnTestCaseEnd(*this);
4296 impl->set_current_test_case(NULL);
4297}

4317// Formats a countable noun. Depending on its quantity, either the
4318// singular form or the plural form is used. e.g.
4319//
4320// FormatCountableNoun(1, "formula", "formuli") returns "1 formula".
4321// FormatCountableNoun(5, "book", "books") returns "5 books".
4322static std::string FormatCountableNoun(int count,
4323 const char * singular_form,
4324 const char * plural_form) {
4325 return internal::StreamableToString(count) + " " +
4326 (count == 1 ? singular_form : plural_form);
4327}
4328
4329// Formats the count of tests.
4330static std::string FormatTestCount(int test_count) {
4331 return FormatCountableNoun(test_count, "test", "tests");
4332}
4333
4334// Formats the count of test cases.
4335static std::string FormatTestCaseCount(int test_case_count) {
4336 return FormatCountableNoun(test_case_count, "test case", "test cases");
4337}
4338
4339// Converts a TestPartResult::Type enum to human-friendly string
4340// representation. Both kNonFatalFailure and kFatalFailure are translated
4341// to "Failure", as the user usually doesn't care about the difference
4342// between the two when viewing the test result.
4343static const char * TestPartResultTypeToString(TestPartResult::Type type) {
4344 switch (type) {
4345 case TestPartResult::kSuccess:
4346 return "Success";
4347
4348 case TestPartResult::kNonFatalFailure:
4349 case TestPartResult::kFatalFailure:
4350#ifdef _MSC_VER
4351 return "error: ";
4352#else
4353 return "Failure\n";
4354#endif
4355 default:
4356 return "Unknown result type";
4357 }
4358}

4360namespace internal {
4361
4362// Prints a TestPartResult to an std::string.
4363static std::string PrintTestPartResultToString(
4364 const TestPartResult& test_part_result) {
4365 return (Message()
4366 << internal::FormatFileLocation(test_part_result.file_name(),
4367 test_part_result.line_number())
4368 << " " << TestPartResultTypeToString(test_part_result.type())
4369 << test_part_result.message()).GetString();
4370}
4371
4372// Prints a TestPartResult.
4373static void PrintTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& test_part_result) {
4374 const std::string& result =
4375 PrintTestPartResultToString(test_part_result);
4376 printf("%s\n", result.c_str());
4377 fflush(stdout);
4378 // If the test program runs in Visual Studio or a debugger, the
4379 // following statements add the test part result message to the Output
4380 // window such that the user can double-click on it to jump to the
4381 // corresponding source code location; otherwise they do nothing.
4382#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
4383 // We don't call OutputDebugString*() on Windows Mobile, as printing
4384 // to stdout is done by OutputDebugString() there already - we don't
4385 // want the same message printed twice.
4386 ::OutputDebugStringA(result.c_str());
4387 ::OutputDebugStringA("\n");
4388#endif
4389}

4391// class PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter
4392
4393enum GTestColor {
4394 COLOR_DEFAULT,
4395 COLOR_RED,
4396 COLOR_GREEN,
4397 COLOR_YELLOW
4398};
4399
4400#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE && \
4401 !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW
4402
4403// Returns the character attribute for the given color.
4404static WORD GetColorAttribute(GTestColor color) {
4405 switch (color) {
4406 case COLOR_RED: return FOREGROUND_RED;
4407 case COLOR_GREEN: return FOREGROUND_GREEN;
4408 case COLOR_YELLOW: return FOREGROUND_RED | FOREGROUND_GREEN;
4409 default: return 0;
4410 }
4411}
4412
4413static int GetBitOffset(WORD color_mask) {
4414 if (color_mask == 0) return 0;
4415
4416 int bitOffset = 0;
4417 while ((color_mask & 1) == 0) {
4418 color_mask >>= 1;
4419 ++bitOffset;
4420 }
4421 return bitOffset;
4422}
4423
4424static WORD GetNewColor(GTestColor color, WORD old_color_attrs) {
4425 // Let's reuse the BG
4426 static const WORD background_mask = BACKGROUND_BLUE | BACKGROUND_GREEN |
4427 BACKGROUND_RED | BACKGROUND_INTENSITY;
4428 static const WORD foreground_mask = FOREGROUND_BLUE | FOREGROUND_GREEN |
4429 FOREGROUND_RED | FOREGROUND_INTENSITY;
4430 const WORD existing_bg = old_color_attrs & background_mask;
4431
4432 WORD new_color =
4433 GetColorAttribute(color) | existing_bg | FOREGROUND_INTENSITY;
4434 static const int bg_bitOffset = GetBitOffset(background_mask);
4435 static const int fg_bitOffset = GetBitOffset(foreground_mask);
4436
4437 if (((new_color & background_mask) >> bg_bitOffset) ==
4438 ((new_color & foreground_mask) >> fg_bitOffset)) {
4439 new_color ^= FOREGROUND_INTENSITY; // invert intensity
4440 }
4441 return new_color;
4442}
4443
4444#else
4445
4446// Returns the ANSI color code for the given color. COLOR_DEFAULT is
4447// an invalid input.
4448static const char* GetAnsiColorCode(GTestColor color) {
4449 switch (color) {
4450 case COLOR_RED: return "1";
4451 case COLOR_GREEN: return "2";
4452 case COLOR_YELLOW: return "3";
4453 default: return NULL;
4454 };
4455}
4456
4457#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
4458
4459// Returns true iff Google Test should use colors in the output.
4460bool ShouldUseColor(bool stdout_is_tty) {
4461 const char* const gtest_color = GTEST_FLAG(color).c_str();
4462
4463 if (String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(gtest_color, "auto")) {
4464#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW
4465 // On Windows the TERM variable is usually not set, but the
4466 // console there does support colors.
4467 return stdout_is_tty;
4468#else
4469 // On non-Windows platforms, we rely on the TERM variable.
4470 const char* const term = posix::GetEnv("TERM");
4471 const bool term_supports_color =
4472 String::CStringEquals(term, "xterm") ||
4473 String::CStringEquals(term, "xterm-color") ||
4474 String::CStringEquals(term, "xterm-256color") ||
4475 String::CStringEquals(term, "screen") ||
4476 String::CStringEquals(term, "screen-256color") ||
4477 String::CStringEquals(term, "tmux") ||
4478 String::CStringEquals(term, "tmux-256color") ||
4479 String::CStringEquals(term, "rxvt-unicode") ||
4480 String::CStringEquals(term, "rxvt-unicode-256color") ||
4481 String::CStringEquals(term, "linux") ||
4482 String::CStringEquals(term, "cygwin");
4483 return stdout_is_tty && term_supports_color;
4484#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
4485 }
4486
4487 return String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(gtest_color, "yes") ||
4488 String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(gtest_color, "true") ||
4489 String::CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(gtest_color, "t") ||
4490 String::CStringEquals(gtest_color, "1");
4491 // We take "yes", "true", "t", and "1" as meaning "yes". If the
4492 // value is neither one of these nor "auto", we treat it as "no" to
4493 // be conservative.
4494}
4495
4496// Helpers for printing colored strings to stdout. Note that on Windows, we
4497// cannot simply emit special characters and have the terminal change colors.
4498// This routine must actually emit the characters rather than return a string
4499// that would be colored when printed, as can be done on Linux.
4500static void ColoredPrintf(GTestColor color, const char* fmt, ...) {
4501 va_list args;
4502 va_start(args, fmt);
4503
4504#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN || GTEST_OS_ZOS || \
4505 GTEST_OS_IOS || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
4506 const bool use_color = AlwaysFalse();
4507#else
4508 static const bool in_color_mode =
4509 ShouldUseColor(posix::IsATTY(posix::FileNo(stdout)) != 0);
4510 const bool use_color = in_color_mode && (color != COLOR_DEFAULT);
4511#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN || GTEST_OS_ZOS
4512 // The '!= 0' comparison is necessary to satisfy MSVC 7.1.
4513
4514 if (!use_color) {
4515 vprintf(fmt, args);
4516 va_end(args);
4517 return;
4518 }
4519
4520#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE && \
4521 !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW
4522 const HANDLE stdout_handle = GetStdHandle(STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE);
4523
4524 // Gets the current text color.
4525 CONSOLE_SCREEN_BUFFER_INFO buffer_info;
4526 GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo(stdout_handle, &buffer_info);
4527 const WORD old_color_attrs = buffer_info.wAttributes;
4528 const WORD new_color = GetNewColor(color, old_color_attrs);
4529
4530 // We need to flush the stream buffers into the console before each
4531 // SetConsoleTextAttribute call lest it affect the text that is already
4532 // printed but has not yet reached the console.
4533 fflush(stdout);
4534 SetConsoleTextAttribute(stdout_handle, new_color);
4535
4536 vprintf(fmt, args);
4537
4538 fflush(stdout);
4539 // Restores the text color.
4540 SetConsoleTextAttribute(stdout_handle, old_color_attrs);
4541#else
4542 printf("\033[0;3%sm", GetAnsiColorCode(color));
4543 vprintf(fmt, args);
4544 printf("\033[m"); // Resets the terminal to default.
4545#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
4546 va_end(args);
4547}
4548
4549// Text printed in Google Test's text output and --gtest_list_tests
4550// output to label the type parameter and value parameter for a test.
4551static const char kTypeParamLabel[] = "TypeParam";
4552static const char kValueParamLabel[] = "GetParam()";
4553
4554static void PrintFullTestCommentIfPresent(const TestInfo& test_info) {
4555 const char* const type_param = test_info.type_param();
4556 const char* const value_param = test_info.value_param();
4557
4558 if (type_param != NULL || value_param != NULL) {
4559 printf(", where ");
4560 if (type_param != NULL) {
4561 printf("%s = %s", kTypeParamLabel, type_param);
4562 if (value_param != NULL)
4563 printf(" and ");
4564 }
4565 if (value_param != NULL) {
4566 printf("%s = %s", kValueParamLabel, value_param);
4567 }
4568 }
4569}

4571// This class implements the TestEventListener interface.
4572//
4573// Class PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter is copyable.
4574class PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter : public TestEventListener {
4575 public:
4576 PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter() {}
4577 static void PrintTestName(const char * test_case, const char * test) {
4578 printf("%s.%s", test_case, test);
4579 }
4580
4581 // The following methods override what's in the TestEventListener class.
4582 virtual void OnTestProgramStart(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
4583 virtual void OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
4584 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4585 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
4586 virtual void OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& test_case);
4587 virtual void OnTestStart(const TestInfo& test_info);
4588 virtual void OnTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& result);
4589 virtual void OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& test_info);
4590 virtual void OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& test_case);
4591 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4592 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
4593 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
4594 virtual void OnTestProgramEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
4595
4596 private:
4597 static void PrintFailedTests(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4598};
4599
4600 // Fired before each iteration of tests starts.
4601void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestIterationStart(
4602 const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration) {
4603 if (GTEST_FLAG(repeat) != 1)
4604 printf("\nRepeating all tests (iteration %d) . . .\n\n", iteration + 1);
4605
4606 const char* const filter = GTEST_FLAG(filter).c_str();
4607
4608 // Prints the filter if it's not *. This reminds the user that some
4609 // tests may be skipped.
4610 if (!String::CStringEquals(filter, kUniversalFilter)) {
4611 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_YELLOW,
4612 "Note: %s filter = %s\n", GTEST_NAME_, filter);
4613 }
4614
4615 const char* const param_filter = GTEST_FLAG(param_filter).c_str();
4616
4617 // Ditto.
4618 if (!String::CStringEquals(param_filter, kUniversalFilter)) {
4619 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_YELLOW,
4620 "Note: %s parameter filter = %s\n", GTEST_NAME_, param_filter);
4621 }
4622
4623 if (internal::ShouldShard(kTestTotalShards, kTestShardIndex, false)) {
4624 const Int32 shard_index = Int32FromEnvOrDie(kTestShardIndex, -1);
4625 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_YELLOW,
4626 "Note: This is test shard %d of %s.\n",
4627 static_cast<int>(shard_index) + 1,
4628 internal::posix::GetEnv(kTestTotalShards));
4629 }
4630
4631 if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) {
4632 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_YELLOW,
4633 "Note: Randomizing tests' orders with a seed of %d .\n",
4634 unit_test.random_seed());
4635 }
4636
4637 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[==========] ");
4638 printf("Running %s from %s.\n",
4639 FormatTestCount(unit_test.test_to_run_count()).c_str(),
4640 FormatTestCaseCount(unit_test.test_case_to_run_count()).c_str());
4641 fflush(stdout);
4642}
4643
4644void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(
4645 const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {
4646 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[----------] ");
4647 printf("Global test environment set-up.\n");
4648 fflush(stdout);
4649}
4650
4651void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& test_case) {
4652 const std::string counts =
4653 FormatCountableNoun(test_case.test_to_run_count(), "test", "tests");
4654 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[----------] ");
4655 printf("%s from %s", counts.c_str(), test_case.name());
4656 if (test_case.type_param() == NULL) {
4657 printf("\n");
4658 } else {
4659 printf(", where %s = %s\n", kTypeParamLabel, test_case.type_param());
4660 }
4661 fflush(stdout);
4662}
4663
4664void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestStart(const TestInfo& test_info) {
4665 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[ RUN ] ");
4666 PrintTestName(test_info.test_case_name(), test_info.name());
4667 PrintFullTestCommentIfPresent(test_info);
4668 printf("\n");
4669 fflush(stdout);
4670}
4671
4672// Called after an assertion failure.
4673void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestPartResult(
4674 const TestPartResult& result) {
4675 // If the test part succeeded, we don't need to do anything.
4676 if (result.type() == TestPartResult::kSuccess)
4677 return;
4678
4679 // Print failure message from the assertion (e.g. expected this and got that).
4680 PrintTestPartResult(result);
4681 fflush(stdout);
4682}
4683
4684void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& test_info) {
4685 if (test_info.result()->Passed()) {
4686 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[ OK ] ");
4687 } else {
4688 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, "[ FAILED ] ");
4689 }
4690 PrintTestName(test_info.test_case_name(), test_info.name());
4691 if (test_info.result()->Failed())
4692 PrintFullTestCommentIfPresent(test_info);
4693
4694 if (GTEST_FLAG(print_time)) {
4695 printf(" (%s ms)\n", internal::StreamableToString(
4696 test_info.result()->elapsed_time()).c_str());
4697 } else {
4698 printf("\n");
4699 }
4700 fflush(stdout);
4701}
4702
4703void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& test_case) {
4704 if (!GTEST_FLAG(print_time)) return;
4705
4706 const std::string counts =
4707 FormatCountableNoun(test_case.test_to_run_count(), "test", "tests");
4708 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[----------] ");
4709 printf("%s from %s (%s ms total)\n\n",
4710 counts.c_str(), test_case.name(),
4711 internal::StreamableToString(test_case.elapsed_time()).c_str());
4712 fflush(stdout);
4713}
4714
4715void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(
4716 const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {
4717 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[----------] ");
4718 printf("Global test environment tear-down\n");
4719 fflush(stdout);
4720}
4721
4722// Internal helper for printing the list of failed tests.
4723void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintFailedTests(const UnitTest& unit_test) {
4724 const int failed_test_count = unit_test.failed_test_count();
4725 if (failed_test_count == 0) {
4726 return;
4727 }
4728
4729 for (int i = 0; i < unit_test.total_test_case_count(); ++i) {
4730 const TestCase& test_case = *unit_test.GetTestCase(i);
4731 if (!test_case.should_run() || (test_case.failed_test_count() == 0)) {
4732 continue;
4733 }
4734 for (int j = 0; j < test_case.total_test_count(); ++j) {
4735 const TestInfo& test_info = *test_case.GetTestInfo(j);
4736 if (!test_info.should_run() || test_info.result()->Passed()) {
4737 continue;
4738 }
4739 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, "[ FAILED ] ");
4740 printf("%s.%s", test_case.name(), test_info.name());
4741 PrintFullTestCommentIfPresent(test_info);
4742 printf("\n");
4743 }
4744 }
4745}
4746
4747void PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter::OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test,
4748 int /*iteration*/) {
4749 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[==========] ");
4750 printf("%s from %s ran.",
4751 FormatTestCount(unit_test.test_to_run_count()).c_str(),
4752 FormatTestCaseCount(unit_test.test_case_to_run_count()).c_str());
4753 if (GTEST_FLAG(print_time)) {
4754 printf(" (%s ms total)",
4755 internal::StreamableToString(unit_test.elapsed_time()).c_str());
4756 }
4757 printf("\n");
4758 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_GREEN, "[ PASSED ] ");
4759 printf("%s.\n", FormatTestCount(unit_test.successful_test_count()).c_str());
4760
4761 int num_failures = unit_test.failed_test_count();
4762 if (!unit_test.Passed()) {
4763 const int failed_test_count = unit_test.failed_test_count();
4764 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, "[ FAILED ] ");
4765 printf("%s, listed below:\n", FormatTestCount(failed_test_count).c_str());
4766 PrintFailedTests(unit_test);
4767 printf("\n%2d FAILED %s\n", num_failures,
4768 num_failures == 1 ? "TEST" : "TESTS");
4769 }
4770
4771 int num_disabled = unit_test.reportable_disabled_test_count();
4772 if (num_disabled && !GTEST_FLAG(also_run_disabled_tests)) {
4773 if (!num_failures) {
4774 printf("\n"); // Add a spacer if no FAILURE banner is displayed.
4775 }
4776 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_YELLOW,
4777 " YOU HAVE %d DISABLED %s\n\n",
4778 num_disabled,
4779 num_disabled == 1 ? "TEST" : "TESTS");
4780 }
4781 // Ensure that Google Test output is printed before, e.g., heapchecker output.
4782 fflush(stdout);
4783}
4784
4785// End PrettyUnitTestResultPrinter

4787// class TestEventRepeater
4788//
4789// This class forwards events to other event listeners.
4790class TestEventRepeater : public TestEventListener {
4791 public:
4792 TestEventRepeater() : forwarding_enabled_(true) {}
4793 virtual ~TestEventRepeater();
4794 void Append(TestEventListener *listener);
4795 TestEventListener* Release(TestEventListener* listener);
4796
4797 // Controls whether events will be forwarded to listeners_. Set to false
4798 // in death test child processes.
4799 bool forwarding_enabled() const { return forwarding_enabled_; }
4800 void set_forwarding_enabled(bool enable) { forwarding_enabled_ = enable; }
4801
4802 virtual void OnTestProgramStart(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4803 virtual void OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
4804 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4805 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4806 virtual void OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& test_case);
4807 virtual void OnTestStart(const TestInfo& test_info);
4808 virtual void OnTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& result);
4809 virtual void OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& test_info);
4810 virtual void OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& test_case);
4811 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4812 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4813 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
4814 virtual void OnTestProgramEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test);
4815
4816 private:
4817 // Controls whether events will be forwarded to listeners_. Set to false
4818 // in death test child processes.
4819 bool forwarding_enabled_;
4820 // The list of listeners that receive events.
4821 std::vector<TestEventListener*> listeners_;
4822
4823 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(TestEventRepeater);
4824};
4825
4826TestEventRepeater::~TestEventRepeater() {
4827 ForEach(listeners_, Delete<TestEventListener>);
4828}
4829
4830void TestEventRepeater::Append(TestEventListener *listener) {
4831 listeners_.push_back(listener);
4832}
4833
4834// FIXME: Factor the search functionality into Vector::Find.
4835TestEventListener* TestEventRepeater::Release(TestEventListener *listener) {
4836 for (size_t i = 0; i < listeners_.size(); ++i) {
4837 if (listeners_[i] == listener) {
4838 listeners_.erase(listeners_.begin() + i);
4839 return listener;
4840 }
4841 }
4842
4843 return NULL;
4844}
4845
4846// Since most methods are very similar, use macros to reduce boilerplate.
4847// This defines a member that forwards the call to all listeners.
4848#define GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(Name, Type) \
4849void TestEventRepeater::Name(const Type& parameter) { \
4850 if (forwarding_enabled_) { \
4851 for (size_t i = 0; i < listeners_.size(); i++) { \
4852 listeners_[i]->Name(parameter); \
4853 } \
4854 } \
4855}
4856// This defines a member that forwards the call to all listeners in reverse
4857// order.
4858#define GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(Name, Type) \
4859void TestEventRepeater::Name(const Type& parameter) { \
4860 if (forwarding_enabled_) { \
4861 for (int i = static_cast<int>(listeners_.size()) - 1; i >= 0; i--) { \
4862 listeners_[i]->Name(parameter); \
4863 } \
4864 } \
4865}
4866
4867GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestProgramStart, UnitTest)
4868GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart, UnitTest)
4869GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestCaseStart, TestCase)
4870GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestStart, TestInfo)
4871GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestPartResult, TestPartResult)
4872GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart, UnitTest)
4873GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd, UnitTest)
4874GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd, UnitTest)
4875GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestEnd, TestInfo)
4876GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestCaseEnd, TestCase)
4877GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_(OnTestProgramEnd, UnitTest)
4878
4879#undef GTEST_REPEATER_METHOD_
4880#undef GTEST_REVERSE_REPEATER_METHOD_
4881
4882void TestEventRepeater::OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& unit_test,
4883 int iteration) {
4884 if (forwarding_enabled_) {
4885 for (size_t i = 0; i < listeners_.size(); i++) {
4886 listeners_[i]->OnTestIterationStart(unit_test, iteration);
4887 }
4888 }
4889}
4890
4891void TestEventRepeater::OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test,
4892 int iteration) {
4893 if (forwarding_enabled_) {
4894 for (int i = static_cast<int>(listeners_.size()) - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
4895 listeners_[i]->OnTestIterationEnd(unit_test, iteration);
4896 }
4897 }
4898}
4899
4900// End TestEventRepeater

4902// This class generates an XML output file.
4903class XmlUnitTestResultPrinter : public EmptyTestEventListener {
4904 public:
4905 explicit XmlUnitTestResultPrinter(const char* output_file);
4906
4907 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
4908 void ListTestsMatchingFilter(const std::vector<TestCase*>& test_cases);
4909
4910 // Prints an XML summary of all unit tests.
4911 static void PrintXmlTestsList(std::ostream* stream,
4912 const std::vector<TestCase*>& test_cases);
4913
4914 private:
4915 // Is c a whitespace character that is normalized to a space character
4916 // when it appears in an XML attribute value?
4917 static bool IsNormalizableWhitespace(char c) {
4918 return c == 0x9 || c == 0xA || c == 0xD;
4919 }
4920
4921 // May c appear in a well-formed XML document?
4922 static bool IsValidXmlCharacter(char c) {
4923 return IsNormalizableWhitespace(c) || c >= 0x20;
4924 }
4925
4926 // Returns an XML-escaped copy of the input string str. If
4927 // is_attribute is true, the text is meant to appear as an attribute
4928 // value, and normalizable whitespace is preserved by replacing it
4929 // with character references.
4930 static std::string EscapeXml(const std::string& str, bool is_attribute);
4931
4932 // Returns the given string with all characters invalid in XML removed.
4933 static std::string RemoveInvalidXmlCharacters(const std::string& str);
4934
4935 // Convenience wrapper around EscapeXml when str is an attribute value.
4936 static std::string EscapeXmlAttribute(const std::string& str) {
4937 return EscapeXml(str, true);
4938 }
4939
4940 // Convenience wrapper around EscapeXml when str is not an attribute value.
4941 static std::string EscapeXmlText(const char* str) {
4942 return EscapeXml(str, false);
4943 }
4944
4945 // Verifies that the given attribute belongs to the given element and
4946 // streams the attribute as XML.
4947 static void OutputXmlAttribute(std::ostream* stream,
4948 const std::string& element_name,
4949 const std::string& name,
4950 const std::string& value);
4951
4952 // Streams an XML CDATA section, escaping invalid CDATA sequences as needed.
4953 static void OutputXmlCDataSection(::std::ostream* stream, const char* data);
4954
4955 // Streams an XML representation of a TestInfo object.
4956 static void OutputXmlTestInfo(::std::ostream* stream,
4957 const char* test_case_name,
4958 const TestInfo& test_info);
4959
4960 // Prints an XML representation of a TestCase object
4961 static void PrintXmlTestCase(::std::ostream* stream,
4962 const TestCase& test_case);
4963
4964 // Prints an XML summary of unit_test to output stream out.
4965 static void PrintXmlUnitTest(::std::ostream* stream,
4966 const UnitTest& unit_test);
4967
4968 // Produces a string representing the test properties in a result as space
4969 // delimited XML attributes based on the property key="value" pairs.
4970 // When the std::string is not empty, it includes a space at the beginning,
4971 // to delimit this attribute from prior attributes.
4972 static std::string TestPropertiesAsXmlAttributes(const TestResult& result);
4973
4974 // Streams an XML representation of the test properties of a TestResult
4975 // object.
4976 static void OutputXmlTestProperties(std::ostream* stream,
4977 const TestResult& result);
4978
4979 // The output file.
4980 const std::string output_file_;
4981
4982 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(XmlUnitTestResultPrinter);
4983};
4984
4985// Creates a new XmlUnitTestResultPrinter.
4986XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::XmlUnitTestResultPrinter(const char* output_file)
4987 : output_file_(output_file) {
4988 if (output_file_.empty()) {
4989 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "XML output file may not be null";
4990 }

5012// Returns an XML-escaped copy of the input string str. If is_attribute
5013// is true, the text is meant to appear as an attribute value, and
5014// normalizable whitespace is preserved by replacing it with character
5015// references.
5016//
5017// Invalid XML characters in str, if any, are stripped from the output.
5018// It is expected that most, if not all, of the text processed by this
5019// module will consist of ordinary English text.
5020// If this module is ever modified to produce version 1.1 XML output,
5021// most invalid characters can be retained using character references.
5022// FIXME: It might be nice to have a minimally invasive, human-readable
5023// escaping scheme for invalid characters, rather than dropping them.
5024std::string XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::EscapeXml(
5025 const std::string& str, bool is_attribute) {
5026 Message m;
5027
5028 for (size_t i = 0; i < str.size(); ++i) {
5029 const char ch = str[i];
5030 switch (ch) {
5031 case '<':
5032 m << "&lt;";
5033 break;
5034 case '>':
5035 m << "&gt;";
5036 break;
5037 case '&':
5038 m << "&amp;";
5039 break;
5040 case '\'':
5041 if (is_attribute)
5042 m << "&apos;";
5043 else
5044 m << '\'';
5045 break;
5046 case '"':
5047 if (is_attribute)
5048 m << "&quot;";
5049 else
5050 m << '"';
5051 break;
5052 default:
5053 if (IsValidXmlCharacter(ch)) {
5054 if (is_attribute && IsNormalizableWhitespace(ch))
5055 m << "&#x" << String::FormatByte(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch))
5056 << ";";
5057 else
5058 m << ch;
5059 }
5060 break;
5061 }
5062 }
5063
5064 return m.GetString();
5065}
5066
5067// Returns the given string with all characters invalid in XML removed.
5068// Currently invalid characters are dropped from the string. An
5069// alternative is to replace them with certain characters such as . or ?.
5070std::string XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::RemoveInvalidXmlCharacters(
5071 const std::string& str) {
5072 std::string output;
5073 output.reserve(str.size());
5074 for (std::string::const_iterator it = str.begin(); it != str.end(); ++it)
5075 if (IsValidXmlCharacter(*it))
5076 output.push_back(*it);
5077
5078 return output;
5079}

5081// The following routines generate an XML representation of a UnitTest
5082// object.
5083// GOOGLETEST_CM0009 DO NOT DELETE
5084//
5085// This is how Google Test concepts map to the DTD:
5086//
5087// <testsuites name="AllTests"> <-- corresponds to a UnitTest object
5088// <testsuite name="testcase-name"> <-- corresponds to a TestCase object
5089// <testcase name="test-name"> <-- corresponds to a TestInfo object
5090// <failure message="...">...</failure>
5091// <failure message="...">...</failure>
5092// <failure message="...">...</failure>
5093// <-- individual assertion failures
5094// </testcase>
5095// </testsuite>
5096// </testsuites>
5097
5098// Formats the given time in milliseconds as seconds.
5099std::string FormatTimeInMillisAsSeconds(TimeInMillis ms) {
5100 ::std::stringstream ss;
5101 ss << (static_cast<double>(ms) * 1e-3);
5102 return ss.str();
5103}
5104
5105static bool PortableLocaltime(time_t seconds, struct tm* out) {
5106#if defined(_MSC_VER)
5107 return localtime_s(out, &seconds) == 0;
5108#elif defined(__MINGW32__) || defined(__MINGW64__)
5109 // MINGW <time.h> provides neither localtime_r nor localtime_s, but uses
5110 // Windows' localtime(), which has a thread-local tm buffer.
5111 struct tm* tm_ptr = localtime(&seconds); // NOLINT
5112 if (tm_ptr == NULL)
5113 return false;
5114 *out = *tm_ptr;
5115 return true;
5116#else
5117 return localtime_r(&seconds, out) != NULL;
5118#endif
5119}
5120
5121// Converts the given epoch time in milliseconds to a date string in the ISO
5122// 8601 format, without the timezone information.
5123std::string FormatEpochTimeInMillisAsIso8601(TimeInMillis ms) {
5124 struct tm time_struct;
5125 if (!PortableLocaltime(static_cast<time_t>(ms / 1000), &time_struct))
5126 return "";
5127 // YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
5128 return StreamableToString(time_struct.tm_year + 1900) + "-" +
5129 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_mon + 1) + "-" +
5130 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_mday) + "T" +
5131 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_hour) + ":" +
5132 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_min) + ":" +
5133 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_sec);
5134}
5135
5136// Streams an XML CDATA section, escaping invalid CDATA sequences as needed.
5137void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputXmlCDataSection(::std::ostream* stream,
5138 const char* data) {
5139 const char* segment = data;
5140 *stream << "<![CDATA[";
5141 for (;;) {
5142 const char* const next_segment = strstr(segment, "]]>");
5143 if (next_segment != NULL) {
5144 stream->write(
5145 segment, static_cast<std::streamsize>(next_segment - segment));
5146 *stream << "]]>]]&gt;<![CDATA[";
5147 segment = next_segment + strlen("]]>");
5148 } else {
5149 *stream << segment;
5150 break;
5151 }
5152 }
5153 *stream << "]]>";
5154}
5155
5156void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputXmlAttribute(
5157 std::ostream* stream,
5158 const std::string& element_name,
5159 const std::string& name,
5160 const std::string& value) {
5161 const std::vector<std::string>& allowed_names =
5162 GetReservedAttributesForElement(element_name);
5163
5164 GTEST_CHECK_(std::find(allowed_names.begin(), allowed_names.end(), name) !=
5165 allowed_names.end())
5166 << "Attribute " << name << " is not allowed for element <" << element_name
5167 << ">.";
5168
5169 *stream << " " << name << "=\"" << EscapeXmlAttribute(value) << "\"";
5170}
5171
5172// Prints an XML representation of a TestInfo object.
5173// FIXME: There is also value in printing properties with the plain printer.
5174void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputXmlTestInfo(::std::ostream* stream,
5175 const char* test_case_name,
5176 const TestInfo& test_info) {
5177 const TestResult& result = *test_info.result();
5178 const std::string kTestcase = "testcase";
5179
5180 if (test_info.is_in_another_shard()) {
5181 return;
5182 }
5183
5184 *stream << " <testcase";
5185 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "name", test_info.name());
5186
5187 if (test_info.value_param() != NULL) {
5188 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "value_param",
5189 test_info.value_param());
5190 }
5191 if (test_info.type_param() != NULL) {
5192 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "type_param", test_info.type_param());
5193 }
5194 if (GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) {
5195 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "file", test_info.file());
5196 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "line",
5197 StreamableToString(test_info.line()));
5198 *stream << " />\n";
5199 return;
5200 }
5201
5202 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "status",
5203 test_info.should_run() ? "run" : "notrun");
5204 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "time",
5205 FormatTimeInMillisAsSeconds(result.elapsed_time()));
5206 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestcase, "classname", test_case_name);
5207
5208 int failures = 0;
5209 for (int i = 0; i < result.total_part_count(); ++i) {
5210 const TestPartResult& part = result.GetTestPartResult(i);
5211 if (part.failed()) {
5212 if (++failures == 1) {
5213 *stream << ">\n";
5214 }
5215 const std::string location =
5216 internal::FormatCompilerIndependentFileLocation(part.file_name(),
5217 part.line_number());
5218 const std::string summary = location + "\n" + part.summary();
5219 *stream << " <failure message=\""
5220 << EscapeXmlAttribute(summary.c_str())
5221 << "\" type=\"\">";
5222 const std::string detail = location + "\n" + part.message();
5223 OutputXmlCDataSection(stream, RemoveInvalidXmlCharacters(detail).c_str());
5224 *stream << "</failure>\n";
5225 }
5226 }
5227
5228 if (failures == 0 && result.test_property_count() == 0) {
5229 *stream << " />\n";
5230 } else {
5231 if (failures == 0) {
5232 *stream << ">\n";
5233 }
5234 OutputXmlTestProperties(stream, result);
5235 *stream << " </testcase>\n";
5236 }
5237}
5238
5239// Prints an XML representation of a TestCase object
5240void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintXmlTestCase(std::ostream* stream,
5241 const TestCase& test_case) {
5242 const std::string kTestsuite = "testsuite";
5243 *stream << " <" << kTestsuite;
5244 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuite, "name", test_case.name());
5245 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuite, "tests",
5246 StreamableToString(test_case.reportable_test_count()));
5247 if (!GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) {
5248 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuite, "failures",
5249 StreamableToString(test_case.failed_test_count()));
5250 OutputXmlAttribute(
5251 stream, kTestsuite, "disabled",
5252 StreamableToString(test_case.reportable_disabled_test_count()));
5253 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuite, "errors", "0");
5254 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuite, "time",
5255 FormatTimeInMillisAsSeconds(test_case.elapsed_time()));
5256 *stream << TestPropertiesAsXmlAttributes(test_case.ad_hoc_test_result());
5257 }
5258 *stream << ">\n";
5259 for (int i = 0; i < test_case.total_test_count(); ++i) {
5260 if (test_case.GetTestInfo(i)->is_reportable())
5261 OutputXmlTestInfo(stream, test_case.name(), *test_case.GetTestInfo(i));
5262 }
5263 *stream << " </" << kTestsuite << ">\n";
5264}
5265
5266// Prints an XML summary of unit_test to output stream out.
5267void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintXmlUnitTest(std::ostream* stream,
5268 const UnitTest& unit_test) {
5269 const std::string kTestsuites = "testsuites";
5270
5271 *stream << "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n";
5272 *stream << "<" << kTestsuites;
5273
5274 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "tests",
5275 StreamableToString(unit_test.reportable_test_count()));
5276 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "failures",
5277 StreamableToString(unit_test.failed_test_count()));
5278 OutputXmlAttribute(
5279 stream, kTestsuites, "disabled",
5280 StreamableToString(unit_test.reportable_disabled_test_count()));
5281 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "errors", "0");
5282 OutputXmlAttribute(
5283 stream, kTestsuites, "timestamp",
5284 FormatEpochTimeInMillisAsIso8601(unit_test.start_timestamp()));
5285 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "time",
5286 FormatTimeInMillisAsSeconds(unit_test.elapsed_time()));
5287
5288 if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) {
5289 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "random_seed",
5290 StreamableToString(unit_test.random_seed()));
5291 }
5292 *stream << TestPropertiesAsXmlAttributes(unit_test.ad_hoc_test_result());
5293
5294 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "name", "AllTests");
5295 *stream << ">\n";
5296
5297 for (int i = 0; i < unit_test.total_test_case_count(); ++i) {
5298 if (unit_test.GetTestCase(i)->reportable_test_count() > 0)
5299 PrintXmlTestCase(stream, *unit_test.GetTestCase(i));
5300 }
5301 *stream << "</" << kTestsuites << ">\n";
5302}
5303
5304void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintXmlTestsList(
5305 std::ostream* stream, const std::vector<TestCase*>& test_cases) {
5306 const std::string kTestsuites = "testsuites";
5307
5308 *stream << "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n";
5309 *stream << "<" << kTestsuites;
5310
5311 int total_tests = 0;
5312 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases.size(); ++i) {
5313 total_tests += test_cases[i]->total_test_count();
5314 }
5315 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "tests",
5316 StreamableToString(total_tests));
5317 OutputXmlAttribute(stream, kTestsuites, "name", "AllTests");
5318 *stream << ">\n";
5319
5320 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases.size(); ++i) {
5321 PrintXmlTestCase(stream, *test_cases[i]);
5322 }
5323 *stream << "</" << kTestsuites << ">\n";
5324}
5325
5326// Produces a string representing the test properties in a result as space
5327// delimited XML attributes based on the property key="value" pairs.
5328std::string XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::TestPropertiesAsXmlAttributes(
5329 const TestResult& result) {
5330 Message attributes;
5331 for (int i = 0; i < result.test_property_count(); ++i) {
5332 const TestProperty& property = result.GetTestProperty(i);
5333 attributes << " " << property.key() << "="
5334 << "\"" << EscapeXmlAttribute(property.value()) << "\"";
5335 }
5336 return attributes.GetString();
5337}
5338
5339void XmlUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputXmlTestProperties(
5340 std::ostream* stream, const TestResult& result) {
5341 const std::string kProperties = "properties";
5342 const std::string kProperty = "property";
5343
5344 if (result.test_property_count() <= 0) {
5345 return;
5346 }
5347
5348 *stream << "<" << kProperties << ">\n";
5349 for (int i = 0; i < result.test_property_count(); ++i) {
5350 const TestProperty& property = result.GetTestProperty(i);
5351 *stream << "<" << kProperty;
5352 *stream << " name=\"" << EscapeXmlAttribute(property.key()) << "\"";
5353 *stream << " value=\"" << EscapeXmlAttribute(property.value()) << "\"";
5354 *stream << "/>\n";
5355 }
5356 *stream << "</" << kProperties << ">\n";
5357}
5358
5359// End XmlUnitTestResultPrinter

5361// This class generates an JSON output file.
5362class JsonUnitTestResultPrinter : public EmptyTestEventListener {
5363 public:
5364 explicit JsonUnitTestResultPrinter(const char* output_file);
5365
5366 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test, int iteration);
5367
5368 // Prints an JSON summary of all unit tests.
5369 static void PrintJsonTestList(::std::ostream* stream,
5370 const std::vector<TestCase*>& test_cases);
5371
5372 private:
5373 // Returns an JSON-escaped copy of the input string str.
5374 static std::string EscapeJson(const std::string& str);
5375
5378 static void OutputJsonKey(std::ostream* stream,
5379 const std::string& element_name,
5380 const std::string& name,
5381 const std::string& value,
5382 const std::string& indent,
5383 bool comma = true);
5384 static void OutputJsonKey(std::ostream* stream,
5385 const std::string& element_name,
5386 const std::string& name,
5387 int value,
5388 const std::string& indent,
5389 bool comma = true);
5390
5391 // Streams a JSON representation of a TestInfo object.
5392 static void OutputJsonTestInfo(::std::ostream* stream,
5393 const char* test_case_name,
5394 const TestInfo& test_info);
5395
5396 // Prints a JSON representation of a TestCase object
5397 static void PrintJsonTestCase(::std::ostream* stream,
5398 const TestCase& test_case);
5399
5400 // Prints a JSON summary of unit_test to output stream out.
5401 static void PrintJsonUnitTest(::std::ostream* stream,
5402 const UnitTest& unit_test);
5403
5404 // Produces a string representing the test properties in a result as
5405 // a JSON dictionary.
5406 static std::string TestPropertiesAsJson(const TestResult& result,
5407 const std::string& indent);
5408
5409 // The output file.
5410 const std::string output_file_;
5411
5412 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(JsonUnitTestResultPrinter);
5413};

5431
5432// Returns an JSON-escaped copy of the input string str.
5433std::string JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::EscapeJson(const std::string& str) {
5434 Message m;
5435
5436 for (size_t i = 0; i < str.size(); ++i) {
5437 const char ch = str[i];
5438 switch (ch) {
5439 case '\\':
5440 case '"':
5441 case '/':
5442 m << '\\' << ch;
5443 break;
5444 case '\b':
5445 m << "\\b";
5446 break;
5447 case '\t':
5448 m << "\\t";
5449 break;
5450 case '\n':
5451 m << "\\n";
5452 break;
5453 case '\f':
5454 m << "\\f";
5455 break;
5456 case '\r':
5457 m << "\\r";
5458 break;
5459 default:
5460 if (ch < ' ') {
5461 m << "\\u00" << String::FormatByte(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch));
5462 } else {
5463 m << ch;
5464 }
5465 break;
5466 }
5467 }
5468
5469 return m.GetString();
5470}

5472// The following routines generate an JSON representation of a UnitTest
5473// object.
5474
5475// Formats the given time in milliseconds as seconds.
5476static std::string FormatTimeInMillisAsDuration(TimeInMillis ms) {
5477 ::std::stringstream ss;
5478 ss << (static_cast<double>(ms) * 1e-3) << "s";
5479 return ss.str();
5480}
5481
5482// Converts the given epoch time in milliseconds to a date string in the
5483// RFC3339 format, without the timezone information.
5484static std::string FormatEpochTimeInMillisAsRFC3339(TimeInMillis ms) {
5485 struct tm time_struct;
5486 if (!PortableLocaltime(static_cast<time_t>(ms / 1000), &time_struct))
5487 return "";
5488 // YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
5489 return StreamableToString(time_struct.tm_year + 1900) + "-" +
5490 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_mon + 1) + "-" +
5491 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_mday) + "T" +
5492 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_hour) + ":" +
5493 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_min) + ":" +
5494 String::FormatIntWidth2(time_struct.tm_sec) + "Z";
5495}

5497static inline std::string Indent(int width) {
5498 return std::string(width, ' ');
5499}

5501void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputJsonKey(
5502 std::ostream* stream,
5503 const std::string& element_name,
5504 const std::string& name,
5505 const std::string& value,
5506 const std::string& indent,
5507 bool comma) {
5508 const std::vector<std::string>& allowed_names =
5509 GetReservedAttributesForElement(element_name);
5510
5511 GTEST_CHECK_(std::find(allowed_names.begin(), allowed_names.end(), name) !=
5512 allowed_names.end())
5513 << "Key \"" << name << "\" is not allowed for value \"" << element_name
5514 << "\".";
5515
5516 *stream << indent << "\"" << name << "\": \"" << EscapeJson(value) << "\"";
5517 if (comma)
5518 *stream << ",\n";
5519}

5521void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputJsonKey(
5522 std::ostream* stream,
5523 const std::string& element_name,
5524 const std::string& name,
5525 int value,
5526 const std::string& indent,
5527 bool comma) {
5528 const std::vector<std::string>& allowed_names =
5529 GetReservedAttributesForElement(element_name);
5530
5531 GTEST_CHECK_(std::find(allowed_names.begin(), allowed_names.end(), name) !=
5532 allowed_names.end())
5533 << "Key \"" << name << "\" is not allowed for value \"" << element_name
5534 << "\".";
5535

5541// Prints a JSON representation of a TestInfo object.
5542void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::OutputJsonTestInfo(::std::ostream* stream,
5543 const char* test_case_name,
5544 const TestInfo& test_info) {
5545 const TestResult& result = *test_info.result();
5546 const std::string kTestcase = "testcase";
5547 const std::string kIndent = Indent(10);
5548
5549 *stream << Indent(8) << "{\n";
5550 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "name", test_info.name(), kIndent);
5551
5552 if (test_info.value_param() != NULL) {
5553 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "value_param",
5554 test_info.value_param(), kIndent);
5555 }
5556 if (test_info.type_param() != NULL) {
5557 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "type_param", test_info.type_param(),
5558 kIndent);
5559 }
5560 if (GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) {
5561 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "file", test_info.file(), kIndent);
5562 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "line", test_info.line(), kIndent, false);
5563 *stream << "\n" << Indent(8) << "}";
5564 return;
5565 }
5566
5567 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "status",
5568 test_info.should_run() ? "RUN" : "NOTRUN", kIndent);
5569 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "time",
5570 FormatTimeInMillisAsDuration(result.elapsed_time()), kIndent);
5571 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestcase, "classname", test_case_name, kIndent, false);
5572 *stream << TestPropertiesAsJson(result, kIndent);
5573
5574 int failures = 0;
5575 for (int i = 0; i < result.total_part_count(); ++i) {
5576 const TestPartResult& part = result.GetTestPartResult(i);
5577 if (part.failed()) {
5578 *stream << ",\n";
5579 if (++failures == 1) {
5580 *stream << kIndent << "\"" << "failures" << "\": [\n";
5581 }
5582 const std::string location =
5583 internal::FormatCompilerIndependentFileLocation(part.file_name(),
5584 part.line_number());
5585 const std::string message = EscapeJson(location + "\n" + part.message());
5586 *stream << kIndent << " {\n"
5587 << kIndent << " \"failure\": \"" << message << "\",\n"
5588 << kIndent << " \"type\": \"\"\n"
5589 << kIndent << " }";
5590 }
5591 }
5592
5593 if (failures > 0)
5594 *stream << "\n" << kIndent << "]";
5595 *stream << "\n" << Indent(8) << "}";
5596}
5597
5598// Prints an JSON representation of a TestCase object
5599void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintJsonTestCase(std::ostream* stream,
5600 const TestCase& test_case) {
5601 const std::string kTestsuite = "testsuite";
5602 const std::string kIndent = Indent(6);
5603
5604 *stream << Indent(4) << "{\n";
5605 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "name", test_case.name(), kIndent);
5606 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "tests", test_case.reportable_test_count(),
5607 kIndent);
5608 if (!GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) {
5609 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "failures", test_case.failed_test_count(),
5610 kIndent);
5611 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "disabled",
5612 test_case.reportable_disabled_test_count(), kIndent);
5613 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "errors", 0, kIndent);
5614 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuite, "time",
5615 FormatTimeInMillisAsDuration(test_case.elapsed_time()),
5616 kIndent, false);
5617 *stream << TestPropertiesAsJson(test_case.ad_hoc_test_result(), kIndent)
5618 << ",\n";
5619 }
5620
5621 *stream << kIndent << "\"" << kTestsuite << "\": [\n";
5622
5623 bool comma = false;
5624 for (int i = 0; i < test_case.total_test_count(); ++i) {
5625 if (test_case.GetTestInfo(i)->is_reportable()) {
5626 if (comma) {
5627 *stream << ",\n";
5628 } else {
5629 comma = true;
5630 }
5631 OutputJsonTestInfo(stream, test_case.name(), *test_case.GetTestInfo(i));
5632 }
5633 }
5634 *stream << "\n" << kIndent << "]\n" << Indent(4) << "}";
5635}
5636
5637// Prints a JSON summary of unit_test to output stream out.
5638void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintJsonUnitTest(std::ostream* stream,
5639 const UnitTest& unit_test) {
5640 const std::string kTestsuites = "testsuites";
5641 const std::string kIndent = Indent(2);
5642 *stream << "{\n";
5643
5644 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "tests", unit_test.reportable_test_count(),
5645 kIndent);
5646 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "failures", unit_test.failed_test_count(),
5647 kIndent);
5648 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "disabled",
5649 unit_test.reportable_disabled_test_count(), kIndent);
5650 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "errors", 0, kIndent);
5651 if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) {
5652 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "random_seed", unit_test.random_seed(),
5653 kIndent);
5654 }
5655 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "timestamp",
5656 FormatEpochTimeInMillisAsRFC3339(unit_test.start_timestamp()),
5657 kIndent);
5658 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "time",
5659 FormatTimeInMillisAsDuration(unit_test.elapsed_time()), kIndent,
5660 false);
5661
5662 *stream << TestPropertiesAsJson(unit_test.ad_hoc_test_result(), kIndent)
5663 << ",\n";
5664
5665 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "name", "AllTests", kIndent);
5666 *stream << kIndent << "\"" << kTestsuites << "\": [\n";
5667
5668 bool comma = false;
5669 for (int i = 0; i < unit_test.total_test_case_count(); ++i) {
5670 if (unit_test.GetTestCase(i)->reportable_test_count() > 0) {
5671 if (comma) {
5672 *stream << ",\n";
5673 } else {
5674 comma = true;
5675 }
5676 PrintJsonTestCase(stream, *unit_test.GetTestCase(i));
5677 }
5678 }
5679
5680 *stream << "\n" << kIndent << "]\n" << "}\n";
5681}
5682
5683void JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::PrintJsonTestList(
5684 std::ostream* stream, const std::vector<TestCase*>& test_cases) {
5685 const std::string kTestsuites = "testsuites";
5686 const std::string kIndent = Indent(2);
5687 *stream << "{\n";
5688 int total_tests = 0;
5689 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases.size(); ++i) {
5690 total_tests += test_cases[i]->total_test_count();
5691 }
5692 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "tests", total_tests, kIndent);
5693
5694 OutputJsonKey(stream, kTestsuites, "name", "AllTests", kIndent);
5695 *stream << kIndent << "\"" << kTestsuites << "\": [\n";
5696
5697 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases.size(); ++i) {
5698 if (i != 0) {
5699 *stream << ",\n";
5700 }
5701 PrintJsonTestCase(stream, *test_cases[i]);
5702 }
5703
5704 *stream << "\n"
5705 << kIndent << "]\n"
5706 << "}\n";
5707}
5708// Produces a string representing the test properties in a result as
5709// a JSON dictionary.
5710std::string JsonUnitTestResultPrinter::TestPropertiesAsJson(
5711 const TestResult& result, const std::string& indent) {
5712 Message attributes;
5713 for (int i = 0; i < result.test_property_count(); ++i) {
5714 const TestProperty& property = result.GetTestProperty(i);
5715 attributes << ",\n" << indent << "\"" << property.key() << "\": "
5716 << "\"" << EscapeJson(property.value()) << "\"";
5717 }
5718 return attributes.GetString();
5719}
5720
5721// End JsonUnitTestResultPrinter
5722
5723#if GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
5724
5725// Checks if str contains '=', '&', '%' or '\n' characters. If yes,
5726// replaces them by "%xx" where xx is their hexadecimal value. For
5727// example, replaces "=" with "%3D". This algorithm is O(strlen(str))
5728// in both time and space -- important as the input str may contain an
5729// arbitrarily long test failure message and stack trace.
5730std::string StreamingListener::UrlEncode(const char* str) {
5731 std::string result;
5732 result.reserve(strlen(str) + 1);
5733 for (char ch = *str; ch != '\0'; ch = *++str) {
5734 switch (ch) {
5735 case '%':
5736 case '=':
5737 case '&':
5738 case '\n':
5739 result.append("%" + String::FormatByte(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
5740 break;
5741 default:
5742 result.push_back(ch);
5743 break;
5744 }
5745 }
5746 return result;
5747}
5748
5749void StreamingListener::SocketWriter::MakeConnection() {
5750 GTEST_CHECK_(sockfd_ == -1)
5751 << "MakeConnection() can't be called when there is already a connection.";
5752
5753 addrinfo hints;
5754 memset(&hints, 0, sizeof(hints));
5755 hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC; // To allow both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
5756 hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
5757 addrinfo* servinfo = NULL;
5758
5759 // Use the getaddrinfo() to get a linked list of IP addresses for
5760 // the given host name.
5761 const int error_num = getaddrinfo(
5762 host_name_.c_str(), port_num_.c_str(), &hints, &servinfo);
5763 if (error_num != 0) {
5764 GTEST_LOG_(WARNING) << "stream_result_to: getaddrinfo() failed: "
5765 << gai_strerror(error_num);
5766 }
5767
5768 // Loop through all the results and connect to the first we can.
5769 for (addrinfo* cur_addr = servinfo; sockfd_ == -1 && cur_addr != NULL;
5770 cur_addr = cur_addr->ai_next) {
5771 sockfd_ = socket(
5772 cur_addr->ai_family, cur_addr->ai_socktype, cur_addr->ai_protocol);
5773 if (sockfd_ != -1) {
5774 // Connect the client socket to the server socket.
5775 if (connect(sockfd_, cur_addr->ai_addr, cur_addr->ai_addrlen) == -1) {
5776 close(sockfd_);
5777 sockfd_ = -1;
5778 }
5779 }
5780 }
5781
5782 freeaddrinfo(servinfo); // all done with this structure
5783
5784 if (sockfd_ == -1) {
5785 GTEST_LOG_(WARNING) << "stream_result_to: failed to connect to "
5786 << host_name_ << ":" << port_num_;
5787 }
5788}
5789
5790// End of class Streaming Listener
5791#endif // GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS__
5792
5793// class OsStackTraceGetter
5794
5795const char* const OsStackTraceGetterInterface::kElidedFramesMarker =
5796 "... " GTEST_NAME_ " internal frames ...";
5797
5798std::string OsStackTraceGetter::CurrentStackTrace(int max_depth, int skip_count)
5799 GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(mutex_) {
5800#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5801 std::string result;
5802
5803 if (max_depth <= 0) {
5804 return result;
5805 }
5806
5807 max_depth = std::min(max_depth, kMaxStackTraceDepth);
5808
5809 std::vector<void*> raw_stack(max_depth);
5810 // Skips the frames requested by the caller, plus this function.
5811 const int raw_stack_size =
5812 absl::GetStackTrace(&raw_stack[0], max_depth, skip_count + 1);
5813
5814 void* caller_frame = nullptr;
5815 {
5816 MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
5817 caller_frame = caller_frame_;
5818 }
5819
5820 for (int i = 0; i < raw_stack_size; ++i) {
5821 if (raw_stack[i] == caller_frame &&
5822 !GTEST_FLAG(show_internal_stack_frames)) {
5823 // Add a marker to the trace and stop adding frames.
5824 absl::StrAppend(&result, kElidedFramesMarker, "\n");
5825 break;
5826 }
5827
5828 char tmp[1024];
5829 const char* symbol = "(unknown)";
5830 if (absl::Symbolize(raw_stack[i], tmp, sizeof(tmp))) {
5831 symbol = tmp;
5832 }
5833
5834 char line[1024];
5835 snprintf(line, sizeof(line), " %p: %s\n", raw_stack[i], symbol);
5836 result += line;
5837 }
5838
5839 return result;
5840
5841#else // !GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5842 static_cast<void>(max_depth);
5843 static_cast<void>(skip_count);
5844 return "";
5845#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5846}
5847
5848void OsStackTraceGetter::UponLeavingGTest() GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(mutex_) {
5849#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5850 void* caller_frame = nullptr;
5851 if (absl::GetStackTrace(&caller_frame, 1, 3) <= 0) {
5852 caller_frame = nullptr;
5853 }
5854
5855 MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
5856 caller_frame_ = caller_frame;
5857#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
5858}
5859
5860// A helper class that creates the premature-exit file in its
5861// constructor and deletes the file in its destructor.
5862class ScopedPrematureExitFile {
5863 public:
5864 explicit ScopedPrematureExitFile(const char* premature_exit_filepath)
5865 : premature_exit_filepath_(premature_exit_filepath ?
5866 premature_exit_filepath : "") {
5867 // If a path to the premature-exit file is specified...
5868 if (!premature_exit_filepath_.empty()) {
5869 // create the file with a single "0" character in it. I/O
5870 // errors are ignored as there's nothing better we can do and we
5871 // don't want to fail the test because of this.
5872 FILE* pfile = posix::FOpen(premature_exit_filepath, "w");
5873 fwrite("0", 1, 1, pfile);
5874 fclose(pfile);
5875 }
5876 }
5877
5878 ~ScopedPrematureExitFile() {
5879 if (!premature_exit_filepath_.empty()) {
5880 int retval = remove(premature_exit_filepath_.c_str());
5881 if (retval) {
5882 GTEST_LOG_(ERROR) << "Failed to remove premature exit filepath \""
5883 << premature_exit_filepath_ << "\" with error "
5884 << retval;
5885 }
5886 }
5887 }
5888
5889 private:
5890 const std::string premature_exit_filepath_;
5891
5892 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ScopedPrematureExitFile);
5893};

5974// Gets the singleton UnitTest object. The first time this method is
5975// called, a UnitTest object is constructed and returned. Consecutive
5976// calls will return the same object.
5977//
5978// We don't protect this under mutex_ as a user is not supposed to
5979// call this before main() starts, from which point on the return
5980// value will never change.
5981UnitTest* UnitTest::GetInstance() {
5982 // When compiled with MSVC 7.1 in optimized mode, destroying the
5983 // UnitTest object upon exiting the program messes up the exit code,
5984 // causing successful tests to appear failed. We have to use a
5985 // different implementation in this case to bypass the compiler bug.
5986 // This implementation makes the compiler happy, at the cost of
5987 // leaking the UnitTest object.
5988
5989 // CodeGear C++Builder insists on a public destructor for the
5990 // default implementation. Use this implementation to keep good OO
5991 // design with private destructor.
5992
5993#if (defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER == 1310 && !defined(_DEBUG)) || defined(__BORLANDC__)
5994 static UnitTest* const instance = new UnitTest;
5995 return instance;
5996#else
5997 static UnitTest instance;
5998 return &instance;
5999#endif // (defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER == 1310 && !defined(_DEBUG)) || defined(__BORLANDC__)
6000}

6113// Adds a TestPartResult to the current TestResult object. All Google Test
6114// assertion macros (e.g. ASSERT_TRUE, EXPECT_EQ, etc) eventually call
6115// this to report their results. The user code should use the
6116// assertion macros instead of calling this directly.
6117void UnitTest::AddTestPartResult(
6118 TestPartResult::Type result_type,
6119 const char* file_name,
6120 int line_number,
6121 const std::string& message,
6122 const std::string& os_stack_trace) GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(mutex_) {
6123 Message msg;
6124 msg << message;
6125
6126 internal::MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
6127 if (impl_->gtest_trace_stack().size() > 0) {
6128 msg << "\n" << GTEST_NAME_ << " trace:";
6129
6130 for (int i = static_cast<int>(impl_->gtest_trace_stack().size());
6131 i > 0; --i) {
6132 const internal::TraceInfo& trace = impl_->gtest_trace_stack()[i - 1];
6133 msg << "\n" << internal::FormatFileLocation(trace.file, trace.line)
6134 << " " << trace.message;
6135 }
6136 }
6137
6138 if (os_stack_trace.c_str() != NULL && !os_stack_trace.empty()) {
6139 msg << internal::kStackTraceMarker << os_stack_trace;
6140 }
6141
6142 const TestPartResult result =
6143 TestPartResult(result_type, file_name, line_number,
6144 msg.GetString().c_str());
6145 impl_->GetTestPartResultReporterForCurrentThread()->
6146 ReportTestPartResult(result);
6147
6148 if (result_type != TestPartResult::kSuccess) {
6149 // gtest_break_on_failure takes precedence over
6150 // gtest_throw_on_failure. This allows a user to set the latter
6151 // in the code (perhaps in order to use Google Test assertions
6152 // with another testing framework) and specify the former on the
6153 // command line for debugging.
6154 if (GTEST_FLAG(break_on_failure)) {
6155#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
6156 // Using DebugBreak on Windows allows gtest to still break into a debugger
6157 // when a failure happens and both the --gtest_break_on_failure and
6158 // the --gtest_catch_exceptions flags are specified.
6159 DebugBreak();
6160#elif (!defined(__native_client__)) && \
6161 ((defined(__clang__) || defined(__GNUC__)) && \
6162 (defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)))
6163 // with clang/gcc we can achieve the same effect on x86 by invoking int3
6164 asm("int3");
6165#else
6166 // Dereference NULL through a volatile pointer to prevent the compiler
6167 // from removing. We use this rather than abort() or __builtin_trap() for
6168 // portability: Symbian doesn't implement abort() well, and some debuggers
6169 // don't correctly trap abort().
6170 *static_cast<volatile int*>(NULL) = 1;
6171#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
6172 } else if (GTEST_FLAG(throw_on_failure)) {
6173#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
6174 throw internal::GoogleTestFailureException(result);
6175#else
6176 // We cannot call abort() as it generates a pop-up in debug mode
6177 // that cannot be suppressed in VC 7.1 or below.
6178 exit(1);
6179#endif
6180 }
6181 }
6182}
6183
6184// Adds a TestProperty to the current TestResult object when invoked from
6185// inside a test, to current TestCase's ad_hoc_test_result_ when invoked
6186// from SetUpTestCase or TearDownTestCase, or to the global property set
6187// when invoked elsewhere. If the result already contains a property with
6188// the same key, the value will be updated.
6189void UnitTest::RecordProperty(const std::string& key,
6190 const std::string& value) {
6191 impl_->RecordProperty(TestProperty(key, value));
6192}
6193
6194// Runs all tests in this UnitTest object and prints the result.
6195// Returns 0 if successful, or 1 otherwise.
6196//
6197// We don't protect this under mutex_, as we only support calling it
6198// from the main thread.
6199int UnitTest::Run() {
6200 const bool in_death_test_child_process =
6201 internal::GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test).length() > 0;
6202
6203 // Google Test implements this protocol for catching that a test
6204 // program exits before returning control to Google Test:
6205 //
6206 // 1. Upon start, Google Test creates a file whose absolute path
6207 // is specified by the environment variable
6208 // TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE.
6209 // 2. When Google Test has finished its work, it deletes the file.
6210 //
6211 // This allows a test runner to set TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE before
6212 // running a Google-Test-based test program and check the existence
6213 // of the file at the end of the test execution to see if it has
6214 // exited prematurely.
6215
6216 // If we are in the child process of a death test, don't
6217 // create/delete the premature exit file, as doing so is unnecessary
6218 // and will confuse the parent process. Otherwise, create/delete
6219 // the file upon entering/leaving this function. If the program
6220 // somehow exits before this function has a chance to return, the
6221 // premature-exit file will be left undeleted, causing a test runner
6222 // that understands the premature-exit-file protocol to report the
6223 // test as having failed.
6224 const internal::ScopedPrematureExitFile premature_exit_file(
6225 in_death_test_child_process ?
6226 NULL : internal::posix::GetEnv("TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE"));
6227
6228 // Captures the value of GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions). This value will be
6229 // used for the duration of the program.
6230 impl()->set_catch_exceptions(GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions));
6231
6232#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
6233 // Either the user wants Google Test to catch exceptions thrown by the
6234 // tests or this is executing in the context of death test child
6235 // process. In either case the user does not want to see pop-up dialogs
6236 // about crashes - they are expected.
6237 if (impl()->catch_exceptions() || in_death_test_child_process) {
6238# if !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
6239 // SetErrorMode doesn't exist on CE.
6240 SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOALIGNMENTFAULTEXCEPT |
6241 SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX | SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX);
6242# endif // !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
6243
6244# if (defined(_MSC_VER) || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW) && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
6245 // Death test children can be terminated with _abort(). On Windows,
6246 // _abort() can show a dialog with a warning message. This forces the
6247 // abort message to go to stderr instead.
6248 _set_error_mode(_OUT_TO_STDERR);
6249# endif
6250
6251# if _MSC_VER >= 1400 && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
6252 // In the debug version, Visual Studio pops up a separate dialog
6253 // offering a choice to debug the aborted program. We need to suppress
6254 // this dialog or it will pop up for every EXPECT/ASSERT_DEATH statement
6255 // executed. Google Test will notify the user of any unexpected
6256 // failure via stderr.
6257 //
6258 // VC++ doesn't define _set_abort_behavior() prior to the version 8.0.
6259 // Users of prior VC versions shall suffer the agony and pain of
6260 // clicking through the countless debug dialogs.
6261 // FIXME: find a way to suppress the abort dialog() in the
6262 // debug mode when compiled with VC 7.1 or lower.
6263 if (!GTEST_FLAG(break_on_failure))
6264 _set_abort_behavior(
6265 0x0, // Clear the following flags:
6266 _WRITE_ABORT_MSG | _CALL_REPORTFAULT); // pop-up window, core dump.
6267# endif
6268 }
6269#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
6270
6271 return internal::HandleExceptionsInMethodIfSupported(
6272 impl(),
6273 &internal::UnitTestImpl::RunAllTests,
6274 "auxiliary test code (environments or event listeners)") ? 0 : 1;
6275}

6377// Adds a TestProperty to the current TestResult object when invoked in a
6378// context of a test, to current test case's ad_hoc_test_result when invoke

6380// otherwise. If the result already contains a property with the same key,

6382void UnitTestImpl::RecordProperty(const TestProperty& test_property) {

6387 xml_element = "testcase";
6388 test_result = &(current_test_info_->result_);
6389 } else if (current_test_case_ != NULL) {

6442// Performs initialization dependent upon flag values obtained in
6443// ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly. Is called from InitGoogleTest after the call to
6444// ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly. In case a user neglects to call InitGoogleTest
6445// this function is also called from RunAllTests. Since this function can be
6446// called more than once, it has to be idempotent.
6447void UnitTestImpl::PostFlagParsingInit() {
6448 // Ensures that this function does not execute more than once.
6449 if (!post_flag_parse_init_performed_) {
6450 post_flag_parse_init_performed_ = true;
6451
6452#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_)
6453 // Register to send notifications about key process state changes.
6454 listeners()->Append(new GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_());
6455#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_TEST_EVENT_LISTENER_)
6456
6457#if GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
6458 InitDeathTestSubprocessControlInfo();
6459 SuppressTestEventsIfInSubprocess();
6460#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
6461
6462 // Registers parameterized tests. This makes parameterized tests
6463 // available to the UnitTest reflection API without running
6464 // RUN_ALL_TESTS.
6465 RegisterParameterizedTests();
6466
6467 // Configures listeners for XML output. This makes it possible for users
6468 // to shut down the default XML output before invoking RUN_ALL_TESTS.
6469 ConfigureXmlOutput();
6470
6471#if GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
6472 // Configures listeners for streaming test results to the specified server.
6473 ConfigureStreamingOutput();
6474#endif // GTEST_CAN_STREAM_RESULTS_
6475
6476#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
6477 if (GTEST_FLAG(install_failure_signal_handler)) {
6478 absl::FailureSignalHandlerOptions options;
6479 absl::InstallFailureSignalHandler(options);
6480 }
6481#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
6482 }
