6485// A predicate that checks the name of a TestCase against a known
6486// value.
6487//
6488// This is used for implementation of the UnitTest class only. We put
6489// it in the anonymous namespace to prevent polluting the outer
6490// namespace.
6491//
6492// TestCaseNameIs is copyable.
6493class TestCaseNameIs {
6494 public:
6495 // Constructor.
6496 explicit TestCaseNameIs(const std::string& name)
6497 : name_(name) {}
6498
6499 // Returns true iff the name of test_case matches name_.
6500 bool operator()(const TestCase* test_case) const {
6501 return test_case != NULL && strcmp(test_case->name(), name_.c_str()) == 0;
6502 }
6503
6504 private:
6505 std::string name_;
6506};
6507
6508// Finds and returns a TestCase with the given name. If one doesn't
6509// exist, creates one and returns it. It's the CALLER'S
6510// RESPONSIBILITY to ensure that this function is only called WHEN THE
6511// TESTS ARE NOT SHUFFLED.
6512//
6513// Arguments:
6514//
6515// test_case_name: name of the test case
6516// type_param: the name of the test case's type parameter, or NULL if
6517// this is not a typed or a type-parameterized test case.
6518// set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test case
6519// tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test case
6520TestCase* UnitTestImpl::GetTestCase(const char* test_case_name,
6521 const char* type_param,
6522 Test::SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc,
6523 Test::TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc) {
6524 // Can we find a TestCase with the given name?
6525 const std::vector<TestCase*>::const_reverse_iterator test_case =
6526 std::find_if(test_cases_.rbegin(), test_cases_.rend(),
6527 TestCaseNameIs(test_case_name));
6528
6529 if (test_case != test_cases_.rend())
6530 return *test_case;
6531
6532 // No. Let's create one.
6533 TestCase* const new_test_case =
6534 new TestCase(test_case_name, type_param, set_up_tc, tear_down_tc);
6535
6536 // Is this a death test case?
6537 if (internal::UnitTestOptions::MatchesFilter(test_case_name,
6538 kDeathTestCaseFilter)) {
6539 // Yes. Inserts the test case after the last death test case
6540 // defined so far. This only works when the test cases haven't
6541 // been shuffled. Otherwise we may end up running a death test
6542 // after a non-death test.
6543 ++last_death_test_case_;
6544 test_cases_.insert(test_cases_.begin() + last_death_test_case_,
6545 new_test_case);
6546 } else {
6547 // No. Appends to the end of the list.
6548 test_cases_.push_back(new_test_case);
6549 }
6550
6551 test_case_indices_.push_back(static_cast<int>(test_case_indices_.size()));
6552 return new_test_case;
6553}
6554
6555// Helpers for setting up / tearing down the given environment. They
6556// are for use in the ForEach() function.
6557static void SetUpEnvironment(Environment* env) { env->SetUp(); }
6558static void TearDownEnvironment(Environment* env) { env->TearDown(); }
6559
6560// Runs all tests in this UnitTest object, prints the result, and
6561// returns true if all tests are successful. If any exception is
6562// thrown during a test, the test is considered to be failed, but the
6563// rest of the tests will still be run.
6564//
6565// When parameterized tests are enabled, it expands and registers
6566// parameterized tests first in RegisterParameterizedTests().
6567// All other functions called from RunAllTests() may safely assume that
6568// parameterized tests are ready to be counted and run.
6569bool UnitTestImpl::RunAllTests() {
6570 // True iff Google Test is initialized before RUN_ALL_TESTS() is called.
6571 const bool gtest_is_initialized_before_run_all_tests = GTestIsInitialized();
6572
6573 // Do not run any test if the --help flag was specified.
6574 if (g_help_flag)
6575 return true;
6576
6577 // Repeats the call to the post-flag parsing initialization in case the
6578 // user didn't call InitGoogleTest.
6579 PostFlagParsingInit();
6580
6581 // Even if sharding is not on, test runners may want to use the
6582 // GTEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE to query whether the test supports the sharding
6583 // protocol.
6584 internal::WriteToShardStatusFileIfNeeded();
6585
6586 // True iff we are in a subprocess for running a thread-safe-style
6587 // death test.
6588 bool in_subprocess_for_death_test = false;
6589
6590#if GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
6591 in_subprocess_for_death_test = (internal_run_death_test_flag_.get() != NULL);
6592# if defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_)
6593 if (in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
6594 GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_();
6595 }
6596# endif // defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_CHILD_SETUP_)
6597#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
6598
6599 const bool should_shard = ShouldShard(kTestTotalShards, kTestShardIndex,
6600 in_subprocess_for_death_test);
6601
6602 // Compares the full test names with the filter to decide which
6603 // tests to run.
6604 const bool has_tests_to_run = FilterTests(should_shard
6605 ? HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL
6606 : IGNORE_SHARDING_PROTOCOL) > 0;
6607
6608 // Lists the tests and exits if the --gtest_list_tests flag was specified.
6609 if (GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) {
6610 // This must be called *after* FilterTests() has been called.
6611 ListTestsMatchingFilter();
6612 return true;
6613 }
6614
6615 random_seed_ = GTEST_FLAG(shuffle) ?
6616 GetRandomSeedFromFlag(GTEST_FLAG(random_seed)) : 0;
6617
6618 // True iff at least one test has failed.
6619 bool failed = false;
6620
6621 TestEventListener* repeater = listeners()->repeater();
6622
6623 start_timestamp_ = GetTimeInMillis();
6624 repeater->OnTestProgramStart(*parent_);
6625
6626 // How many times to repeat the tests? We don't want to repeat them
6627 // when we are inside the subprocess of a death test.
6628 const int repeat = in_subprocess_for_death_test ? 1 : GTEST_FLAG(repeat);
6629 // Repeats forever if the repeat count is negative.
6630 const bool forever = repeat < 0;
6631 for (int i = 0; forever || i != repeat; i++) {
6632 // We want to preserve failures generated by ad-hoc test
6633 // assertions executed before RUN_ALL_TESTS().
6634 ClearNonAdHocTestResult();
6635
6636 const TimeInMillis start = GetTimeInMillis();
6637
6638 // Shuffles test cases and tests if requested.
6639 if (has_tests_to_run && GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) {
6640 random()->Reseed(random_seed_);
6641 // This should be done before calling OnTestIterationStart(),
6642 // such that a test event listener can see the actual test order
6643 // in the event.
6644 ShuffleTests();
6645 }
6646
6647 // Tells the unit test event listeners that the tests are about to start.
6648 repeater->OnTestIterationStart(*parent_, i);
6649
6650 // Runs each test case if there is at least one test to run.
6651 if (has_tests_to_run) {
6652 // Sets up all environments beforehand.
6653 repeater->OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(*parent_);
6654 ForEach(environments_, SetUpEnvironment);
6655 repeater->OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(*parent_);
6656
6657 // Runs the tests only if there was no fatal failure during global
6658 // set-up.
6659 if (!Test::HasFatalFailure()) {
6660 for (int test_index = 0; test_index < total_test_case_count();
6661 test_index++) {
6662 GetMutableTestCase(test_index)->Run();
6663 }
6664 }
6665
6666 // Tears down all environments in reverse order afterwards.
6667 repeater->OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(*parent_);
6668 std::for_each(environments_.rbegin(), environments_.rend(),
6669 TearDownEnvironment);
6670 repeater->OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(*parent_);
6671 }
6672
6673 elapsed_time_ = GetTimeInMillis() - start;
6674
6675 // Tells the unit test event listener that the tests have just finished.
6676 repeater->OnTestIterationEnd(*parent_, i);
6677
6678 // Gets the result and clears it.
6679 if (!Passed()) {
6680 failed = true;
6681 }
6682
6683 // Restores the original test order after the iteration. This
6684 // allows the user to quickly repro a failure that happens in the
6685 // N-th iteration without repeating the first (N - 1) iterations.
6686 // This is not enclosed in "if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) { ... }", in
6687 // case the user somehow changes the value of the flag somewhere
6688 // (it's always safe to unshuffle the tests).
6689 UnshuffleTests();
6690
6691 if (GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) {
6692 // Picks a new random seed for each iteration.
6693 random_seed_ = GetNextRandomSeed(random_seed_);
6694 }
6695 }
6696
6697 repeater->OnTestProgramEnd(*parent_);
6698
6699 if (!gtest_is_initialized_before_run_all_tests) {
6700 ColoredPrintf(
6701 COLOR_RED,
6702 "\nIMPORTANT NOTICE - DO NOT IGNORE:\n"
6703 "This test program did NOT call " GTEST_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_NAME_
6704 "() before calling RUN_ALL_TESTS(). This is INVALID. Soon " GTEST_NAME_
6705 " will start to enforce the valid usage. "
6706 "Please fix it ASAP, or IT WILL START TO FAIL.\n"); // NOLINT
6707#if GTEST_FOR_GOOGLE_
6708 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED,
6709 "For more details, see http://wiki/Main/ValidGUnitMain.\n");
6710#endif // GTEST_FOR_GOOGLE_
6711 }
6712
6713 return !failed;
6714}
6715
6716// Reads the GTEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE environment variable, and creates the file
6717// if the variable is present. If a file already exists at this location, this
6718// function will write over it. If the variable is present, but the file cannot
6719// be created, prints an error and exits.
6720void WriteToShardStatusFileIfNeeded() {
6721 const char* const test_shard_file = posix::GetEnv(kTestShardStatusFile);
6722 if (test_shard_file != NULL) {
6723 FILE* const file = posix::FOpen(test_shard_file, "w");
6724 if (file == NULL) {
6725 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED,
6726 "Could not write to the test shard status file \"%s\" "
6727 "specified by the %s environment variable.\n",
6728 test_shard_file, kTestShardStatusFile);
6729 fflush(stdout);
6730 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6731 }
6732 fclose(file);
6733 }
6734}
6735
6736// Checks whether sharding is enabled by examining the relevant
6737// environment variable values. If the variables are present,
6738// but inconsistent (i.e., shard_index >= total_shards), prints
6739// an error and exits. If in_subprocess_for_death_test, sharding is
6740// disabled because it must only be applied to the original test
6741// process. Otherwise, we could filter out death tests we intended to execute.
6742bool ShouldShard(const char* total_shards_env,
6743 const char* shard_index_env,
6744 bool in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
6745 if (in_subprocess_for_death_test) {
6746 return false;
6747 }
6748
6749 const Int32 total_shards = Int32FromEnvOrDie(total_shards_env, -1);
6750 const Int32 shard_index = Int32FromEnvOrDie(shard_index_env, -1);
6751
6752 if (total_shards == -1 && shard_index == -1) {
6753 return false;
6754 } else if (total_shards == -1 && shard_index != -1) {
6755 const Message msg = Message()
6756 << "Invalid environment variables: you have "
6757 << kTestShardIndex << " = " << shard_index
6758 << ", but have left " << kTestTotalShards << " unset.\n";
6759 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, msg.GetString().c_str());
6760 fflush(stdout);
6761 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6762 } else if (total_shards != -1 && shard_index == -1) {
6763 const Message msg = Message()
6764 << "Invalid environment variables: you have "
6765 << kTestTotalShards << " = " << total_shards
6766 << ", but have left " << kTestShardIndex << " unset.\n";
6767 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, msg.GetString().c_str());
6768 fflush(stdout);
6769 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6770 } else if (shard_index < 0 || shard_index >= total_shards) {
6771 const Message msg = Message()
6772 << "Invalid environment variables: we require 0 <= "
6773 << kTestShardIndex << " < " << kTestTotalShards
6774 << ", but you have " << kTestShardIndex << "=" << shard_index
6775 << ", " << kTestTotalShards << "=" << total_shards << ".\n";
6776 ColoredPrintf(COLOR_RED, msg.GetString().c_str());
6777 fflush(stdout);
6778 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6779 }
6780
6781 return total_shards > 1;
6782}
6783
6784// Parses the environment variable var as an Int32. If it is unset,
6785// returns default_val. If it is not an Int32, prints an error
6786// and aborts.
6787Int32 Int32FromEnvOrDie(const char* var, Int32 default_val) {
6788 const char* str_val = posix::GetEnv(var);
6789 if (str_val == NULL) {
6790 return default_val;
6791 }
6792
6793 Int32 result;
6794 if (!ParseInt32(Message() << "The value of environment variable " << var,
6795 str_val, &result)) {
6796 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
6797 }
6798 return result;
6799}
6800
6801// Given the total number of shards, the shard index, and the test id,
6802// returns true iff the test should be run on this shard. The test id is
6803// some arbitrary but unique non-negative integer assigned to each test
6804// method. Assumes that 0 <= shard_index < total_shards.
6805bool ShouldRunTestOnShard(int total_shards, int shard_index, int test_id) {
6806 return (test_id % total_shards) == shard_index;
6807}
6808
6809// Compares the name of each test with the user-specified filter to
6810// decide whether the test should be run, then records the result in
6811// each TestCase and TestInfo object.
6812// If shard_tests == true, further filters tests based on sharding
6813// variables in the environment - see
6814// https://github.com/google/googletest/blob/master/googletest/docs/advanced.md
6815// . Returns the number of tests that should run.
6816int UnitTestImpl::FilterTests(ReactionToSharding shard_tests) {
6817 const Int32 total_shards = shard_tests == HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL ?
6818 Int32FromEnvOrDie(kTestTotalShards, -1) : -1;
6819 const Int32 shard_index = shard_tests == HONOR_SHARDING_PROTOCOL ?
6820 Int32FromEnvOrDie(kTestShardIndex, -1) : -1;
6821
6822 // num_runnable_tests are the number of tests that will
6823 // run across all shards (i.e., match filter and are not disabled).
6824 // num_selected_tests are the number of tests to be run on
6825 // this shard.
6826 int num_runnable_tests = 0;
6827 int num_selected_tests = 0;
6828 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases_.size(); i++) {
6829 TestCase* const test_case = test_cases_[i];
6830 const std::string &test_case_name = test_case->name();
6831 test_case->set_should_run(false);
6832
6833 for (size_t j = 0; j < test_case->test_info_list().size(); j++) {
6834 TestInfo* const test_info = test_case->test_info_list()[j];
6835 const std::string test_name(test_info->name());
6836 // A test is disabled if test case name or test name matches
6837 // kDisableTestFilter.
6838 const bool is_disabled =
6839 internal::UnitTestOptions::MatchesFilter(test_case_name,
6840 kDisableTestFilter) ||
6841 internal::UnitTestOptions::MatchesFilter(test_name,
6842 kDisableTestFilter);
6843 test_info->is_disabled_ = is_disabled;
6844
6845 const std::string value_param(test_info->value_param() == NULL ?
6846 "" : test_info->value_param());
6847
6848 const bool matches_filter =
6849 internal::UnitTestOptions::FilterMatchesTest(test_case_name,
6850 test_name) &&
6851 internal::UnitTestOptions::MatchesFilter(value_param,
6852 GTEST_FLAG(param_filter).c_str());
6853
6854 test_info->matches_filter_ = matches_filter;
6855
6856 const bool is_runnable =
6857 (GTEST_FLAG(also_run_disabled_tests) || !is_disabled) &&
6858 matches_filter;
6859
6860 const bool is_in_another_shard =
6861 shard_tests != IGNORE_SHARDING_PROTOCOL &&
6862 !ShouldRunTestOnShard(total_shards, shard_index, num_runnable_tests);
6863 test_info->is_in_another_shard_ = is_in_another_shard;
6864 const bool is_selected = is_runnable && !is_in_another_shard;
6865
6866 num_runnable_tests += is_runnable;
6867 num_selected_tests += is_selected;
6868
6869 test_info->should_run_ = is_selected;
6870 test_case->set_should_run(test_case->should_run() || is_selected);
6871 }
6872 }
6873 return num_selected_tests;
6874}
6875
6876// Prints the given C-string on a single line by replacing all '\n'
6877// characters with string "\\n". If the output takes more than
6878// max_length characters, only prints the first max_length characters
6879// and "...".
6880static void PrintOnOneLine(const char* str, int max_length) {
6881 if (str != NULL) {
6882 for (int i = 0; *str != '\0'; ++str) {
6883 if (i >= max_length) {
6884 printf("...");
6885 break;
6886 }
6887 if (*str == '\n') {
6888 printf("\\n");
6889 i += 2;
6890 } else {
6891 printf("%c", *str);
6892 ++i;
6893 }
6894 }
6895 }
6896}

6898// Prints the names of the tests matching the user-specified filter flag.
6899void UnitTestImpl::ListTestsMatchingFilter() {
6900 // Print at most this many characters for each type/value parameter.
6901 const int kMaxParamLength = 250;
6902
6903 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases_.size(); i++) {
6904 const TestCase* const test_case = test_cases_[i];
6905 bool printed_test_case_name = false;
6906
6907 for (size_t j = 0; j < test_case->test_info_list().size(); j++) {
6908 const TestInfo* const test_info =
6909 test_case->test_info_list()[j];
6910 if (test_info->matches_filter_) {
6911 if (!printed_test_case_name) {
6912 printed_test_case_name = true;
6913 printf("%s.", test_case->name());
6914 if (test_case->type_param() != NULL) {
6915 printf(" # %s = ", kTypeParamLabel);
6916 // We print the type parameter on a single line to make
6917 // the output easy to parse by a program.
6918 PrintOnOneLine(test_case->type_param(), kMaxParamLength);
6919 }
6920 printf("\n");
6921 }
6922 printf(" %s", test_info->name());
6923 if (test_info->value_param() != NULL) {
6924 printf(" # %s = ", kValueParamLabel);
6925 // We print the value parameter on a single line to make the
6926 // output easy to parse by a program.
6927 PrintOnOneLine(test_info->value_param(), kMaxParamLength);
6928 }
6929 printf("\n");
6930 }
6931 }
6932 }
6933 fflush(stdout);
6934 const std::string& output_format = UnitTestOptions::GetOutputFormat();
6935 if (output_format == "xml" || output_format == "json") {
6936 FILE* fileout = OpenFileForWriting(
6937 UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile().c_str());
6938 std::stringstream stream;
6939 if (output_format == "xml") {
6940 XmlUnitTestResultPrinter(
6941 UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile().c_str())
6942 .PrintXmlTestsList(&stream, test_cases_);
6943 } else if (output_format == "json") {
6944 JsonUnitTestResultPrinter(
6945 UnitTestOptions::GetAbsolutePathToOutputFile().c_str())
6946 .PrintJsonTestList(&stream, test_cases_);
6947 }
6948 fprintf(fileout, "%s", StringStreamToString(&stream).c_str());
6949 fclose(fileout);
6950 }
6951}

6992// Shuffles all test cases, and the tests within each test case,
6993// making sure that death tests are still run first.
6994void UnitTestImpl::ShuffleTests() {
6995 // Shuffles the death test cases.
6996 ShuffleRange(random(), 0, last_death_test_case_ + 1, &test_case_indices_);
6997
6998 // Shuffles the non-death test cases.
6999 ShuffleRange(random(), last_death_test_case_ + 1,
7000 static_cast<int>(test_cases_.size()), &test_case_indices_);
7001
7002 // Shuffles the tests inside each test case.
7003 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases_.size(); i++) {
7004 test_cases_[i]->ShuffleTests(random());
7005 }
7006}
7007
7008// Restores the test cases and tests to their order before the first shuffle.
7009void UnitTestImpl::UnshuffleTests() {
7010 for (size_t i = 0; i < test_cases_.size(); i++) {
7011 // Unshuffles the tests in each test case.
7012 test_cases_[i]->UnshuffleTests();
7013 // Resets the index of each test case.
7014 test_case_indices_[i] = static_cast<int>(i);
7015 }
7016}

7018// Returns the current OS stack trace as an std::string.
7019//
7020// The maximum number of stack frames to be included is specified by
7021// the gtest_stack_trace_depth flag. The skip_count parameter
7022// specifies the number of top frames to be skipped, which doesn't
7023// count against the number of frames to be included.
7024//
7025// For example, if Foo() calls Bar(), which in turn calls
7026// GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(..., 1), Foo() will be included in
7027// the trace but Bar() and GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop() won't.
7028std::string GetCurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(UnitTest* /*unit_test*/,
7029 int skip_count) {
7030 // We pass skip_count + 1 to skip this wrapper function in addition
7031 // to what the user really wants to skip.
7032 return GetUnitTestImpl()->CurrentOsStackTraceExceptTop(skip_count + 1);
7033}

7035// Used by the GTEST_SUPPRESS_UNREACHABLE_CODE_WARNING_BELOW_ macro to
7036// suppress unreachable code warnings.
7037namespace {
7038class ClassUniqueToAlwaysTrue {};
7039}
7040
7041bool IsTrue(bool condition) { return condition; }
7042
7043bool AlwaysTrue() {
7044#if GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
7045 // This condition is always false so AlwaysTrue() never actually throws,
7046 // but it makes the compiler think that it may throw.
7047 if (IsTrue(false))
7048 throw ClassUniqueToAlwaysTrue();
7049#endif // GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS
7050 return true;
7051}
7052
7053// If *pstr starts with the given prefix, modifies *pstr to be right
7054// past the prefix and returns true; otherwise leaves *pstr unchanged
7055// and returns false. None of pstr, *pstr, and prefix can be NULL.
7056bool SkipPrefix(const char* prefix, const char** pstr) {
7057 const size_t prefix_len = strlen(prefix);
7058 if (strncmp(*pstr, prefix, prefix_len) == 0) {
7059 *pstr += prefix_len;
7060 return true;
7061 }
7062 return false;
7063}
7064
7065// Parses a string as a command line flag. The string should have
7066// the format "--flag=value". When def_optional is true, the "=value"
7067// part can be omitted.
7068//
7069// Returns the value of the flag, or NULL if the parsing failed.
7070static const char* ParseFlagValue(const char* str, const char* flag,
7071 bool def_optional) {
7072 // str and flag must not be NULL.
7073 if (str == NULL || flag == NULL) return NULL;
7074
7075 // The flag must start with "--" followed by GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_.
7076 const std::string flag_str = std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + flag;
7077 const size_t flag_len = flag_str.length();
7078 if (strncmp(str, flag_str.c_str(), flag_len) != 0) return NULL;
7079
7080 // Skips the flag name.
7081 const char* flag_end = str + flag_len;
7082
7083 // When def_optional is true, it's OK to not have a "=value" part.
7084 if (def_optional && (flag_end[0] == '\0')) {
7085 return flag_end;
7086 }
7087
7088 // If def_optional is true and there are more characters after the
7089 // flag name, or if def_optional is false, there must be a '=' after
7090 // the flag name.
7091 if (flag_end[0] != '=') return NULL;
7092
7093 // Returns the string after "=".
7094 return flag_end + 1;
7095}
7096
7097// Parses a string for a bool flag, in the form of either
7098// "--flag=value" or "--flag".
7099//
7100// In the former case, the value is taken as true as long as it does
7101// not start with '0', 'f', or 'F'.
7102//
7103// In the latter case, the value is taken as true.
7104//
7105// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
7106// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
7107static bool ParseBoolFlag(const char* str, const char* flag, bool* value) {
7108 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
7109 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag, true);
7110
7111 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
7112 if (value_str == NULL) return false;
7113
7114 // Converts the string value to a bool.
7115 *value = !(*value_str == '0' || *value_str == 'f' || *value_str == 'F');
7116 return true;
7117}
7118
7119// Parses a string for an Int32 flag, in the form of
7120// "--flag=value".
7121//
7122// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
7123// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
7124bool ParseInt32Flag(const char* str, const char* flag, Int32* value) {
7125 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
7126 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag, false);
7127
7128 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
7129 if (value_str == NULL) return false;
7130
7131 // Sets *value to the value of the flag.
7132 return ParseInt32(Message() << "The value of flag --" << flag,
7133 value_str, value);
7134}
7135
7136// Parses a string for a string flag, in the form of
7137// "--flag=value".
7138//
7139// On success, stores the value of the flag in *value, and returns
7140// true. On failure, returns false without changing *value.
7141template <typename String>
7142static bool ParseStringFlag(const char* str, const char* flag, String* value) {
7143 // Gets the value of the flag as a string.
7144 const char* const value_str = ParseFlagValue(str, flag, false);
7145
7146 // Aborts if the parsing failed.
7147 if (value_str == NULL) return false;
7148
7149 // Sets *value to the value of the flag.
7150 *value = value_str;
7151 return true;
7152}
7153
7154// Determines whether a string has a prefix that Google Test uses for its
7155// flags, i.e., starts with GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ or GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_DASH_.
7156// If Google Test detects that a command line flag has its prefix but is not
7157// recognized, it will print its help message. Flags starting with
7158// GTEST_INTERNAL_PREFIX_ followed by "internal_" are considered Google Test
7159// internal flags and do not trigger the help message.
7160static bool HasGoogleTestFlagPrefix(const char* str) {
7161 return (SkipPrefix("--", &str) ||
7162 SkipPrefix("-", &str) ||
7163 SkipPrefix("/", &str)) &&
7164 !SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ "internal_", &str) &&
7165 (SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_, &str) ||
7166 SkipPrefix(GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_DASH_, &str));
7167}
7168
7169// Prints a string containing code-encoded text. The following escape
7170// sequences can be used in the string to control the text color:
7171//
7172// @@ prints a single '@' character.
7173// @R changes the color to red.
7174// @G changes the color to green.
7175// @Y changes the color to yellow.
7176// @D changes to the default terminal text color.
7177//
7178// FIXME: Write tests for this once we add stdout
7179// capturing to Google Test.
7180static void PrintColorEncoded(const char* str) {
7181 GTestColor color = COLOR_DEFAULT; // The current color.
7182
7183 // Conceptually, we split the string into segments divided by escape
7184 // sequences. Then we print one segment at a time. At the end of
7185 // each iteration, the str pointer advances to the beginning of the
7186 // next segment.
7187 for (;;) {
7188 const char* p = strchr(str, '@');
7189 if (p == NULL) {
7190 ColoredPrintf(color, "%s", str);
7191 return;
7192 }
7193
7194 ColoredPrintf(color, "%s", std::string(str, p).c_str());
7195
7196 const char ch = p[1];
7197 str = p + 2;
7198 if (ch == '@') {
7199 ColoredPrintf(color, "@");
7200 } else if (ch == 'D') {
7201 color = COLOR_DEFAULT;
7202 } else if (ch == 'R') {
7203 color = COLOR_RED;
7204 } else if (ch == 'G') {
7205 color = COLOR_GREEN;
7206 } else if (ch == 'Y') {
7207 color = COLOR_YELLOW;
7208 } else {
7209 --str;
7210 }
7211 }
7212}

7223 "[@G-@YNEGATIVE_PATTERNS]@D\n"
7224" Run only the tests whose name matches one of the positive patterns but\n"
7225" none of the negative patterns. '?' matches any single character; '*'\n"
7226" matches any substring; ':' separates two patterns.\n"

7239" @G--" GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ "shuffle@D\n"

7264" @G--" GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ "break_on_failure@D\n"

7285static bool ParseGoogleTestFlag(const char* const arg) {
7286 return ParseBoolFlag(arg, kAlsoRunDisabledTestsFlag,
7287 &GTEST_FLAG(also_run_disabled_tests)) ||
7288 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kBreakOnFailureFlag,
7289 &GTEST_FLAG(break_on_failure)) ||
7290 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kCatchExceptionsFlag,
7291 &GTEST_FLAG(catch_exceptions)) ||
7292 ParseStringFlag(arg, kColorFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(color)) ||
7293 ParseStringFlag(arg, kDeathTestStyleFlag,
7294 &GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style)) ||
7295 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kDeathTestUseFork,
7296 &GTEST_FLAG(death_test_use_fork)) ||
7297 ParseStringFlag(arg, kFilterFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(filter)) ||
7298 ParseStringFlag(arg, kParamFilterFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(param_filter)) ||
7299 ParseStringFlag(arg, kInternalRunDeathTestFlag,
7300 &GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test)) ||
7301 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kListTestsFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(list_tests)) ||
7302 ParseStringFlag(arg, kOutputFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(output)) ||
7303 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kPrintTimeFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(print_time)) ||
7304 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kPrintUTF8Flag, &GTEST_FLAG(print_utf8)) ||
7305 ParseInt32Flag(arg, kRandomSeedFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(random_seed)) ||
7306 ParseInt32Flag(arg, kRepeatFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(repeat)) ||
7307 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kShuffleFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(shuffle)) ||
7308 ParseInt32Flag(arg, kStackTraceDepthFlag,
7309 &GTEST_FLAG(stack_trace_depth)) ||
7310 ParseStringFlag(arg, kStreamResultToFlag,
7311 &GTEST_FLAG(stream_result_to)) ||
7312 ParseBoolFlag(arg, kThrowOnFailureFlag,
7313 &GTEST_FLAG(throw_on_failure));
7314}

7316#if GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_
7317static void LoadFlagsFromFile(const std::string& path) {
7318 FILE* flagfile = posix::FOpen(path.c_str(), "r");
7319 if (!flagfile) {
7320 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Unable to open file \"" << GTEST_FLAG(flagfile)
7321 << "\"";
7322 }
7323 std::string contents(ReadEntireFile(flagfile));
7324 posix::FClose(flagfile);
7325 std::vector<std::string> lines;
7326 SplitString(contents, '\n', &lines);
7327 for (size_t i = 0; i < lines.size(); ++i) {
7328 if (lines[i].empty())
7329 continue;
7330 if (!ParseGoogleTestFlag(lines[i].c_str()))
7331 g_help_flag = true;
7332 }
7333}
7334#endif // GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_
7335
7336// Parses the command line for Google Test flags, without initializing
7337// other parts of Google Test. The type parameter CharType can be
7338// instantiated to either char or wchar_t.
7339template <typename CharType>
7340void ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnlyImpl(int* argc, CharType** argv) {
7341 for (int i = 1; i < *argc; i++) {
7342 const std::string arg_string = StreamableToString(argv[i]);
7343 const char* const arg = arg_string.c_str();
7344
7345 using internal::ParseBoolFlag;
7346 using internal::ParseInt32Flag;
7347 using internal::ParseStringFlag;
7348
7349 bool remove_flag = false;
7350 if (ParseGoogleTestFlag(arg)) {
7351 remove_flag = true;
7352#if GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_
7353 } else if (ParseStringFlag(arg, kFlagfileFlag, &GTEST_FLAG(flagfile))) {
7354 LoadFlagsFromFile(GTEST_FLAG(flagfile));
7355 remove_flag = true;
7356#endif // GTEST_USE_OWN_FLAGFILE_FLAG_
7357 } else if (arg_string == "--help" || arg_string == "-h" ||
7358 arg_string == "-?" || arg_string == "/?" ||
7359 HasGoogleTestFlagPrefix(arg)) {
7360 // Both help flag and unrecognized Google Test flags (excluding
7361 // internal ones) trigger help display.
7362 g_help_flag = true;
7363 }
7364
7365 if (remove_flag) {
7366 // Shift the remainder of the argv list left by one. Note
7367 // that argv has (*argc + 1) elements, the last one always being
7368 // NULL. The following loop moves the trailing NULL element as
7369 // well.
7370 for (int j = i; j != *argc; j++) {
7371 argv[j] = argv[j + 1];
7372 }
7373
7374 // Decrements the argument count.
7375 (*argc)--;
7376
7377 // We also need to decrement the iterator as we just removed
7378 // an element.
7379 i--;
7380 }
7381 }
7382
7383 if (g_help_flag) {
7384 // We print the help here instead of in RUN_ALL_TESTS(), as the
7385 // latter may not be called at all if the user is using Google
7386 // Test with another testing framework.
7387 PrintColorEncoded(kColorEncodedHelpMessage);
7388 }
7389}

7391// Parses the command line for Google Test flags, without initializing
7392// other parts of Google Test.
7393void ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly(int* argc, char** argv) {
7394 ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnlyImpl(argc, argv);
7395

7397 // *_NSGetArgv() == argv
7398 // Only applicable to char** version of argv
7399#if GTEST_OS_MAC
7400#ifndef GTEST_OS_IOS
7401 if (*_NSGetArgv() == argv) {
7402 *_NSGetArgc() = *argc;
7403 }
7404#endif
7405#endif

7410
7411// The internal implementation of InitGoogleTest().
7412//
7413// The type parameter CharType can be instantiated to either char or
7414// wchar_t.
7415template <typename CharType>
7416void InitGoogleTestImpl(int* argc, CharType** argv) {
7417 // We don't want to run the initialization code twice.
7418 if (GTestIsInitialized()) return;
7419
7420 if (*argc <= 0) return;
7421
7422 g_argvs.clear();
7423 for (int i = 0; i != *argc; i++) {
7424 g_argvs.push_back(StreamableToString(argv[i]));
7425 }
7426
7427#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
7428 absl::InitializeSymbolizer(g_argvs[0].c_str());
7429#endif // GTEST_HAS_ABSL
7430
7431 ParseGoogleTestFlagsOnly(argc, argv);
7432 GetUnitTestImpl()->PostFlagParsingInit();
7433}

7437// Initializes Google Test. This must be called before calling
7438// RUN_ALL_TESTS(). In particular, it parses a command line for the
7439// flags that Google Test recognizes. Whenever a Google Test flag is
7440// seen, it is removed from argv, and *argc is decremented.
7441//
7442// No value is returned. Instead, the Google Test flag variables are
7443// updated.
7444//
7445// Calling the function for the second time has no user-visible effect.
7446void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, char** argv) {
7447#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7448 GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_(argc, argv);
7449#else // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7450 internal::InitGoogleTestImpl(argc, argv);
7451#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7452}
7453
7454// This overloaded version can be used in Windows programs compiled in
7455// UNICODE mode.
7456void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, wchar_t** argv) {
7457#if defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7458 GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_(argc, argv);
7459#else // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7460 internal::InitGoogleTestImpl(argc, argv);
7461#endif // defined(GTEST_CUSTOM_INIT_GOOGLE_TEST_FUNCTION_)
7462}

7693// Generates a textual description of a given exit code, in the format
7694// specified by wait(2).
7695static std::string ExitSummary(int exit_code) {
7696 Message m;
7697
7698# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS || GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
7699
7700 m << "Exited with exit status " << exit_code;
7701
7702# else
7703
7704 if (WIFEXITED(exit_code)) {
7705 m << "Exited with exit status " << WEXITSTATUS(exit_code);
7706 } else if (WIFSIGNALED(exit_code)) {
7707 m << "Terminated by signal " << WTERMSIG(exit_code);
7708 }
7709# ifdef WCOREDUMP
7710 if (WCOREDUMP(exit_code)) {
7711 m << " (core dumped)";
7712 }
7713# endif
7714# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS || GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
7715
7716 return m.GetString();
7717}

7726// Generates a textual failure message when a death test finds more than
7727// one thread running, or cannot determine the number of threads, prior
7728// to executing the given statement. It is the responsibility of the
7729// caller not to pass a thread_count of 1.
7730static std::string DeathTestThreadWarning(size_t thread_count) {
7731 Message msg;
7732 msg << "Death tests use fork(), which is unsafe particularly"
7733 << " in a threaded context. For this test, " << GTEST_NAME_ << " ";
7734 if (thread_count == 0) {
7735 msg << "couldn't detect the number of threads.";
7736 } else {
7737 msg << "detected " << thread_count << " threads.";
7738 }
7739 msg << " See "
7740 "https://github.com/google/googletest/blob/master/googletest/docs/"
7741 "advanced.md#death-tests-and-threads"
7742 << " for more explanation and suggested solutions, especially if"
7743 << " this is the last message you see before your test times out.";
7744 return msg.GetString();
7745}

7748// Flag characters for reporting a death test that did not die.
7749static const char kDeathTestLived = 'L';
7750static const char kDeathTestReturned = 'R';
7751static const char kDeathTestThrew = 'T';
7752static const char kDeathTestInternalError = 'I';
7753
7754#if GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
7755
7756// File descriptor used for the pipe in the child process.
7757static const int kFuchsiaReadPipeFd = 3;
7758
7759#endif
7760
7761// An enumeration describing all of the possible ways that a death test can
7762// conclude. DIED means that the process died while executing the test
7763// code; LIVED means that process lived beyond the end of the test code;
7764// RETURNED means that the test statement attempted to execute a return
7765// statement, which is not allowed; THREW means that the test statement
7766// returned control by throwing an exception. IN_PROGRESS means the test
7767// has not yet concluded.
7768// FIXME: Unify names and possibly values for
7769// AbortReason, DeathTestOutcome, and flag characters above.
7770enum DeathTestOutcome { IN_PROGRESS, DIED, LIVED, RETURNED, THREW };
7771
7772// Routine for aborting the program which is safe to call from an
7773// exec-style death test child process, in which case the error
7774// message is propagated back to the parent process. Otherwise, the
7775// message is simply printed to stderr. In either case, the program
7776// then exits with status 1.
7777static void DeathTestAbort(const std::string& message) {
7778 // On a POSIX system, this function may be called from a threadsafe-style
7779 // death test child process, which operates on a very small stack. Use
7780 // the heap for any additional non-minuscule memory requirements.
7781 const InternalRunDeathTestFlag* const flag =
7782 GetUnitTestImpl()->internal_run_death_test_flag();
7783 if (flag != NULL) {
7784 FILE* parent = posix::FDOpen(flag->write_fd(), "w");
7785 fputc(kDeathTestInternalError, parent);
7786 fprintf(parent, "%s", message.c_str());
7787 fflush(parent);
7788 _exit(1);
7789 } else {
7790 fprintf(stderr, "%s", message.c_str());
7791 fflush(stderr);
7792 posix::Abort();
7793 }
7794}
7795
7796// A replacement for CHECK that calls DeathTestAbort if the assertion
7797// fails.
7798# define GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(expression) \
7799 do { \
7800 if (!::testing::internal::IsTrue(expression)) { \
7801 DeathTestAbort( \
7802 ::std::string("CHECK failed: File ") + __FILE__ + ", line " \
7803 + ::testing::internal::StreamableToString(__LINE__) + ": " \
7804 + #expression); \
7805 } \
7806 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
7807
7808// This macro is similar to GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_, but it is meant for
7809// evaluating any system call that fulfills two conditions: it must return
7810// -1 on failure, and set errno to EINTR when it is interrupted and
7811// should be tried again. The macro expands to a loop that repeatedly
7812// evaluates the expression as long as it evaluates to -1 and sets
7813// errno to EINTR. If the expression evaluates to -1 but errno is
7814// something other than EINTR, DeathTestAbort is called.
7815# define GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(expression) \
7816 do { \
7817 int gtest_retval; \
7818 do { \
7819 gtest_retval = (expression); \
7820 } while (gtest_retval == -1 && errno == EINTR); \
7821 if (gtest_retval == -1) { \
7822 DeathTestAbort( \
7823 ::std::string("CHECK failed: File ") + __FILE__ + ", line " \
7824 + ::testing::internal::StreamableToString(__LINE__) + ": " \
7825 + #expression + " != -1"); \
7826 } \
7827 } while (::testing::internal::AlwaysFalse())
7828
7829// Returns the message describing the last system error in errno.
7830std::string GetLastErrnoDescription() {
7831 return errno == 0 ? "" : posix::StrError(errno);
7832}
7833
7834// This is called from a death test parent process to read a failure
7835// message from the death test child process and log it with the FATAL
7836// severity. On Windows, the message is read from a pipe handle. On other
7837// platforms, it is read from a file descriptor.
7838static void FailFromInternalError(int fd) {
7839 Message error;
7840 char buffer[256];
7841 int num_read;
7842
7843 do {
7844 while ((num_read = posix::Read(fd, buffer, 255)) > 0) {
7845 buffer[num_read] = '\0';
7846 error << buffer;
7847 }
7848 } while (num_read == -1 && errno == EINTR);
7849
7850 if (num_read == 0) {
7851 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << error.GetString();
7852 } else {
7853 const int last_error = errno;
7854 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Error while reading death test internal: "
7855 << GetLastErrnoDescription() << " [" << last_error << "]";
7856 }
7857}

7887// Provides cross platform implementation for some death functionality.
7888class DeathTestImpl : public DeathTest {
7889 protected:
7890 DeathTestImpl(const char* a_statement, const RE* a_regex)
7891 : statement_(a_statement),
7892 regex_(a_regex),
7893 spawned_(false),
7894 status_(-1),
7895 outcome_(IN_PROGRESS),
7896 read_fd_(-1),
7897 write_fd_(-1) {}
7898
7899 // read_fd_ is expected to be closed and cleared by a derived class.
7900 ~DeathTestImpl() { GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(read_fd_ == -1); }
7901
7902 void Abort(AbortReason reason);
7903 virtual bool Passed(bool status_ok);
7904
7905 const char* statement() const { return statement_; }
7906 const RE* regex() const { return regex_; }
7907 bool spawned() const { return spawned_; }
7908 void set_spawned(bool is_spawned) { spawned_ = is_spawned; }
7909 int status() const { return status_; }
7910 void set_status(int a_status) { status_ = a_status; }
7911 DeathTestOutcome outcome() const { return outcome_; }
7912 void set_outcome(DeathTestOutcome an_outcome) { outcome_ = an_outcome; }
7913 int read_fd() const { return read_fd_; }
7914 void set_read_fd(int fd) { read_fd_ = fd; }
7915 int write_fd() const { return write_fd_; }
7916 void set_write_fd(int fd) { write_fd_ = fd; }
7917
7918 // Called in the parent process only. Reads the result code of the death
7919 // test child process via a pipe, interprets it to set the outcome_
7920 // member, and closes read_fd_. Outputs diagnostics and terminates in
7921 // case of unexpected codes.
7922 void ReadAndInterpretStatusByte();
7923
7924 private:
7925 // The textual content of the code this object is testing. This class
7926 // doesn't own this string and should not attempt to delete it.
7927 const char* const statement_;
7928 // The regular expression which test output must match. DeathTestImpl
7929 // doesn't own this object and should not attempt to delete it.
7930 const RE* const regex_;
7931 // True if the death test child process has been successfully spawned.
7932 bool spawned_;
7933 // The exit status of the child process.
7934 int status_;
7935 // How the death test concluded.
7936 DeathTestOutcome outcome_;
7937 // Descriptor to the read end of the pipe to the child process. It is
7938 // always -1 in the child process. The child keeps its write end of the
7939 // pipe in write_fd_.
7940 int read_fd_;
7941 // Descriptor to the child's write end of the pipe to the parent process.
7942 // It is always -1 in the parent process. The parent keeps its end of the
7943 // pipe in read_fd_.
7944 int write_fd_;
7945};
7946
7947// Called in the parent process only. Reads the result code of the death
7948// test child process via a pipe, interprets it to set the outcome_
7949// member, and closes read_fd_. Outputs diagnostics and terminates in
7950// case of unexpected codes.
7951void DeathTestImpl::ReadAndInterpretStatusByte() {
7952 char flag;
7953 int bytes_read;
7954
7955 // The read() here blocks until data is available (signifying the
7956 // failure of the death test) or until the pipe is closed (signifying
7957 // its success), so it's okay to call this in the parent before
7958 // the child process has exited.
7959 do {
7960 bytes_read = posix::Read(read_fd(), &flag, 1);
7961 } while (bytes_read == -1 && errno == EINTR);
7962
7963 if (bytes_read == 0) {
7964 set_outcome(DIED);
7965 } else if (bytes_read == 1) {
7966 switch (flag) {
7967 case kDeathTestReturned:
7968 set_outcome(RETURNED);
7969 break;
7970 case kDeathTestThrew:
7971 set_outcome(THREW);
7972 break;
7973 case kDeathTestLived:
7974 set_outcome(LIVED);
7975 break;
7976 case kDeathTestInternalError:
7977 FailFromInternalError(read_fd()); // Does not return.
7978 break;
7979 default:
7980 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Death test child process reported "
7981 << "unexpected status byte ("
7982 << static_cast<unsigned int>(flag) << ")";
7983 }
7984 } else {
7985 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Read from death test child process failed: "
7986 << GetLastErrnoDescription();
7987 }
7988 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(posix::Close(read_fd()));
7989 set_read_fd(-1);
7990}
7991
7992// Signals that the death test code which should have exited, didn't.
7993// Should be called only in a death test child process.
7994// Writes a status byte to the child's status file descriptor, then
7995// calls _exit(1).
7996void DeathTestImpl::Abort(AbortReason reason) {
7997 // The parent process considers the death test to be a failure if
7998 // it finds any data in our pipe. So, here we write a single flag byte
7999 // to the pipe, then exit.
8000 const char status_ch =
8001 reason == TEST_DID_NOT_DIE ? kDeathTestLived :
8002 reason == TEST_THREW_EXCEPTION ? kDeathTestThrew : kDeathTestReturned;
8003
8004 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(posix::Write(write_fd(), &status_ch, 1));
8005 // We are leaking the descriptor here because on some platforms (i.e.,
8006 // when built as Windows DLL), destructors of global objects will still
8007 // run after calling _exit(). On such systems, write_fd_ will be
8008 // indirectly closed from the destructor of UnitTestImpl, causing double
8009 // close if it is also closed here. On debug configurations, double close
8010 // may assert. As there are no in-process buffers to flush here, we are
8011 // relying on the OS to close the descriptor after the process terminates
8012 // when the destructors are not run.
8013 _exit(1); // Exits w/o any normal exit hooks (we were supposed to crash)
8014}
8015
8016// Returns an indented copy of stderr output for a death test.
8017// This makes distinguishing death test output lines from regular log lines
8018// much easier.
8019static ::std::string FormatDeathTestOutput(const ::std::string& output) {
8020 ::std::string ret;
8021 for (size_t at = 0; ; ) {
8022 const size_t line_end = output.find('\n', at);
8023 ret += "[ DEATH ] ";
8024 if (line_end == ::std::string::npos) {
8025 ret += output.substr(at);
8026 break;
8027 }
8028 ret += output.substr(at, line_end + 1 - at);
8029 at = line_end + 1;
8030 }
8031 return ret;
8032}
8033
8034// Assesses the success or failure of a death test, using both private
8035// members which have previously been set, and one argument:
8036//
8037// Private data members:
8038// outcome: An enumeration describing how the death test
8039// concluded: DIED, LIVED, THREW, or RETURNED. The death test
8040// fails in the latter three cases.
8041// status: The exit status of the child process. On *nix, it is in the
8042// in the format specified by wait(2). On Windows, this is the
8043// value supplied to the ExitProcess() API or a numeric code
8044// of the exception that terminated the program.
8045// regex: A regular expression object to be applied to
8046// the test's captured standard error output; the death test
8047// fails if it does not match.
8048//
8049// Argument:
8050// status_ok: true if exit_status is acceptable in the context of
8051// this particular death test, which fails if it is false
8052//
8053// Returns true iff all of the above conditions are met. Otherwise, the
8054// first failing condition, in the order given above, is the one that is
8055// reported. Also sets the last death test message string.
8056bool DeathTestImpl::Passed(bool status_ok) {
8057 if (!spawned())
8058 return false;
8059
8060 const std::string error_message = GetCapturedStderr();
8061
8062 bool success = false;
8063 Message buffer;
8064
8065 buffer << "Death test: " << statement() << "\n";
8066 switch (outcome()) {
8067 case LIVED:
8068 buffer << " Result: failed to die.\n"
8069 << " Error msg:\n" << FormatDeathTestOutput(error_message);
8070 break;
8071 case THREW:
8072 buffer << " Result: threw an exception.\n"
8073 << " Error msg:\n" << FormatDeathTestOutput(error_message);
8074 break;
8075 case RETURNED:
8076 buffer << " Result: illegal return in test statement.\n"
8077 << " Error msg:\n" << FormatDeathTestOutput(error_message);
8078 break;
8079 case DIED:
8080 if (status_ok) {
8081# if GTEST_USES_PCRE
8082 // PCRE regexes support embedded NULs.
8083 const bool matched = RE::PartialMatch(error_message, *regex());
8084# else
8085 const bool matched = RE::PartialMatch(error_message.c_str(), *regex());
8086# endif // GTEST_USES_PCRE
8087 if (matched) {
8088 success = true;
8089 } else {
8090 buffer << " Result: died but not with expected error.\n"
8091 << " Expected: " << regex()->pattern() << "\n"
8092 << "Actual msg:\n" << FormatDeathTestOutput(error_message);
8093 }
8094 } else {
8095 buffer << " Result: died but not with expected exit code:\n"
8096 << " " << ExitSummary(status()) << "\n"
8097 << "Actual msg:\n" << FormatDeathTestOutput(error_message);
8098 }
8099 break;
8100 case IN_PROGRESS:
8101 default:
8102 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL)
8103 << "DeathTest::Passed somehow called before conclusion of test";
8104 }
8105
8106 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message(buffer.GetString());
8107 return success;
8108}
8109
8110# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
8111// WindowsDeathTest implements death tests on Windows. Due to the
8112// specifics of starting new processes on Windows, death tests there are
8113// always threadsafe, and Google Test considers the
8114// --gtest_death_test_style=fast setting to be equivalent to
8115// --gtest_death_test_style=threadsafe there.
8116//
8117// A few implementation notes: Like the Linux version, the Windows
8118// implementation uses pipes for child-to-parent communication. But due to
8119// the specifics of pipes on Windows, some extra steps are required:
8120//
8121// 1. The parent creates a communication pipe and stores handles to both
8122// ends of it.
8123// 2. The parent starts the child and provides it with the information
8124// necessary to acquire the handle to the write end of the pipe.
8125// 3. The child acquires the write end of the pipe and signals the parent
8126// using a Windows event.
8127// 4. Now the parent can release the write end of the pipe on its side. If
8128// this is done before step 3, the object's reference count goes down to
8129// 0 and it is destroyed, preventing the child from acquiring it. The
8130// parent now has to release it, or read operations on the read end of
8131// the pipe will not return when the child terminates.
8132// 5. The parent reads child's output through the pipe (outcome code and
8133// any possible error messages) from the pipe, and its stderr and then
8134// determines whether to fail the test.
8135//
8136// Note: to distinguish Win32 API calls from the local method and function
8137// calls, the former are explicitly resolved in the global namespace.
8138//
8139class WindowsDeathTest : public DeathTestImpl {
8140 public:
8141 WindowsDeathTest(const char* a_statement,
8142 const RE* a_regex,
8143 const char* file,
8144 int line)
8145 : DeathTestImpl(a_statement, a_regex), file_(file), line_(line) {}
8146
8147 // All of these virtual functions are inherited from DeathTest.
8148 virtual int Wait();
8149 virtual TestRole AssumeRole();
8150
8151 private:
8152 // The name of the file in which the death test is located.
8153 const char* const file_;
8154 // The line number on which the death test is located.
8155 const int line_;
8156 // Handle to the write end of the pipe to the child process.
8157 AutoHandle write_handle_;
8158 // Child process handle.
8159 AutoHandle child_handle_;
8160 // Event the child process uses to signal the parent that it has
8161 // acquired the handle to the write end of the pipe. After seeing this
8162 // event the parent can release its own handles to make sure its
8163 // ReadFile() calls return when the child terminates.
8164 AutoHandle event_handle_;
8165};
8166
8167// Waits for the child in a death test to exit, returning its exit
8168// status, or 0 if no child process exists. As a side effect, sets the
8169// outcome data member.
8170int WindowsDeathTest::Wait() {
8171 if (!spawned())
8172 return 0;
8173
8174 // Wait until the child either signals that it has acquired the write end
8175 // of the pipe or it dies.
8176 const HANDLE wait_handles[2] = { child_handle_.Get(), event_handle_.Get() };
8177 switch (::WaitForMultipleObjects(2,
8178 wait_handles,
8179 FALSE, // Waits for any of the handles.
8180 INFINITE)) {
8181 case WAIT_OBJECT_0:
8182 case WAIT_OBJECT_0 + 1:
8183 break;
8184 default:
8185 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(false); // Should not get here.
8186 }
8187
8188 // The child has acquired the write end of the pipe or exited.
8189 // We release the handle on our side and continue.
8190 write_handle_.Reset();
8191 event_handle_.Reset();
8192
8193 ReadAndInterpretStatusByte();
8194
8195 // Waits for the child process to exit if it haven't already. This
8196 // returns immediately if the child has already exited, regardless of
8197 // whether previous calls to WaitForMultipleObjects synchronized on this
8198 // handle or not.
8199 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(
8200 WAIT_OBJECT_0 == ::WaitForSingleObject(child_handle_.Get(),
8201 INFINITE));
8202 DWORD status_code;
8203 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(
8204 ::GetExitCodeProcess(child_handle_.Get(), &status_code) != FALSE);
8205 child_handle_.Reset();
8206 set_status(static_cast<int>(status_code));
8207 return status();
8208}
8209
8210// The AssumeRole process for a Windows death test. It creates a child
8211// process with the same executable as the current process to run the
8212// death test. The child process is given the --gtest_filter and
8213// --gtest_internal_run_death_test flags such that it knows to run the
8214// current death test only.
8215DeathTest::TestRole WindowsDeathTest::AssumeRole() {
8216 const UnitTestImpl* const impl = GetUnitTestImpl();
8217 const InternalRunDeathTestFlag* const flag =
8218 impl->internal_run_death_test_flag();
8219 const TestInfo* const info = impl->current_test_info();
8220 const int death_test_index = info->result()->death_test_count();
8221
8222 if (flag != NULL) {
8223 // ParseInternalRunDeathTestFlag() has performed all the necessary
8224 // processing.
8225 set_write_fd(flag->write_fd());
8226 return EXECUTE_TEST;
8227 }
8228
8229 // WindowsDeathTest uses an anonymous pipe to communicate results of
8230 // a death test.
8231 SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES handles_are_inheritable = {
8232 sizeof(SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES), NULL, TRUE };
8233 HANDLE read_handle, write_handle;
8234 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(
8235 ::CreatePipe(&read_handle, &write_handle, &handles_are_inheritable,
8236 0) // Default buffer size.
8237 != FALSE);
8238 set_read_fd(::_open_osfhandle(reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(read_handle),
8239 O_RDONLY));
8240 write_handle_.Reset(write_handle);
8241 event_handle_.Reset(::CreateEvent(
8242 &handles_are_inheritable,
8243 TRUE, // The event will automatically reset to non-signaled state.
8244 FALSE, // The initial state is non-signalled.
8245 NULL)); // The even is unnamed.
8246 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(event_handle_.Get() != NULL);
8247 const std::string filter_flag =
8248 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kFilterFlag + "=" +
8249 info->test_case_name() + "." + info->name();
8250 const std::string internal_flag =
8251 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kInternalRunDeathTestFlag +
8252 "=" + file_ + "|" + StreamableToString(line_) + "|" +
8253 StreamableToString(death_test_index) + "|" +
8254 StreamableToString(static_cast<unsigned int>(::GetCurrentProcessId())) +
8255 // size_t has the same width as pointers on both 32-bit and 64-bit
8256 // Windows platforms.
8257 // See http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/tcxf1dw6.aspx.
8258 "|" + StreamableToString(reinterpret_cast<size_t>(write_handle)) +
8259 "|" + StreamableToString(reinterpret_cast<size_t>(event_handle_.Get()));
8260
8261 char executable_path[_MAX_PATH + 1]; // NOLINT
8262 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(
8263 _MAX_PATH + 1 != ::GetModuleFileNameA(NULL,
8264 executable_path,
8265 _MAX_PATH));
8266
8267 std::string command_line =
8268 std::string(::GetCommandLineA()) + " " + filter_flag + " \"" +
8269 internal_flag + "\"";
8270
8271 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message("");
8272
8273 CaptureStderr();
8274 // Flush the log buffers since the log streams are shared with the child.
8275 FlushInfoLog();
8276
8277 // The child process will share the standard handles with the parent.
8278 STARTUPINFOA startup_info;
8279 memset(&startup_info, 0, sizeof(STARTUPINFO));
8280 startup_info.dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES;
8281 startup_info.hStdInput = ::GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE);
8282 startup_info.hStdOutput = ::GetStdHandle(STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE);
8283 startup_info.hStdError = ::GetStdHandle(STD_ERROR_HANDLE);
8284
8285 PROCESS_INFORMATION process_info;
8286 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(::CreateProcessA(
8287 executable_path,
8288 const_cast<char*>(command_line.c_str()),
8289 NULL, // Returned process handle is not inheritable.
8290 NULL, // Returned thread handle is not inheritable.
8291 TRUE, // Child inherits all inheritable handles (for write_handle_).
8292 0x0, // Default creation flags.
8293 NULL, // Inherit the parent's environment.
8294 UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir(),
8295 &startup_info,
8296 &process_info) != FALSE);
8297 child_handle_.Reset(process_info.hProcess);
8298 ::CloseHandle(process_info.hThread);
8299 set_spawned(true);
8300 return OVERSEE_TEST;
8301}

8314 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status == ZX_OK);
8315 status = zx_handle_close(port_);

8319 // All of these virtual functions are inherited from DeathTest.

8332
8333// Utility class for accumulating command-line arguments.
8334class Arguments {
8335 public:
8336 Arguments() {
8337 args_.push_back(NULL);
8338 }
8339
8340 ~Arguments() {
8341 for (std::vector<char*>::iterator i = args_.begin(); i != args_.end();
8342 ++i) {
8343 free(*i);
8344 }
8345 }
8346 void AddArgument(const char* argument) {
8347 args_.insert(args_.end() - 1, posix::StrDup(argument));
8348 }
8349
8350 template <typename Str>
8351 void AddArguments(const ::std::vector<Str>& arguments) {
8352 for (typename ::std::vector<Str>::const_iterator i = arguments.begin();
8353 i != arguments.end();
8354 ++i) {
8355 args_.insert(args_.end() - 1, posix::StrDup(i->c_str()));
8356 }
8357 }
8358 char* const* Argv() {
8359 return &args_[0];
8360 }
8361
8362 int size() {
8363 return args_.size() - 1;
8364 }
8365
8366 private:
8367 std::vector<char*> args_;
8368};
8369
8370// Waits for the child in a death test to exit, returning its exit
8371// status, or 0 if no child process exists. As a side effect, sets the
8372// outcome data member.
8373int FuchsiaDeathTest::Wait() {
8374 if (!spawned())
8375 return 0;
8376
8377 // Register to wait for the child process to terminate.
8378 zx_status_t status_zx;
8379 status_zx = zx_object_wait_async(child_process_,
8380 port_,
8381 0 /* key */,
8382 ZX_PROCESS_TERMINATED,
8383 ZX_WAIT_ASYNC_ONCE);
8384 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status_zx == ZX_OK);
8385
8386 // Wait for it to terminate, or an exception to be received.
8387 zx_port_packet_t packet;
8388 status_zx = zx_port_wait(port_, ZX_TIME_INFINITE, &packet);
8389 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status_zx == ZX_OK);
8390
8391 if (ZX_PKT_IS_EXCEPTION(packet.type)) {
8392 // Process encountered an exception. Kill it directly rather than letting
8393 // other handlers process the event.
8394 status_zx = zx_task_kill(child_process_);
8395 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status_zx == ZX_OK);
8396
8397 // Now wait for |child_process_| to terminate.
8398 zx_signals_t signals = 0;
8399 status_zx = zx_object_wait_one(
8400 child_process_, ZX_PROCESS_TERMINATED, ZX_TIME_INFINITE, &signals);
8401 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status_zx == ZX_OK);
8402 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(signals & ZX_PROCESS_TERMINATED);
8403 } else {
8404 // Process terminated.
8405 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(ZX_PKT_IS_SIGNAL_ONE(packet.type));
8406 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(packet.signal.observed & ZX_PROCESS_TERMINATED);
8407 }
8408
8409 ReadAndInterpretStatusByte();
8410
8411 zx_info_process_t buffer;
8412 status_zx = zx_object_get_info(
8413 child_process_,
8414 ZX_INFO_PROCESS,
8415 &buffer,
8416 sizeof(buffer),
8417 nullptr,
8418 nullptr);
8419 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status_zx == ZX_OK);
8420
8421 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(buffer.exited);
8422 set_status(buffer.return_code);
8423 return status();
8424}
8425
8426// The AssumeRole process for a Fuchsia death test. It creates a child
8427// process with the same executable as the current process to run the
8428// death test. The child process is given the --gtest_filter and
8429// --gtest_internal_run_death_test flags such that it knows to run the
8430// current death test only.
8431DeathTest::TestRole FuchsiaDeathTest::AssumeRole() {
8432 const UnitTestImpl* const impl = GetUnitTestImpl();
8433 const InternalRunDeathTestFlag* const flag =
8434 impl->internal_run_death_test_flag();
8435 const TestInfo* const info = impl->current_test_info();
8436 const int death_test_index = info->result()->death_test_count();
8437
8438 if (flag != NULL) {
8439 // ParseInternalRunDeathTestFlag() has performed all the necessary
8440 // processing.
8441 set_write_fd(kFuchsiaReadPipeFd);
8442 return EXECUTE_TEST;
8443 }
8444
8445 CaptureStderr();
8446 // Flush the log buffers since the log streams are shared with the child.
8447 FlushInfoLog();
8448
8449 // Build the child process command line.
8450 const std::string filter_flag =
8451 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kFilterFlag + "="
8452 + info->test_case_name() + "." + info->name();
8453 const std::string internal_flag =
8454 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kInternalRunDeathTestFlag + "="
8455 + file_ + "|"
8456 + StreamableToString(line_) + "|"
8457 + StreamableToString(death_test_index);
8458 Arguments args;
8459 args.AddArguments(GetInjectableArgvs());
8460 args.AddArgument(filter_flag.c_str());
8461 args.AddArgument(internal_flag.c_str());
8462
8463 // Build the pipe for communication with the child.
8464 zx_status_t status;
8465 zx_handle_t child_pipe_handle;
8466 uint32_t type;
8467 status = fdio_pipe_half(&child_pipe_handle, &type);
8468 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status >= 0);
8469 set_read_fd(status);
8470
8471 // Set the pipe handle for the child.
8472 fdio_spawn_action_t add_handle_action = {};
8473 add_handle_action.action = FDIO_SPAWN_ACTION_ADD_HANDLE;
8474 add_handle_action.h.id = PA_HND(type, kFuchsiaReadPipeFd);
8475 add_handle_action.h.handle = child_pipe_handle;
8476
8477 // Spawn the child process.
8478 status = fdio_spawn_etc(ZX_HANDLE_INVALID, FDIO_SPAWN_CLONE_ALL,
8479 args.Argv()[0], args.Argv(), nullptr, 1,
8480 &add_handle_action, &child_process_, nullptr);
8481 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status == ZX_OK);
8482
8483 // Create an exception port and attach it to the |child_process_|, to allow
8484 // us to suppress the system default exception handler from firing.
8485 status = zx_port_create(0, &port_);
8486 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status == ZX_OK);
8487 status = zx_task_bind_exception_port(
8488 child_process_, port_, 0 /* key */, 0 /*options */);
8489 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(status == ZX_OK);
8490
8491 set_spawned(true);
8492 return OVERSEE_TEST;
8493}
