8543
8544// The AssumeRole process for a fork-and-run death test. It implements a
8545// straightforward fork, with a simple pipe to transmit the status byte.
8546DeathTest::TestRole NoExecDeathTest::AssumeRole() {
8547 const size_t thread_count = GetThreadCount();
8548 if (thread_count != 1) {
8549 GTEST_LOG_(WARNING) << DeathTestThreadWarning(thread_count);
8550 }
8551
8552 int pipe_fd[2];
8553 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(pipe(pipe_fd) != -1);
8554
8555 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message("");
8556 CaptureStderr();
8557 // When we fork the process below, the log file buffers are copied, but the
8558 // file descriptors are shared. We flush all log files here so that closing
8559 // the file descriptors in the child process doesn't throw off the
8560 // synchronization between descriptors and buffers in the parent process.
8561 // This is as close to the fork as possible to avoid a race condition in case
8562 // there are multiple threads running before the death test, and another
8563 // thread writes to the log file.
8564 FlushInfoLog();
8565
8566 const pid_t child_pid = fork();
8567 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(child_pid != -1);
8568 set_child_pid(child_pid);
8569 if (child_pid == 0) {
8570 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(close(pipe_fd[0]));
8571 set_write_fd(pipe_fd[1]);
8572 // Redirects all logging to stderr in the child process to prevent
8573 // concurrent writes to the log files. We capture stderr in the parent
8574 // process and append the child process' output to a log.
8575 LogToStderr();
8576 // Event forwarding to the listeners of event listener API mush be shut
8577 // down in death test subprocesses.
8578 GetUnitTestImpl()->listeners()->SuppressEventForwarding();
8579 g_in_fast_death_test_child = true;
8580 return EXECUTE_TEST;
8581 } else {
8582 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(close(pipe_fd[1]));
8583 set_read_fd(pipe_fd[0]);
8584 set_spawned(true);
8585 return OVERSEE_TEST;
8586 }
8587}
8588
8589// A concrete death test class that forks and re-executes the main
8590// program from the beginning, with command-line flags set that cause
8591// only this specific death test to be run.
8592class ExecDeathTest : public ForkingDeathTest {
8593 public:
8594 ExecDeathTest(const char* a_statement, const RE* a_regex,
8595 const char* file, int line) :
8596 ForkingDeathTest(a_statement, a_regex), file_(file), line_(line) { }
8597 virtual TestRole AssumeRole();
8598 private:
8599 static ::std::vector<std::string> GetArgvsForDeathTestChildProcess() {
8600 ::std::vector<std::string> args = GetInjectableArgvs();
8601# if defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_COMMAND_LINE_ARGS_)
8602 ::std::vector<std::string> extra_args =
8603 GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_COMMAND_LINE_ARGS_();
8604 args.insert(args.end(), extra_args.begin(), extra_args.end());
8605# endif // defined(GTEST_EXTRA_DEATH_TEST_COMMAND_LINE_ARGS_)
8606 return args;
8607 }
8608 // The name of the file in which the death test is located.
8609 const char* const file_;
8610 // The line number on which the death test is located.
8611 const int line_;
8612};
8613
8614// Utility class for accumulating command-line arguments.
8615class Arguments {
8616 public:
8617 Arguments() {
8618 args_.push_back(NULL);
8619 }
8620
8621 ~Arguments() {
8622 for (std::vector<char*>::iterator i = args_.begin(); i != args_.end();
8623 ++i) {
8624 free(*i);
8625 }
8626 }
8627 void AddArgument(const char* argument) {
8628 args_.insert(args_.end() - 1, posix::StrDup(argument));
8629 }
8630
8631 template <typename Str>
8632 void AddArguments(const ::std::vector<Str>& arguments) {
8633 for (typename ::std::vector<Str>::const_iterator i = arguments.begin();
8634 i != arguments.end();
8635 ++i) {
8636 args_.insert(args_.end() - 1, posix::StrDup(i->c_str()));
8637 }
8638 }
8639 char* const* Argv() {
8640 return &args_[0];
8641 }
8642
8643 private:
8644 std::vector<char*> args_;
8645};
8646
8647// A struct that encompasses the arguments to the child process of a
8648// threadsafe-style death test process.
8649struct ExecDeathTestArgs {
8650 char* const* argv; // Command-line arguments for the child's call to exec
8651 int close_fd; // File descriptor to close; the read end of a pipe
8652};
8653
8654# if GTEST_OS_MAC
8655inline char** GetEnviron() {
8656 // When Google Test is built as a framework on MacOS X, the environ variable
8657 // is unavailable. Apple's documentation (man environ) recommends using
8658 // _NSGetEnviron() instead.
8659 return *_NSGetEnviron();
8660}
8661# else
8662// Some POSIX platforms expect you to declare environ. extern "C" makes
8663// it reside in the global namespace.
8664extern "C" char** environ;
8665inline char** GetEnviron() { return environ; }
8666# endif // GTEST_OS_MAC
8667
8668# if !GTEST_OS_QNX
8669// The main function for a threadsafe-style death test child process.
8670// This function is called in a clone()-ed process and thus must avoid
8671// any potentially unsafe operations like malloc or libc functions.
8672static int ExecDeathTestChildMain(void* child_arg) {
8673 ExecDeathTestArgs* const args = static_cast<ExecDeathTestArgs*>(child_arg);
8674 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(close(args->close_fd));
8675
8676 // We need to execute the test program in the same environment where
8677 // it was originally invoked. Therefore we change to the original
8678 // working directory first.
8679 const char* const original_dir =
8680 UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir();
8681 // We can safely call chdir() as it's a direct system call.
8682 if (chdir(original_dir) != 0) {
8683 DeathTestAbort(std::string("chdir(\"") + original_dir + "\") failed: " +
8684 GetLastErrnoDescription());
8685 return EXIT_FAILURE;
8686 }
8687
8688 // We can safely call execve() as it's a direct system call. We
8689 // cannot use execvp() as it's a libc function and thus potentially
8690 // unsafe. Since execve() doesn't search the PATH, the user must
8691 // invoke the test program via a valid path that contains at least
8692 // one path separator.
8693 execve(args->argv[0], args->argv, GetEnviron());
8694 DeathTestAbort(std::string("execve(") + args->argv[0] + ", ...) in " +
8695 original_dir + " failed: " +
8696 GetLastErrnoDescription());
8697 return EXIT_FAILURE;
8698}
8699# endif // !GTEST_OS_QNX
8700
8701# if GTEST_HAS_CLONE
8702// Two utility routines that together determine the direction the stack
8703// grows.
8704// This could be accomplished more elegantly by a single recursive
8705// function, but we want to guard against the unlikely possibility of
8706// a smart compiler optimizing the recursion away.
8707//
8708// GTEST_NO_INLINE_ is required to prevent GCC 4.6 from inlining
8709// StackLowerThanAddress into StackGrowsDown, which then doesn't give
8710// correct answer.
8711static void StackLowerThanAddress(const void* ptr,
8712 bool* result) GTEST_NO_INLINE_;
8713static void StackLowerThanAddress(const void* ptr, bool* result) {
8714 int dummy;
8715 *result = (&dummy < ptr);
8716}
8717
8718// Make sure AddressSanitizer does not tamper with the stack here.
8719GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS_
8720static bool StackGrowsDown() {
8721 int dummy = 0;
8722 bool result;
8723 StackLowerThanAddress(&dummy, &result);
8724 return result;
8725}
8726# endif // GTEST_HAS_CLONE
8727
8728// Spawns a child process with the same executable as the current process in
8729// a thread-safe manner and instructs it to run the death test. The
8730// implementation uses fork(2) + exec. On systems where clone(2) is
8731// available, it is used instead, being slightly more thread-safe. On QNX,
8732// fork supports only single-threaded environments, so this function uses
8733// spawn(2) there instead. The function dies with an error message if
8734// anything goes wrong.
8735static pid_t ExecDeathTestSpawnChild(char* const* argv, int close_fd) {
8736 ExecDeathTestArgs args = { argv, close_fd };
8737 pid_t child_pid = -1;
8738
8739# if GTEST_OS_QNX
8740 // Obtains the current directory and sets it to be closed in the child
8741 // process.
8742 const int cwd_fd = open(".", O_RDONLY);
8743 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(cwd_fd != -1);
8744 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(fcntl(cwd_fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC));
8745 // We need to execute the test program in the same environment where
8746 // it was originally invoked. Therefore we change to the original
8747 // working directory first.
8748 const char* const original_dir =
8749 UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir();
8750 // We can safely call chdir() as it's a direct system call.
8751 if (chdir(original_dir) != 0) {
8752 DeathTestAbort(std::string("chdir(\"") + original_dir + "\") failed: " +
8753 GetLastErrnoDescription());
8754 return EXIT_FAILURE;
8755 }
8756
8757 int fd_flags;
8758 // Set close_fd to be closed after spawn.
8759 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(fd_flags = fcntl(close_fd, F_GETFD));
8760 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(fcntl(close_fd, F_SETFD,
8761 fd_flags | FD_CLOEXEC));
8762 struct inheritance inherit = {0};
8763 // spawn is a system call.
8764 child_pid = spawn(args.argv[0], 0, NULL, &inherit, args.argv, GetEnviron());
8765 // Restores the current working directory.
8766 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(fchdir(cwd_fd) != -1);
8767 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(close(cwd_fd));
8768
8769# else // GTEST_OS_QNX
8770# if GTEST_OS_LINUX
8771 // When a SIGPROF signal is received while fork() or clone() are executing,
8772 // the process may hang. To avoid this, we ignore SIGPROF here and re-enable
8773 // it after the call to fork()/clone() is complete.
8774 struct sigaction saved_sigprof_action;
8775 struct sigaction ignore_sigprof_action;
8776 memset(&ignore_sigprof_action, 0, sizeof(ignore_sigprof_action));
8777 sigemptyset(&ignore_sigprof_action.sa_mask);
8778 ignore_sigprof_action.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
8779 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(sigaction(
8780 SIGPROF, &ignore_sigprof_action, &saved_sigprof_action));
8781# endif // GTEST_OS_LINUX
8782
8783# if GTEST_HAS_CLONE
8784 const bool use_fork = GTEST_FLAG(death_test_use_fork);
8785
8786 if (!use_fork) {
8787 static const bool stack_grows_down = StackGrowsDown();
8788 const size_t stack_size = getpagesize();
8789 // MMAP_ANONYMOUS is not defined on Mac, so we use MAP_ANON instead.
8790 void* const stack = mmap(NULL, stack_size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
8791 MAP_ANON | MAP_PRIVATE, -1, 0);
8792 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(stack != MAP_FAILED);
8793
8794 // Maximum stack alignment in bytes: For a downward-growing stack, this
8795 // amount is subtracted from size of the stack space to get an address
8796 // that is within the stack space and is aligned on all systems we care
8797 // about. As far as I know there is no ABI with stack alignment greater
8798 // than 64. We assume stack and stack_size already have alignment of
8799 // kMaxStackAlignment.
8800 const size_t kMaxStackAlignment = 64;
8801 void* const stack_top =
8802 static_cast<char*>(stack) +
8803 (stack_grows_down ? stack_size - kMaxStackAlignment : 0);
8804 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(stack_size > kMaxStackAlignment &&
8805 reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(stack_top) % kMaxStackAlignment == 0);
8806
8807 child_pid = clone(&ExecDeathTestChildMain, stack_top, SIGCHLD, &args);
8808
8809 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(munmap(stack, stack_size) != -1);
8810 }
8811# else
8812 const bool use_fork = true;
8813# endif // GTEST_HAS_CLONE
8814
8815 if (use_fork && (child_pid = fork()) == 0) {
8816 ExecDeathTestChildMain(&args);
8817 _exit(0);
8818 }
8819# endif // GTEST_OS_QNX
8820# if GTEST_OS_LINUX
8821 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(
8822 sigaction(SIGPROF, &saved_sigprof_action, NULL));
8823# endif // GTEST_OS_LINUX
8824
8825 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(child_pid != -1);
8826 return child_pid;
8827}
8828
8829// The AssumeRole process for a fork-and-exec death test. It re-executes the
8830// main program from the beginning, setting the --gtest_filter
8831// and --gtest_internal_run_death_test flags to cause only the current
8832// death test to be re-run.
8833DeathTest::TestRole ExecDeathTest::AssumeRole() {
8834 const UnitTestImpl* const impl = GetUnitTestImpl();
8835 const InternalRunDeathTestFlag* const flag =
8836 impl->internal_run_death_test_flag();
8837 const TestInfo* const info = impl->current_test_info();
8838 const int death_test_index = info->result()->death_test_count();
8839
8840 if (flag != NULL) {
8841 set_write_fd(flag->write_fd());
8842 return EXECUTE_TEST;
8843 }
8844
8845 int pipe_fd[2];
8846 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(pipe(pipe_fd) != -1);
8847 // Clear the close-on-exec flag on the write end of the pipe, lest
8848 // it be closed when the child process does an exec:
8849 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_(fcntl(pipe_fd[1], F_SETFD, 0) != -1);
8850
8851 const std::string filter_flag =
8852 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kFilterFlag + "="
8853 + info->test_case_name() + "." + info->name();
8854 const std::string internal_flag =
8855 std::string("--") + GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ + kInternalRunDeathTestFlag + "="
8856 + file_ + "|" + StreamableToString(line_) + "|"
8857 + StreamableToString(death_test_index) + "|"
8858 + StreamableToString(pipe_fd[1]);
8859 Arguments args;
8860 args.AddArguments(GetArgvsForDeathTestChildProcess());
8861 args.AddArgument(filter_flag.c_str());
8862 args.AddArgument(internal_flag.c_str());
8863
8864 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message("");
8865
8866 CaptureStderr();
8867 // See the comment in NoExecDeathTest::AssumeRole for why the next line
8868 // is necessary.
8869 FlushInfoLog();
8870
8871 const pid_t child_pid = ExecDeathTestSpawnChild(args.Argv(), pipe_fd[0]);
8872 GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_SYSCALL_(close(pipe_fd[1]));
8873 set_child_pid(child_pid);
8874 set_read_fd(pipe_fd[0]);
8875 set_spawned(true);
8876 return OVERSEE_TEST;
8877}
8878
8879# endif // !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
8880
8881// Creates a concrete DeathTest-derived class that depends on the
8882// --gtest_death_test_style flag, and sets the pointer pointed to
8883// by the "test" argument to its address. If the test should be
8884// skipped, sets that pointer to NULL. Returns true, unless the
8885// flag is set to an invalid value.
8886bool DefaultDeathTestFactory::Create(const char* statement, const RE* regex,
8887 const char* file, int line,
8888 DeathTest** test) {
8889 UnitTestImpl* const impl = GetUnitTestImpl();
8890 const InternalRunDeathTestFlag* const flag =
8891 impl->internal_run_death_test_flag();
8892 const int death_test_index = impl->current_test_info()
8893 ->increment_death_test_count();
8894
8895 if (flag != NULL) {
8896 if (death_test_index > flag->index()) {
8897 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message(
8898 "Death test count (" + StreamableToString(death_test_index)
8899 + ") somehow exceeded expected maximum ("
8900 + StreamableToString(flag->index()) + ")");
8901 return false;
8902 }
8903
8904 if (!(flag->file() == file && flag->line() == line &&
8905 flag->index() == death_test_index)) {
8906 *test = NULL;
8907 return true;
8908 }
8909 }
8910
8911# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
8912
8913 if (GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "threadsafe" ||
8914 GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "fast") {
8915 *test = new WindowsDeathTest(statement, regex, file, line);
8916 }
8917
8918# elif GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
8919
8920 if (GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "threadsafe" ||
8921 GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "fast") {
8922 *test = new FuchsiaDeathTest(statement, regex, file, line);
8923 }
8924
8925# else
8926
8927 if (GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "threadsafe") {
8928 *test = new ExecDeathTest(statement, regex, file, line);
8929 } else if (GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style) == "fast") {
8930 *test = new NoExecDeathTest(statement, regex);
8931 }
8932
8933# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
8934
8935 else { // NOLINT - this is more readable than unbalanced brackets inside #if.
8936 DeathTest::set_last_death_test_message(
8937 "Unknown death test style \"" + GTEST_FLAG(death_test_style)
8938 + "\" encountered");
8939 return false;
8940 }
8941
8942 return true;
8943}
8944
8945# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
8946// Recreates the pipe and event handles from the provided parameters,
8947// signals the event, and returns a file descriptor wrapped around the pipe
8948// handle. This function is called in the child process only.
8949static int GetStatusFileDescriptor(unsigned int parent_process_id,
8950 size_t write_handle_as_size_t,
8951 size_t event_handle_as_size_t) {
8952 AutoHandle parent_process_handle(::OpenProcess(PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE,
8953 FALSE, // Non-inheritable.
8954 parent_process_id));
8955 if (parent_process_handle.Get() == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
8956 DeathTestAbort("Unable to open parent process " +
8957 StreamableToString(parent_process_id));
8958 }
8959
8960 // FIXME: Replace the following check with a
8961 // compile-time assertion when available.
8962 GTEST_CHECK_(sizeof(HANDLE) <= sizeof(size_t));
8963
8964 const HANDLE write_handle =
8965 reinterpret_cast<HANDLE>(write_handle_as_size_t);
8966 HANDLE dup_write_handle;
8967
8968 // The newly initialized handle is accessible only in the parent
8969 // process. To obtain one accessible within the child, we need to use
8970 // DuplicateHandle.
8971 if (!::DuplicateHandle(parent_process_handle.Get(), write_handle,
8972 ::GetCurrentProcess(), &dup_write_handle,
8973 0x0, // Requested privileges ignored since
8974 // DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS is used.
8975 FALSE, // Request non-inheritable handler.
8976 DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS)) {
8977 DeathTestAbort("Unable to duplicate the pipe handle " +
8978 StreamableToString(write_handle_as_size_t) +
8979 " from the parent process " +
8980 StreamableToString(parent_process_id));
8981 }
8982
8983 const HANDLE event_handle = reinterpret_cast<HANDLE>(event_handle_as_size_t);
8984 HANDLE dup_event_handle;
8985
8986 if (!::DuplicateHandle(parent_process_handle.Get(), event_handle,
8987 ::GetCurrentProcess(), &dup_event_handle,
8988 0x0,
8989 FALSE,
8990 DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS)) {
8991 DeathTestAbort("Unable to duplicate the event handle " +
8992 StreamableToString(event_handle_as_size_t) +
8993 " from the parent process " +
8994 StreamableToString(parent_process_id));
8995 }
8996
8997 const int write_fd =
8998 ::_open_osfhandle(reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(dup_write_handle), O_APPEND);
8999 if (write_fd == -1) {
9000 DeathTestAbort("Unable to convert pipe handle " +
9001 StreamableToString(write_handle_as_size_t) +
9002 " to a file descriptor");
9003 }
9004
9005 // Signals the parent that the write end of the pipe has been acquired
9006 // so the parent can release its own write end.
9007 ::SetEvent(dup_event_handle);
9008
9009 return write_fd;
9010}
9011# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9012
9013// Returns a newly created InternalRunDeathTestFlag object with fields
9014// initialized from the GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test) flag if
9015// the flag is specified; otherwise returns NULL.
9016InternalRunDeathTestFlag* ParseInternalRunDeathTestFlag() {
9017 if (GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test) == "") return NULL;
9018
9019 // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST implies that we have ::std::string, so we
9020 // can use it here.
9021 int line = -1;
9022 int index = -1;
9023 ::std::vector< ::std::string> fields;
9024 SplitString(GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test).c_str(), '|', &fields);
9025 int write_fd = -1;
9026
9027# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9028
9029 unsigned int parent_process_id = 0;
9030 size_t write_handle_as_size_t = 0;
9031 size_t event_handle_as_size_t = 0;
9032
9033 if (fields.size() != 6
9034 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[1], &line)
9035 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[2], &index)
9036 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[3], &parent_process_id)
9037 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[4], &write_handle_as_size_t)
9038 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[5], &event_handle_as_size_t)) {
9039 DeathTestAbort("Bad --gtest_internal_run_death_test flag: " +
9040 GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test));
9041 }
9042 write_fd = GetStatusFileDescriptor(parent_process_id,
9043 write_handle_as_size_t,
9044 event_handle_as_size_t);
9045
9046# elif GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
9047
9048 if (fields.size() != 3
9049 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[1], &line)
9050 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[2], &index)) {
9051 DeathTestAbort("Bad --gtest_internal_run_death_test flag: "
9052 + GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test));
9053 }
9054
9055# else
9056
9057 if (fields.size() != 4
9058 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[1], &line)
9059 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[2], &index)
9060 || !ParseNaturalNumber(fields[3], &write_fd)) {
9061 DeathTestAbort("Bad --gtest_internal_run_death_test flag: "
9062 + GTEST_FLAG(internal_run_death_test));
9063 }
9064
9065# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9066
9067 return new InternalRunDeathTestFlag(fields[0], line, index, write_fd);
9068}

9134#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9135// On Windows, '\\' is the standard path separator, but many tools and the
9136// Windows API also accept '/' as an alternate path separator. Unless otherwise
9137// noted, a file path can contain either kind of path separators, or a mixture
9138// of them.
9139const char kPathSeparator = '\\';
9140const char kAlternatePathSeparator = '/';
9141//const char kPathSeparatorString[] = "\\";
9142const char kAlternatePathSeparatorString[] = "/";
9143# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9144// Windows CE doesn't have a current directory. You should not use
9145// the current directory in tests on Windows CE, but this at least
9146// provides a reasonable fallback.
9147const char kCurrentDirectoryString[] = "\\";
9148// Windows CE doesn't define INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES
9149const DWORD kInvalidFileAttributes = 0xffffffff;
9150# else
9151const char kCurrentDirectoryString[] = ".\\";
9152# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9153#else
9154const char kPathSeparator = '/';
9155//const char kPathSeparatorString[] = "/";
9156const char kCurrentDirectoryString[] = "./";
9157#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9158
9159// Returns whether the given character is a valid path separator.
9160static bool IsPathSeparator(char c) {
9161#if GTEST_HAS_ALT_PATH_SEP_
9162 return (c == kPathSeparator) || (c == kAlternatePathSeparator);
9163#else
9164 return c == kPathSeparator;
9165#endif
9166}
9167
9168// Returns the current working directory, or "" if unsuccessful.
9169FilePath FilePath::GetCurrentDir() {
9170#if OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9171#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
9172 // Windows CE doesn't have a current directory, so we just return
9173 // something reasonable.
9174 return FilePath(kCurrentDirectoryString);
9175#elif GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9176 char cwd[GTEST_PATH_MAX_ + 1] = { '\0' };
9177 return FilePath(_getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd)) == NULL ? "" : cwd);
9178#else
9179 char cwd[GTEST_PATH_MAX_ + 1] = { '\0' };
9180 char* result = getcwd(cwd, sizeof(cwd));
9181# if GTEST_OS_NACL
9182 // getcwd will likely fail in NaCl due to the sandbox, so return something
9183 // reasonable. The user may have provided a shim implementation for getcwd,
9184 // however, so fallback only when failure is detected.
9185 return FilePath(result == NULL ? kCurrentDirectoryString : cwd);
9186# endif // GTEST_OS_NACL
9187 return FilePath(result == NULL ? "" : cwd);
9188#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9189#else // OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9190 return FilePath("");
9191#endif // OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9192}
9193
9194// Returns a copy of the FilePath with the case-insensitive extension removed.
9195// Example: FilePath("dir/file.exe").RemoveExtension("EXE") returns
9196// FilePath("dir/file"). If a case-insensitive extension is not
9197// found, returns a copy of the original FilePath.
9198FilePath FilePath::RemoveExtension(const char* extension) const {
9199 const std::string dot_extension = std::string(".") + extension;
9200 if (String::EndsWithCaseInsensitive(pathname_, dot_extension)) {
9201 return FilePath(pathname_.substr(
9202 0, pathname_.length() - dot_extension.length()));
9203 }
9204 return *this;
9205}
9206
9207// Returns a pointer to the last occurrence of a valid path separator in
9208// the FilePath. On Windows, for example, both '/' and '\' are valid path
9209// separators. Returns NULL if no path separator was found.
9210const char* FilePath::FindLastPathSeparator() const {
9211 const char* const last_sep = strrchr(c_str(), kPathSeparator);
9212#if GTEST_HAS_ALT_PATH_SEP_
9213 const char* const last_alt_sep = strrchr(c_str(), kAlternatePathSeparator);
9214 // Comparing two pointers of which only one is NULL is undefined.
9215 if (last_alt_sep != NULL &&
9216 (last_sep == NULL || last_alt_sep > last_sep)) {
9217 return last_alt_sep;
9218 }
9219#endif
9220 return last_sep;
9221}
9222
9223// Returns a copy of the FilePath with the directory part removed.
9224// Example: FilePath("path/to/file").RemoveDirectoryName() returns
9225// FilePath("file"). If there is no directory part ("just_a_file"), it returns
9226// the FilePath unmodified. If there is no file part ("just_a_dir/") it
9227// returns an empty FilePath ("").
9228// On Windows platform, '\' is the path separator, otherwise it is '/'.
9229FilePath FilePath::RemoveDirectoryName() const {
9230 const char* const last_sep = FindLastPathSeparator();
9231 return last_sep ? FilePath(last_sep + 1) : *this;
9232}
9233
9234// RemoveFileName returns the directory path with the filename removed.
9235// Example: FilePath("path/to/file").RemoveFileName() returns "path/to/".
9236// If the FilePath is "a_file" or "/a_file", RemoveFileName returns
9237// FilePath("./") or, on Windows, FilePath(".\\"). If the filepath does
9238// not have a file, like "just/a/dir/", it returns the FilePath unmodified.
9239// On Windows platform, '\' is the path separator, otherwise it is '/'.
9240FilePath FilePath::RemoveFileName() const {
9241 const char* const last_sep = FindLastPathSeparator();
9242 std::string dir;
9243 if (last_sep) {
9244 dir = std::string(c_str(), last_sep + 1 - c_str());
9245 } else {
9246 dir = kCurrentDirectoryString;
9247 }
9248 return FilePath(dir);
9249}
9250
9251// Helper functions for naming files in a directory for xml output.
9252
9253// Given directory = "dir", base_name = "test", number = 0,
9254// extension = "xml", returns "dir/test.xml". If number is greater
9255// than zero (e.g., 12), returns "dir/test_12.xml".
9256// On Windows platform, uses \ as the separator rather than /.
9257FilePath FilePath::MakeFileName(const FilePath& directory,
9258 const FilePath& base_name,
9259 int number,
9260 const char* extension) {
9261 std::string file;
9262 if (number == 0) {
9263 file = base_name.string() + "." + extension;
9264 } else {
9265 file = base_name.string() + "_" + StreamableToString(number)
9266 + "." + extension;
9267 }
9268 return ConcatPaths(directory, FilePath(file));
9269}
9270
9271// Given directory = "dir", relative_path = "test.xml", returns "dir/test.xml".
9272// On Windows, uses \ as the separator rather than /.
9273FilePath FilePath::ConcatPaths(const FilePath& directory,
9274 const FilePath& relative_path) {
9275 if (directory.IsEmpty())
9276 return relative_path;
9277 const FilePath dir(directory.RemoveTrailingPathSeparator());
9278 return FilePath(dir.string() + kPathSeparator + relative_path.string());
9279}
9280
9281// Returns true if pathname describes something findable in the file-system,
9282// either a file, directory, or whatever.
9283bool FilePath::FileOrDirectoryExists() const {
9284#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9285 LPCWSTR unicode = String::AnsiToUtf16(pathname_.c_str());
9286 const DWORD attributes = GetFileAttributes(unicode);
9287 delete [] unicode;
9288 return attributes != kInvalidFileAttributes;
9289#else
9290 posix::StatStruct file_stat;
9291 return posix::Stat(pathname_.c_str(), &file_stat) == 0;
9292#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9293}
9294
9295// Returns true if pathname describes a directory in the file-system
9296// that exists.
9297bool FilePath::DirectoryExists() const {
9298 bool result = false;
9299#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9300 // Don't strip off trailing separator if path is a root directory on
9301 // Windows (like "C:\\").
9302 const FilePath& path(IsRootDirectory() ? *this :
9303 RemoveTrailingPathSeparator());
9304#else
9305 const FilePath& path(*this);
9306#endif
9307
9308#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9309 LPCWSTR unicode = String::AnsiToUtf16(path.c_str());
9310 const DWORD attributes = GetFileAttributes(unicode);
9311 delete [] unicode;
9312 if ((attributes != kInvalidFileAttributes) &&
9313 (attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY)) {
9314 result = true;
9315 }
9316#else
9317 posix::StatStruct file_stat;
9318 result = posix::Stat(path.c_str(), &file_stat) == 0 &&
9319 posix::IsDir(file_stat);
9320#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9321
9322 return result;
9323}
9324
9325// Returns true if pathname describes a root directory. (Windows has one
9326// root directory per disk drive.)
9327bool FilePath::IsRootDirectory() const {
9328#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9329 // FIXME: on Windows a network share like
9330 // \\server\share can be a root directory, although it cannot be the
9331 // current directory. Handle this properly.
9332 return pathname_.length() == 3 && IsAbsolutePath();
9333#else
9334 return pathname_.length() == 1 && IsPathSeparator(pathname_.c_str()[0]);
9335#endif
9336}
9337
9338// Returns true if pathname describes an absolute path.
9339bool FilePath::IsAbsolutePath() const {
9340 const char* const name = pathname_.c_str();
9341#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9342 return pathname_.length() >= 3 &&
9343 ((name[0] >= 'a' && name[0] <= 'z') ||
9344 (name[0] >= 'A' && name[0] <= 'Z')) &&
9345 name[1] == ':' &&
9346 IsPathSeparator(name[2]);
9347#else
9348 return IsPathSeparator(name[0]);
9349#endif
9350}
9351
9352// Returns a pathname for a file that does not currently exist. The pathname
9353// will be directory/base_name.extension or
9354// directory/base_name_<number>.extension if directory/base_name.extension
9355// already exists. The number will be incremented until a pathname is found
9356// that does not already exist.
9357// Examples: 'dir/foo_test.xml' or 'dir/foo_test_1.xml'.
9358// There could be a race condition if two or more processes are calling this
9359// function at the same time -- they could both pick the same filename.
9360FilePath FilePath::GenerateUniqueFileName(const FilePath& directory,
9361 const FilePath& base_name,
9362 const char* extension) {
9363 FilePath full_pathname;
9364 int number = 0;
9365 do {
9366 full_pathname.Set(MakeFileName(directory, base_name, number++, extension));
9367 } while (full_pathname.FileOrDirectoryExists());
9368 return full_pathname;
9369}
9370
9371// Returns true if FilePath ends with a path separator, which indicates that
9372// it is intended to represent a directory. Returns false otherwise.
9373// This does NOT check that a directory (or file) actually exists.
9374bool FilePath::IsDirectory() const {
9375 return !pathname_.empty() &&
9376 IsPathSeparator(pathname_.c_str()[pathname_.length() - 1]);
9377}
9378
9379// Create directories so that path exists. Returns true if successful or if
9380// the directories already exist; returns false if unable to create directories
9381// for any reason.
9382bool FilePath::CreateDirectoriesRecursively() const {
9383 if (!this->IsDirectory()) {
9384 return false;
9385 }
9386
9387 if (pathname_.length() == 0 || this->DirectoryExists()) {
9388 return true;
9389 }
9390
9391 const FilePath parent(this->RemoveTrailingPathSeparator().RemoveFileName());
9392 return parent.CreateDirectoriesRecursively() && this->CreateFolder();
9393}
9394
9395// Create the directory so that path exists. Returns true if successful or
9396// if the directory already exists; returns false if unable to create the
9397// directory for any reason, including if the parent directory does not
9398// exist. Not named "CreateDirectory" because that's a macro on Windows.
9399bool FilePath::CreateFolder() const {
9400#if OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9401#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9402 FilePath removed_sep(this->RemoveTrailingPathSeparator());
9403 LPCWSTR unicode = String::AnsiToUtf16(removed_sep.c_str());
9404 int result = CreateDirectory(unicode, NULL) ? 0 : -1;
9405 delete [] unicode;
9406#elif GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
9407 int result = _mkdir(pathname_.c_str());
9408#else
9409 int result = mkdir(pathname_.c_str(), 0777);
9410#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
9411
9412 if (result == -1) {
9413 return this->DirectoryExists(); // An error is OK if the directory exists.
9414 }
9415 return true; // No error.
9416#else // OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9417 return false;
9418#endif // OPENCV_HAVE_FILESYSTEM_SUPPORT
9419}
9420
9421// If input name has a trailing separator character, remove it and return the
9422// name, otherwise return the name string unmodified.
9423// On Windows platform, uses \ as the separator, other platforms use /.
9424FilePath FilePath::RemoveTrailingPathSeparator() const {
9425 return IsDirectory()
9426 ? FilePath(pathname_.substr(0, pathname_.length() - 1))
9427 : *this;
9428}
9429
9430// Removes any redundant separators that might be in the pathname.
9431// For example, "bar///foo" becomes "bar/foo". Does not eliminate other
9432// redundancies that might be in a pathname involving "." or "..".
9433// FIXME: handle Windows network shares (e.g. \\server\share).
9434void FilePath::Normalize() {
9435 if (pathname_.c_str() == NULL) {
9436 pathname_ = "";
9437 return;
9438 }
9439 const char* src = pathname_.c_str();
9440 char* const dest = new char[pathname_.length() + 1];
9441 char* dest_ptr = dest;
9442 memset(dest_ptr, 0, pathname_.length() + 1);
9443
9444 while (*src != '\0') {
9445 *dest_ptr = *src;
9446 if (!IsPathSeparator(*src)) {
9447 src++;
9448 } else {
9449#if GTEST_HAS_ALT_PATH_SEP_
9450 if (*dest_ptr == kAlternatePathSeparator) {
9451 *dest_ptr = kPathSeparator;
9452 }
9453#endif
9454 while (IsPathSeparator(*src))
9455 src++;
9456 }
9457 dest_ptr++;
9458 }
9459 *dest_ptr = '\0';
9460 pathname_ = dest;
9461 delete[] dest;
9462}

9549namespace {
9550template <typename T>
9551T ReadProcFileField(const std::string& filename, int field) {
9552 std::string dummy;
9553 std::ifstream file(filename.c_str());
9554 while (field-- > 0) {
9555 file >> dummy;
9556 }
9557 T output = 0;
9558 file >> output;
9559 return output;
9560}

9563// Returns the number of active threads, or 0 when there is an error.
9564size_t GetThreadCount() {
9565 const std::string filename =
9566 (Message() << "/proc/" << getpid() << "/stat").GetString();
9567 return ReadProcFileField<int>(filename, 19);
9568}
9569
9570#elif GTEST_OS_MAC
9571
9572size_t GetThreadCount() {
9573 const task_t task = mach_task_self();
9574 mach_msg_type_number_t thread_count;
9575 thread_act_array_t thread_list;
9576 const kern_return_t status = task_threads(task, &thread_list, &thread_count);
9577 if (status == KERN_SUCCESS) {
9578 // task_threads allocates resources in thread_list and we need to free them
9579 // to avoid leaks.
9580 vm_deallocate(task,
9581 reinterpret_cast<vm_address_t>(thread_list),
9582 sizeof(thread_t) * thread_count);
9583 return static_cast<size_t>(thread_count);
9584 } else {
9585 return 0;
9586 }
9587}
9588
9589#elif GTEST_OS_QNX
9590
9591// Returns the number of threads running in the process, or 0 to indicate that
9592// we cannot detect it.
9593size_t GetThreadCount() {
9594 const int fd = open("/proc/self/as", O_RDONLY);
9595 if (fd < 0) {
9596 return 0;
9597 }
9598 procfs_info process_info;
9599 const int status =
9600 devctl(fd, DCMD_PROC_INFO, &process_info, sizeof(process_info), NULL);
9601 close(fd);
9602 if (status == EOK) {
9603 return static_cast<size_t>(process_info.num_threads);
9604 } else {
9605 return 0;
9606 }
9607}
9608
9609#elif GTEST_OS_AIX
9610
9611size_t GetThreadCount() {
9612 struct procentry64 entry;
9613 pid_t pid = getpid();
9614 int status = getprocs64(&entry, sizeof(entry), NULL, 0, &pid, 1);
9615 if (status == 1) {
9616 return entry.pi_thcount;
9617 } else {
9618 return 0;
9619 }
9620}
9621
9622#elif GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
9623
9624size_t GetThreadCount() {
9625 int dummy_buffer;
9626 size_t avail;
9627 zx_status_t status = zx_object_get_info(
9628 zx_process_self(),
9629 ZX_INFO_PROCESS_THREADS,
9630 &dummy_buffer,
9631 0,
9632 nullptr,
9633 &avail);
9634 if (status == ZX_OK) {
9635 return avail;
9636 } else {
9637 return 0;
9638 }
9639}
9640
9641#else
9642
9643size_t GetThreadCount() {
9644 // There's no portable way to detect the number of threads, so we just
9645 // return 0 to indicate that we cannot detect it.
9646 return 0;
9647}

9649#endif // GTEST_OS_LINUX

9675void AutoHandle::Reset(HANDLE handle) {
9676 // Resetting with the same handle we already own is invalid.

9681 handle_ = handle;

9685 "and thus not allowed.";

9712Mutex::Mutex()
9713 : owner_thread_id_(0),
9714 type_(kDynamic),
9715 critical_section_init_phase_(0),
9716 critical_section_(new CRITICAL_SECTION) {
9717 ::InitializeCriticalSection(critical_section_);
9718}
9719
9720Mutex::~Mutex() {
9721 // Static mutexes are leaked intentionally. It is not thread-safe to try
9722 // to clean them up.
9723 // FIXME: Switch to Slim Reader/Writer (SRW) Locks, which requires
9724 // nothing to clean it up but is available only on Vista and later.
9725 // https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/Sync/slim-reader-writer--srw--locks
9726 if (type_ == kDynamic) {
9727 ::DeleteCriticalSection(critical_section_);
9728 delete critical_section_;
9729 critical_section_ = NULL;
9730 }
9731}
9732
9733void Mutex::Lock() {
9734 ThreadSafeLazyInit();
9735 ::EnterCriticalSection(critical_section_);
9736 owner_thread_id_ = ::GetCurrentThreadId();
9737}
9738
9739void Mutex::Unlock() {
9740 ThreadSafeLazyInit();
9741 // We don't protect writing to owner_thread_id_ here, as it's the
9742 // caller's responsibility to ensure that the current thread holds the
9743 // mutex when this is called.
9744 owner_thread_id_ = 0;
9745 ::LeaveCriticalSection(critical_section_);
9746}
9747
9748// Does nothing if the current thread holds the mutex. Otherwise, crashes
9749// with high probability.
9750void Mutex::AssertHeld() {
9751 ThreadSafeLazyInit();
9752 GTEST_CHECK_(owner_thread_id_ == ::GetCurrentThreadId())
9753 << "The current thread is not holding the mutex @" << this;
9754}

9756namespace {
9757
9758// Use the RAII idiom to flag mem allocs that are intentionally never
9759// deallocated. The motivation is to silence the false positive mem leaks
9760// that are reported by the debug version of MS's CRT which can only detect
9761// if an alloc is missing a matching deallocation.
9762// Example:
9763// MemoryIsNotDeallocated memory_is_not_deallocated;
9764// critical_section_ = new CRITICAL_SECTION;
9765//
9766class MemoryIsNotDeallocated
9767{
9768 public:
9769 MemoryIsNotDeallocated() : old_crtdbg_flag_(0) {
9770#ifdef _MSC_VER
9771 old_crtdbg_flag_ = _CrtSetDbgFlag(_CRTDBG_REPORT_FLAG);
9772 // Set heap allocation block type to _IGNORE_BLOCK so that MS debug CRT
9773 // doesn't report mem leak if there's no matching deallocation.
9774 _CrtSetDbgFlag(old_crtdbg_flag_ & ~_CRTDBG_ALLOC_MEM_DF);
9775#endif // _MSC_VER
9776 }
9777
9778 ~MemoryIsNotDeallocated() {
9779#ifdef _MSC_VER
9780 // Restore the original _CRTDBG_ALLOC_MEM_DF flag
9781 _CrtSetDbgFlag(old_crtdbg_flag_);
9782#endif // _MSC_VER
9783 }
9784
9785 private:
9786 int old_crtdbg_flag_;
9787
9788 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(MemoryIsNotDeallocated);
9789};
9790
9791} // namespace
9792
9793// Initializes owner_thread_id_ and critical_section_ in static mutexes.
9794void Mutex::ThreadSafeLazyInit() {
9795 // Dynamic mutexes are initialized in the constructor.
9796 if (type_ == kStatic) {
9797 switch (
9798 ::InterlockedCompareExchange(&critical_section_init_phase_, 1L, 0L)) {
9799 case 0:
9800 // If critical_section_init_phase_ was 0 before the exchange, we
9801 // are the first to test it and need to perform the initialization.
9802 owner_thread_id_ = 0;
9803 {
9804 // Use RAII to flag that following mem alloc is never deallocated.
9805 MemoryIsNotDeallocated memory_is_not_deallocated;
9806 critical_section_ = new CRITICAL_SECTION;
9807 }
9808 ::InitializeCriticalSection(critical_section_);
9809 // Updates the critical_section_init_phase_ to 2 to signal
9810 // initialization complete.
9811 GTEST_CHECK_(::InterlockedCompareExchange(
9812 &critical_section_init_phase_, 2L, 1L) ==
9813 1L);
9814 break;
9815 case 1:
9816 // Somebody else is already initializing the mutex; spin until they
9817 // are done.
9818 while (::InterlockedCompareExchange(&critical_section_init_phase_,
9819 2L,
9820 2L) != 2L) {
9821 // Possibly yields the rest of the thread's time slice to other
9822 // threads.
9823 ::Sleep(0);
9824 }
9825 break;
9826
9827 case 2:
9828 break; // The mutex is already initialized and ready for use.
9829
9830 default:
9831 GTEST_CHECK_(false)
9832 << "Unexpected value of critical_section_init_phase_ "
9833 << "while initializing a static mutex.";
9834 }
9835 }
9836}

9840class ThreadWithParamSupport : public ThreadWithParamBase {
9841 public:
9842 static HANDLE CreateThread(Runnable* runnable,
9843 Notification* thread_can_start) {
9844 ThreadMainParam* param = new ThreadMainParam(runnable, thread_can_start);
9845 DWORD thread_id;
9846 // FIXME: Consider to use _beginthreadex instead.
9847 HANDLE thread_handle = ::CreateThread(
9848 NULL, // Default security.
9849 0, // Default stack size.
9850 &ThreadWithParamSupport::ThreadMain,
9851 param, // Parameter to ThreadMainStatic
9852 0x0, // Default creation flags.
9853 &thread_id); // Need a valid pointer for the call to work under Win98.
9854 GTEST_CHECK_(thread_handle != NULL) << "CreateThread failed with error "
9855 << ::GetLastError() << ".";
9856 if (thread_handle == NULL) {
9857 delete param;
9858 }
9859 return thread_handle;
9860 }
9861
9862 private:
9863 struct ThreadMainParam {
9864 ThreadMainParam(Runnable* runnable, Notification* thread_can_start)
9865 : runnable_(runnable),
9866 thread_can_start_(thread_can_start) {
9867 }
9868 scoped_ptr<Runnable> runnable_;
9869 // Does not own.
9870 Notification* thread_can_start_;
9871 };
9872
9873 static DWORD WINAPI ThreadMain(void* ptr) {
9874 // Transfers ownership.
9875 scoped_ptr<ThreadMainParam> param(static_cast<ThreadMainParam*>(ptr));
9876 if (param->thread_can_start_ != NULL)
9877 param->thread_can_start_->WaitForNotification();
9878 param->runnable_->Run();
9879 return 0;
9880 }
9881
9882 // Prohibit instantiation.
9883 ThreadWithParamSupport();
9884
9885 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ThreadWithParamSupport);
9886};

9888} // namespace

9900void ThreadWithParamBase::Join() {

9902 << "Failed to join the thread with error " << ::GetLastError() << ".";

9904
9905// Maps a thread to a set of ThreadIdToThreadLocals that have values
9906// instantiated on that thread and notifies them when the thread exits. A
9907// ThreadLocal instance is expected to persist until all threads it has
9908// values on have terminated.
9909class ThreadLocalRegistryImpl {
9910 public:
9911 // Registers thread_local_instance as having value on the current thread.
9912 // Returns a value that can be used to identify the thread from other threads.
9913 static ThreadLocalValueHolderBase* GetValueOnCurrentThread(
9914 const ThreadLocalBase* thread_local_instance) {
9915 DWORD current_thread = ::GetCurrentThreadId();
9916 MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
9917 ThreadIdToThreadLocals* const thread_to_thread_locals =
9918 GetThreadLocalsMapLocked();
9919 ThreadIdToThreadLocals::iterator thread_local_pos =
9920 thread_to_thread_locals->find(current_thread);
9921 if (thread_local_pos == thread_to_thread_locals->end()) {
9922 thread_local_pos = thread_to_thread_locals->insert(
9923 std::make_pair(current_thread, ThreadLocalValues())).first;
9924 StartWatcherThreadFor(current_thread);
9925 }
9926 ThreadLocalValues& thread_local_values = thread_local_pos->second;
9927 ThreadLocalValues::iterator value_pos =
9928 thread_local_values.find(thread_local_instance);
9929 if (value_pos == thread_local_values.end()) {
9930 value_pos =
9931 thread_local_values
9932 .insert(std::make_pair(
9933 thread_local_instance,
9934 linked_ptr<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase>(
9935 thread_local_instance->NewValueForCurrentThread())))
9936 .first;
9937 }
9938 return value_pos->second.get();
9939 }
9940
9941 static void OnThreadLocalDestroyed(
9942 const ThreadLocalBase* thread_local_instance) {
9943 std::vector<linked_ptr<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase> > value_holders;
9944 // Clean up the ThreadLocalValues data structure while holding the lock, but
9945 // defer the destruction of the ThreadLocalValueHolderBases.
9946 {
9947 MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
9948 ThreadIdToThreadLocals* const thread_to_thread_locals =
9949 GetThreadLocalsMapLocked();
9950 for (ThreadIdToThreadLocals::iterator it =
9951 thread_to_thread_locals->begin();
9952 it != thread_to_thread_locals->end();
9953 ++it) {
9954 ThreadLocalValues& thread_local_values = it->second;
9955 ThreadLocalValues::iterator value_pos =
9956 thread_local_values.find(thread_local_instance);
9957 if (value_pos != thread_local_values.end()) {
9958 value_holders.push_back(value_pos->second);
9959 thread_local_values.erase(value_pos);
9960 // This 'if' can only be successful at most once, so theoretically we
9961 // could break out of the loop here, but we don't bother doing so.
9962 }
9963 }
9964 }
9965 // Outside the lock, let the destructor for 'value_holders' deallocate the
9966 // ThreadLocalValueHolderBases.
9967 }
9968
9969 static void OnThreadExit(DWORD thread_id) {
9970 GTEST_CHECK_(thread_id != 0) << ::GetLastError();
9971 std::vector<linked_ptr<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase> > value_holders;
9972 // Clean up the ThreadIdToThreadLocals data structure while holding the
9973 // lock, but defer the destruction of the ThreadLocalValueHolderBases.
9974 {
9975 MutexLock lock(&mutex_);
9976 ThreadIdToThreadLocals* const thread_to_thread_locals =
9977 GetThreadLocalsMapLocked();
9978 ThreadIdToThreadLocals::iterator thread_local_pos =
9979 thread_to_thread_locals->find(thread_id);
9980 if (thread_local_pos != thread_to_thread_locals->end()) {
9981 ThreadLocalValues& thread_local_values = thread_local_pos->second;
9982 for (ThreadLocalValues::iterator value_pos =
9983 thread_local_values.begin();
9984 value_pos != thread_local_values.end();
9985 ++value_pos) {
9986 value_holders.push_back(value_pos->second);
9987 }
9988 thread_to_thread_locals->erase(thread_local_pos);
9989 }
9990 }
9991 // Outside the lock, let the destructor for 'value_holders' deallocate the
9992 // ThreadLocalValueHolderBases.
9993 }
9994
9995 private:
9996 // In a particular thread, maps a ThreadLocal object to its value.
9997 typedef std::map<const ThreadLocalBase*,
9998 linked_ptr<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase> > ThreadLocalValues;
9999 // Stores all ThreadIdToThreadLocals having values in a thread, indexed by
10000 // thread's ID.
10001 typedef std::map<DWORD, ThreadLocalValues> ThreadIdToThreadLocals;
10002
10003 // Holds the thread id and thread handle that we pass from
10004 // StartWatcherThreadFor to WatcherThreadFunc.
10005 typedef std::pair<DWORD, HANDLE> ThreadIdAndHandle;
10006
10007 static void StartWatcherThreadFor(DWORD thread_id) {
10008 // The returned handle will be kept in thread_map and closed by
10009 // watcher_thread in WatcherThreadFunc.
10010 HANDLE thread = ::OpenThread(SYNCHRONIZE | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION,
10011 FALSE,
10012 thread_id);
10013 GTEST_CHECK_(thread != NULL);
10014 // We need to pass a valid thread ID pointer into CreateThread for it
10015 // to work correctly under Win98.
10016 DWORD watcher_thread_id;
10017 HANDLE watcher_thread = ::CreateThread(
10018 NULL, // Default security.
10019 0, // Default stack size
10020 &ThreadLocalRegistryImpl::WatcherThreadFunc,
10021 reinterpret_cast<LPVOID>(new ThreadIdAndHandle(thread_id, thread)),
10022 CREATE_SUSPENDED,
10023 &watcher_thread_id);
10024 GTEST_CHECK_(watcher_thread != NULL);
10025 // Give the watcher thread the same priority as ours to avoid being
10026 // blocked by it.
10027 ::SetThreadPriority(watcher_thread,
10028 ::GetThreadPriority(::GetCurrentThread()));
10029 ::ResumeThread(watcher_thread);
10030 ::CloseHandle(watcher_thread);
10031 }
10032
10033 // Monitors exit from a given thread and notifies those
10034 // ThreadIdToThreadLocals about thread termination.
10035 static DWORD WINAPI WatcherThreadFunc(LPVOID param) {
10036 const ThreadIdAndHandle* tah =
10037 reinterpret_cast<const ThreadIdAndHandle*>(param);
10038 GTEST_CHECK_(
10039 ::WaitForSingleObject(tah->second, INFINITE) == WAIT_OBJECT_0);
10040 OnThreadExit(tah->first);
10041 ::CloseHandle(tah->second);
10042 delete tah;
10043 return 0;
10044 }
10045
10046 // Returns map of thread local instances.
10047 static ThreadIdToThreadLocals* GetThreadLocalsMapLocked() {
10048 mutex_.AssertHeld();
10049 MemoryIsNotDeallocated memory_is_not_deallocated;
10050 static ThreadIdToThreadLocals* map = new ThreadIdToThreadLocals();
10051 return map;
10052 }
10053
10054 // Protects access to GetThreadLocalsMapLocked() and its return value.
10055 static Mutex mutex_;
10056 // Protects access to GetThreadMapLocked() and its return value.
10057 static Mutex thread_map_mutex_;
10058};
10059
10060Mutex ThreadLocalRegistryImpl::mutex_(Mutex::kStaticMutex);
10061Mutex ThreadLocalRegistryImpl::thread_map_mutex_(Mutex::kStaticMutex);
10062
10063ThreadLocalValueHolderBase* ThreadLocalRegistry::GetValueOnCurrentThread(
10064 const ThreadLocalBase* thread_local_instance) {
10065 return ThreadLocalRegistryImpl::GetValueOnCurrentThread(
10066 thread_local_instance);
10067}
10068
10069void ThreadLocalRegistry::OnThreadLocalDestroyed(
10070 const ThreadLocalBase* thread_local_instance) {
10071 ThreadLocalRegistryImpl::OnThreadLocalDestroyed(thread_local_instance);
10072}

10076#if GTEST_USES_POSIX_RE
10077
10078// Implements RE. Currently only needed for death tests.
10079
10080RE::~RE() {
10081 if (is_valid_) {
10082 // regfree'ing an invalid regex might crash because the content
10083 // of the regex is undefined. Since the regex's are essentially
10084 // the same, one cannot be valid (or invalid) without the other
10085 // being so too.
10086 regfree(&partial_regex_);
10087 regfree(&full_regex_);
10088 }
10089 free(const_cast<char*>(pattern_));
10090}
10091
10092// Returns true iff regular expression re matches the entire str.
10093bool RE::FullMatch(const char* str, const RE& re) {
10094 if (!re.is_valid_) return false;
10095
10096 regmatch_t match;
10097 return regexec(&re.full_regex_, str, 1, &match, 0) == 0;
10098}
10099
10100// Returns true iff regular expression re matches a substring of str
10101// (including str itself).
10102bool RE::PartialMatch(const char* str, const RE& re) {
10103 if (!re.is_valid_) return false;
10104
10105 regmatch_t match;
10106 return regexec(&re.partial_regex_, str, 1, &match, 0) == 0;
10107}
10108
10109// Initializes an RE from its string representation.
10110void RE::Init(const char* regex) {
10111 pattern_ = posix::StrDup(regex);
10112
10113 // Reserves enough bytes to hold the regular expression used for a
10114 // full match.
10115 const size_t full_regex_len = strlen(regex) + 10;
10116 char* const full_pattern = new char[full_regex_len];
10117
10118 snprintf(full_pattern, full_regex_len, "^(%s)$", regex);
10119 is_valid_ = regcomp(&full_regex_, full_pattern, REG_EXTENDED) == 0;
10120 // We want to call regcomp(&partial_regex_, ...) even if the
10121 // previous expression returns false. Otherwise partial_regex_ may
10122 // not be properly initialized can may cause trouble when it's
10123 // freed.
10124 //
10125 // Some implementation of POSIX regex (e.g. on at least some
10126 // versions of Cygwin) doesn't accept the empty string as a valid
10127 // regex. We change it to an equivalent form "()" to be safe.
10128 if (is_valid_) {
10129 const char* const partial_regex = (*regex == '\0') ? "()" : regex;
10130 is_valid_ = regcomp(&partial_regex_, partial_regex, REG_EXTENDED) == 0;
10131 }
10132 EXPECT_TRUE(is_valid_)
10133 << "Regular expression \"" << regex
10134 << "\" is not a valid POSIX Extended regular expression.";
10135
10136 delete[] full_pattern;
10137}
10138
10139#elif GTEST_USES_SIMPLE_RE
10140
10141// Returns true iff ch appears anywhere in str (excluding the
10142// terminating '\0' character).
10143bool IsInSet(char ch, const char* str) {
10144 return ch != '\0' && strchr(str, ch) != NULL;
10145}
10146
10147// Returns true iff ch belongs to the given classification. Unlike
10148// similar functions in <ctype.h>, these aren't affected by the
10149// current locale.
10150bool IsAsciiDigit(char ch) { return '0' <= ch && ch <= '9'; }
10151bool IsAsciiPunct(char ch) {
10152 return IsInSet(ch, "^-!\"#$%&'()*+,./:;<=>?@[\\]_`{|}~");
10153}
10154bool IsRepeat(char ch) { return IsInSet(ch, "?*+"); }
10155bool IsAsciiWhiteSpace(char ch) { return IsInSet(ch, " \f\n\r\t\v"); }
10156bool IsAsciiWordChar(char ch) {
10157 return ('a' <= ch && ch <= 'z') || ('A' <= ch && ch <= 'Z') ||
10158 ('0' <= ch && ch <= '9') || ch == '_';
10159}
10160
10161// Returns true iff "\\c" is a supported escape sequence.
10162bool IsValidEscape(char c) {
10163 return (IsAsciiPunct(c) || IsInSet(c, "dDfnrsStvwW"));
10164}
10165
10166// Returns true iff the given atom (specified by escaped and pattern)
10167// matches ch. The result is undefined if the atom is invalid.
10168bool AtomMatchesChar(bool escaped, char pattern_char, char ch) {
10169 if (escaped) { // "\\p" where p is pattern_char.
10170 switch (pattern_char) {
10171 case 'd': return IsAsciiDigit(ch);
10172 case 'D': return !IsAsciiDigit(ch);
10173 case 'f': return ch == '\f';
10174 case 'n': return ch == '\n';
10175 case 'r': return ch == '\r';
10176 case 's': return IsAsciiWhiteSpace(ch);
10177 case 'S': return !IsAsciiWhiteSpace(ch);
10178 case 't': return ch == '\t';
10179 case 'v': return ch == '\v';
10180 case 'w': return IsAsciiWordChar(ch);
10181 case 'W': return !IsAsciiWordChar(ch);
10182 }
10183 return IsAsciiPunct(pattern_char) && pattern_char == ch;
10184 }
10185
10186 return (pattern_char == '.' && ch != '\n') || pattern_char == ch;
10187}
10188
10189// Helper function used by ValidateRegex() to format error messages.
10190static std::string FormatRegexSyntaxError(const char* regex, int index) {
10191 return (Message() << "Syntax error at index " << index
10192 << " in simple regular expression \"" << regex << "\": ").GetString();
10193}
10194
10195// Generates non-fatal failures and returns false if regex is invalid;
10196// otherwise returns true.
10197bool ValidateRegex(const char* regex) {
10198 if (regex == NULL) {
10199 // FIXME: fix the source file location in the
10200 // assertion failures to match where the regex is used in user
10201 // code.
10202 ADD_FAILURE() << "NULL is not a valid simple regular expression.";
10203 return false;
10204 }
10205
10206 bool is_valid = true;
10207
10208 // True iff ?, *, or + can follow the previous atom.
10209 bool prev_repeatable = false;
10210 for (int i = 0; regex[i]; i++) {
10211 if (regex[i] == '\\') { // An escape sequence
10212 i++;
10213 if (regex[i] == '\0') {
10214 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i - 1)
10215 << "'\\' cannot appear at the end.";
10216 return false;
10217 }
10218
10219 if (!IsValidEscape(regex[i])) {
10220 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i - 1)
10221 << "invalid escape sequence \"\\" << regex[i] << "\".";
10222 is_valid = false;
10223 }
10224 prev_repeatable = true;
10225 } else { // Not an escape sequence.
10226 const char ch = regex[i];
10227
10228 if (ch == '^' && i > 0) {
10229 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i)
10230 << "'^' can only appear at the beginning.";
10231 is_valid = false;
10232 } else if (ch == '$' && regex[i + 1] != '\0') {
10233 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i)
10234 << "'$' can only appear at the end.";
10235 is_valid = false;
10236 } else if (IsInSet(ch, "()[]{}|")) {
10237 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i)
10238 << "'" << ch << "' is unsupported.";
10239 is_valid = false;
10240 } else if (IsRepeat(ch) && !prev_repeatable) {
10241 ADD_FAILURE() << FormatRegexSyntaxError(regex, i)
10242 << "'" << ch << "' can only follow a repeatable token.";
10243 is_valid = false;
10244 }
10245
10246 prev_repeatable = !IsInSet(ch, "^$?*+");
10247 }
10248 }
10249
10250 return is_valid;
10251}
10252
10253// Matches a repeated regex atom followed by a valid simple regular
10254// expression. The regex atom is defined as c if escaped is false,
10255// or \c otherwise. repeat is the repetition meta character (?, *,
10256// or +). The behavior is undefined if str contains too many
10257// characters to be indexable by size_t, in which case the test will
10258// probably time out anyway. We are fine with this limitation as
10259// std::string has it too.
10260bool MatchRepetitionAndRegexAtHead(
10261 bool escaped, char c, char repeat, const char* regex,
10262 const char* str) {
10263 const size_t min_count = (repeat == '+') ? 1 : 0;
10264 const size_t max_count = (repeat == '?') ? 1 :
10265 static_cast<size_t>(-1) - 1;
10266 // We cannot call numeric_limits::max() as it conflicts with the
10267 // max() macro on Windows.
10268
10269 for (size_t i = 0; i <= max_count; ++i) {
10270 // We know that the atom matches each of the first i characters in str.
10271 if (i >= min_count && MatchRegexAtHead(regex, str + i)) {
10272 // We have enough matches at the head, and the tail matches too.
10273 // Since we only care about *whether* the pattern matches str
10274 // (as opposed to *how* it matches), there is no need to find a
10275 // greedy match.
10276 return true;
10277 }
10278 if (str[i] == '\0' || !AtomMatchesChar(escaped, c, str[i]))
10279 return false;
10280 }
10281 return false;
10282}
10283
10284// Returns true iff regex matches a prefix of str. regex must be a
10285// valid simple regular expression and not start with "^", or the
10286// result is undefined.
10287bool MatchRegexAtHead(const char* regex, const char* str) {
10288 if (*regex == '\0') // An empty regex matches a prefix of anything.
10289 return true;
10290
10291 // "$" only matches the end of a string. Note that regex being
10292 // valid guarantees that there's nothing after "$" in it.
10293 if (*regex == '$')
10294 return *str == '\0';
10295
10296 // Is the first thing in regex an escape sequence?
10297 const bool escaped = *regex == '\\';
10298 if (escaped)
10299 ++regex;
10300 if (IsRepeat(regex[1])) {
10301 // MatchRepetitionAndRegexAtHead() calls MatchRegexAtHead(), so
10302 // here's an indirect recursion. It terminates as the regex gets
10303 // shorter in each recursion.
10304 return MatchRepetitionAndRegexAtHead(
10305 escaped, regex[0], regex[1], regex + 2, str);
10306 } else {
10307 // regex isn't empty, isn't "$", and doesn't start with a
10308 // repetition. We match the first atom of regex with the first
10309 // character of str and recurse.
10310 return (*str != '\0') && AtomMatchesChar(escaped, *regex, *str) &&
10311 MatchRegexAtHead(regex + 1, str + 1);
10312 }
10313}
10314
10315// Returns true iff regex matches any substring of str. regex must be
10316// a valid simple regular expression, or the result is undefined.
10317//
10318// The algorithm is recursive, but the recursion depth doesn't exceed
10319// the regex length, so we won't need to worry about running out of
10320// stack space normally. In rare cases the time complexity can be
10321// exponential with respect to the regex length + the string length,
10322// but usually it's must faster (often close to linear).
10323bool MatchRegexAnywhere(const char* regex, const char* str) {
10324 if (regex == NULL || str == NULL)
10325 return false;
10326
10327 if (*regex == '^')
10328 return MatchRegexAtHead(regex + 1, str);
10329
10330 // A successful match can be anywhere in str.
10331 do {
10332 if (MatchRegexAtHead(regex, str))
10333 return true;
10334 } while (*str++ != '\0');
10335 return false;
10336}
10337
10338// Implements the RE class.
10339
10340RE::~RE() {
10341 free(const_cast<char*>(pattern_));
10342 free(const_cast<char*>(full_pattern_));
10343}
10344
10345// Returns true iff regular expression re matches the entire str.
10346bool RE::FullMatch(const char* str, const RE& re) {
10347 return re.is_valid_ && MatchRegexAnywhere(re.full_pattern_, str);
10348}
10349
10350// Returns true iff regular expression re matches a substring of str
10351// (including str itself).
10352bool RE::PartialMatch(const char* str, const RE& re) {
10353 return re.is_valid_ && MatchRegexAnywhere(re.pattern_, str);
10354}
10355
10356// Initializes an RE from its string representation.
10357void RE::Init(const char* regex) {
10358 pattern_ = full_pattern_ = NULL;
10359 if (regex != NULL) {
10360 pattern_ = posix::StrDup(regex);
10361 }
10362
10363 is_valid_ = ValidateRegex(regex);
10364 if (!is_valid_) {
10365 // No need to calculate the full pattern when the regex is invalid.
10366 return;
10367 }
10368
10369 const size_t len = strlen(regex);
10370 // Reserves enough bytes to hold the regular expression used for a
10371 // full match: we need space to prepend a '^', append a '$', and
10372 // terminate the string with '\0'.
10373 char* buffer = static_cast<char*>(malloc(len + 3));
10374 full_pattern_ = buffer;
10375
10376 if (*regex != '^')
10377 *buffer++ = '^'; // Makes sure full_pattern_ starts with '^'.
10378
10379 // We don't use snprintf or strncpy, as they trigger a warning when
10380 // compiled with VC++ 8.0.
10381 memcpy(buffer, regex, len);
10382 buffer += len;
10383
10384 if (len == 0 || regex[len - 1] != '$')
10385 *buffer++ = '$'; // Makes sure full_pattern_ ends with '$'.
10386
10387 *buffer = '\0';
10388}

10392const char kUnknownFile[] = "unknown file";
10393
10394// Formats a source file path and a line number as they would appear
10395// in an error message from the compiler used to compile this code.
10396GTEST_API_ ::std::string FormatFileLocation(const char* file, int line) {
10397 const std::string file_name(file == NULL ? kUnknownFile : file);
10398
10399 if (line < 0) {
10400 return file_name + ":";
10401 }
10402#ifdef _MSC_VER
10403 return file_name + "(" + StreamableToString(line) + "):";
10404#else
10405 return file_name + ":" + StreamableToString(line) + ":";
10406#endif // _MSC_VER
10407}
10408
10409// Formats a file location for compiler-independent XML output.
10410// Although this function is not platform dependent, we put it next to
10411// FormatFileLocation in order to contrast the two functions.
10412// Note that FormatCompilerIndependentFileLocation() does NOT append colon
10413// to the file location it produces, unlike FormatFileLocation().
10414GTEST_API_ ::std::string FormatCompilerIndependentFileLocation(
10415 const char* file, int line) {
10416 const std::string file_name(file == NULL ? kUnknownFile : file);
10417
10418 if (line < 0)
10419 return file_name;
10420 else
10421 return file_name + ":" + StreamableToString(line);
10422}

10424GTestLog::GTestLog(GTestLogSeverity severity, const char* file, int line)
10425 : severity_(severity) {
10426 const char* const marker =
10427 severity == GTEST_INFO ? "[ INFO ]" :
10428 severity == GTEST_WARNING ? "[WARNING]" :
10429 severity == GTEST_ERROR ? "[ ERROR ]" : "[ FATAL ]";
10430 GetStream() << ::std::endl << marker << " "
10431 << FormatFileLocation(file, line).c_str() << ": ";
10432}
10433
10434// Flushes the buffers and, if severity is GTEST_FATAL, aborts the program.
10435GTestLog::~GTestLog() {
10436 GetStream() << ::std::endl;
10437 if (severity_ == GTEST_FATAL) {
10438 fflush(stderr);
10439 posix::Abort();
10440 }
10441}

10449// Object that captures an output stream (stdout/stderr).
10450class CapturedStream {
10451 public:
10452 // The ctor redirects the stream to a temporary file.
10453 explicit CapturedStream(int fd) : fd_(fd), uncaptured_fd_(dup(fd)) {
10454# if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
10455 wchar_t temp_dir_path_w[MAX_PATH + 1] = { L'\0' };
10456 wchar_t temp_file_path_w[MAX_PATH + 1] = { L'\0' };
10457
10458 ::GetTempPathW(sizeof(temp_dir_path_w)/sizeof(wchar_t), temp_dir_path_w);
10459 // Convert to UTF-8 to support Unicode paths
10460 int len = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, temp_dir_path_w, -1, NULL, 0, NULL, NULL);
10461 std::string temp_dir_path;
10462 if (len > 0)
10463 {
10464 std::vector<char> utf8_buf(len);
10465 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, temp_dir_path_w, -1, utf8_buf.data(), len, NULL, NULL);
10466 temp_dir_path = std::string(utf8_buf.data());
10467 }
10468 const UINT success = ::GetTempFileNameW(temp_dir_path_w,
10469 L"gtest_redir",
10470 0, // Generate unique file name.
10471 temp_file_path_w);
10472 // Convert filename back to UTF-8
10473 std::string temp_file_path;
10474 int captured_fd = -1;
10475 if (success != 0)
10476 {
10477 len = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, temp_file_path_w, -1, NULL, 0, NULL, NULL);
10478 if (len > 0)
10479 {
10480 std::vector<char> utf8_buf(len);
10481 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, temp_file_path_w, -1, utf8_buf.data(), len, NULL, NULL);
10482 temp_file_path = std::string(utf8_buf.data());
10483 }
10484 // Create file and get fd for redirect
10485 captured_fd = _open(temp_file_path.c_str(), _O_CREAT | _O_WRONLY | _O_TRUNC, _S_IREAD | _S_IWRITE);
10486 GTEST_CHECK_(captured_fd != -1) << "Unable to open temporary file "
10487 << temp_file_path;
10488 filename_ = temp_file_path;
10489 }
10490# else
10491 // There's no guarantee that a test has write access to the current
10492 // directory, so we create the temporary file in the /tmp directory
10493 // instead. We use /tmp on most systems, and /sdcard on Android.
10494 // That's because Android doesn't have /tmp.
10495# if GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID
10496 // Note: Android applications are expected to call the framework's
10497 // Context.getExternalStorageDirectory() method through JNI to get
10498 // the location of the world-writable SD Card directory. However,
10499 // this requires a Context handle, which cannot be retrieved
10500 // globally from native code. Doing so also precludes running the
10501 // code as part of a regular standalone executable, which doesn't
10502 // run in a Dalvik process (e.g. when running it through 'adb shell').
10503 //
10504 // The location /sdcard is directly accessible from native code
10505 // and is the only location (unofficially) supported by the Android
10506 // team. It's generally a symlink to the real SD Card mount point
10507 // which can be /mnt/sdcard, /mnt/sdcard0, /system/media/sdcard, or
10508 // other OEM-customized locations. Never rely on these, and always
10509 // use /sdcard.
10510 char name_template[] = "/sdcard/gtest_captured_stream.XXXXXX";
10511# else
10512 char name_template[] = "/tmp/captured_stream.XXXXXX";
10513# endif // GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID
10514 const int captured_fd = mkstemp(name_template);
10515 filename_ = name_template;
10516# endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
10517 fflush(NULL);
10518 dup2(captured_fd, fd_);
10519 close(captured_fd);
10520 }
10521
10522 ~CapturedStream() {
10523 remove(filename_.c_str());
10524 }
10525
10526 std::string GetCapturedString() {
10527 if (uncaptured_fd_ != -1) {
10528 // Restores the original stream.
10529 fflush(NULL);
10530 dup2(uncaptured_fd_, fd_);
10531 close(uncaptured_fd_);
10532 uncaptured_fd_ = -1;
10533 }
10534
10535 FILE* const file = posix::FOpen(filename_.c_str(), "r");
10536 const std::string content = ReadEntireFile(file);
10537 posix::FClose(file);
10538 return content;
10539 }
10540
10541 private:
10542 const int fd_; // A stream to capture.
10543 int uncaptured_fd_;
10544 // Name of the temporary file holding the stderr output.
10545 ::std::string filename_;
10546
10547 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(CapturedStream);
10548};

10555// Starts capturing an output stream (stdout/stderr).
10556static void CaptureStream(int fd, const char* stream_name,
10557 CapturedStream** stream) {
10558 if (*stream != NULL) {
10559 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Only one " << stream_name
10560 << " capturer can exist at a time.";
10561 }
10562 *stream = new CapturedStream(fd);
10563}

10565// Stops capturing the output stream and returns the captured string.
10566static std::string GetCapturedStream(CapturedStream** captured_stream) {
10567 const std::string content = (*captured_stream)->GetCapturedString();
10568
10569 delete *captured_stream;
10570 *captured_stream = NULL;
10571
10572 return content;
10573}

10601size_t GetFileSize(FILE* file) {
10602 fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END);
10603 return static_cast<size_t>(ftell(file));
10604}
10605
10606std::string ReadEntireFile(FILE* file) {
10607 const size_t file_size = GetFileSize(file);
10608 char* const buffer = new char[file_size];
10609
10610 size_t bytes_last_read = 0; // # of bytes read in the last fread()
10611 size_t bytes_read = 0; // # of bytes read so far
10612
10613 fseek(file, 0, SEEK_SET);
10614
10615 // Keeps reading the file until we cannot read further or the
10616 // pre-determined file size is reached.
10617 do {
10618 bytes_last_read = fread(buffer+bytes_read, 1, file_size-bytes_read, file);
10619 bytes_read += bytes_last_read;
10620 } while (bytes_last_read > 0 && bytes_read < file_size);
10621
10622 const std::string content(buffer, bytes_read);
10623 delete[] buffer;
10624
10625 return content;
10626}

10670// Returns the name of the environment variable corresponding to the
10671// given flag. For example, FlagToEnvVar("foo") will return
10672// "GTEST_FOO" in the open-source version.
10673static std::string FlagToEnvVar(const char* flag) {
10674 const std::string full_flag =
10675 (Message() << GTEST_FLAG_PREFIX_ << flag).GetString();
10676
10677 Message env_var;
10678 for (size_t i = 0; i != full_flag.length(); i++) {
10679 env_var << ToUpper(full_flag.c_str()[i]);
10680 }
10681
10682 return env_var.GetString();
10683}
10684
10685// Parses 'str' for a 32-bit signed integer. If successful, writes
10686// the result to *value and returns true; otherwise leaves *value
10687// unchanged and returns false.
10688bool ParseInt32(const Message& src_text, const char* str, Int32* value) {
10689 // Parses the environment variable as a decimal integer.
10690 char* end = NULL;
10691 const long long_value = strtol(str, &end, 10); // NOLINT
10692
10693 // Has strtol() consumed all characters in the string?
10694 if (*end != '\0') {
10695 // No - an invalid character was encountered.
10696 Message msg;
10697 msg << "WARNING: " << src_text
10698 << " is expected to be a 32-bit integer, but actually"
10699 << " has value \"" << str << "\".\n";
10700 printf("%s", msg.GetString().c_str());
10701 fflush(stdout);
10702 return false;
10703 }
10704
10705 // Is the parsed value in the range of an Int32?
10706 const Int32 result = static_cast<Int32>(long_value);
10707 if (long_value == LONG_MAX || long_value == LONG_MIN ||
10708 // The parsed value overflows as a long. (strtol() returns
10709 // LONG_MAX or LONG_MIN when the input overflows.)
10710 result != long_value
10711 // The parsed value overflows as an Int32.
10712 ) {
10713 Message msg;
10714 msg << "WARNING: " << src_text
10715 << " is expected to be a 32-bit integer, but actually"
10716 << " has value " << str << ", which overflows.\n";
10717 printf("%s", msg.GetString().c_str());
10718 fflush(stdout);
10719 return false;
10720 }
10721
10722 *value = result;
10723 return true;
10724}
10725
10726// Reads and returns the Boolean environment variable corresponding to
10727// the given flag; if it's not set, returns default_value.
10728//
10729// The value is considered true iff it's not "0".
10730bool BoolFromGTestEnv(const char* flag, bool default_value) {
10731#if defined(GTEST_GET_BOOL_FROM_ENV_)
10732 return GTEST_GET_BOOL_FROM_ENV_(flag, default_value);
10733#else
10734 const std::string env_var = FlagToEnvVar(flag);
10735 const char* const string_value = posix::GetEnv(env_var.c_str());
10736 return string_value == NULL ?
10737 default_value : strcmp(string_value, "0") != 0;
10738#endif // defined(GTEST_GET_BOOL_FROM_ENV_)
10739}
10740
10741// Reads and returns a 32-bit integer stored in the environment
10742// variable corresponding to the given flag; if it isn't set or
10743// doesn't represent a valid 32-bit integer, returns default_value.
10744Int32 Int32FromGTestEnv(const char* flag, Int32 default_value) {
10745#if defined(GTEST_GET_INT32_FROM_ENV_)
10746 return GTEST_GET_INT32_FROM_ENV_(flag, default_value);
10747#else
10748 const std::string env_var = FlagToEnvVar(flag);
10749 const char* const string_value = posix::GetEnv(env_var.c_str());
10750 if (string_value == NULL) {
10751 // The environment variable is not set.
10752 return default_value;
10753 }
10754
10755 Int32 result = default_value;
10756 if (!ParseInt32(Message() << "Environment variable " << env_var,
10757 string_value, &result)) {
10758 printf("The default value %s is used.\n",
10759 (Message() << default_value).GetString().c_str());
10760 fflush(stdout);
10761 return default_value;
10762 }
10763
10764 return result;
10765#endif // defined(GTEST_GET_INT32_FROM_ENV_)
10766}
10767
10768// As a special case for the 'output' flag, if GTEST_OUTPUT is not
10769// set, we look for XML_OUTPUT_FILE, which is set by the Bazel build
10770// system. The value of XML_OUTPUT_FILE is a filename without the
10771// "xml:" prefix of GTEST_OUTPUT.
10772// Note that this is meant to be called at the call site so it does
10773// not check that the flag is 'output'
10774// In essence this checks an env variable called XML_OUTPUT_FILE
10775// and if it is set we prepend "xml:" to its value, if it not set we return ""
10776std::string OutputFlagAlsoCheckEnvVar(){
10777 std::string default_value_for_output_flag = "";
10778 const char* xml_output_file_env = posix::GetEnv("XML_OUTPUT_FILE");
10779 if (NULL != xml_output_file_env) {
10780 default_value_for_output_flag = std::string("xml:") + xml_output_file_env;
10781 }
10782 return default_value_for_output_flag;
10783}
10784
10785// Reads and returns the string environment variable corresponding to
10786// the given flag; if it's not set, returns default_value.
10787const char* StringFromGTestEnv(const char* flag, const char* default_value) {
10788#if defined(GTEST_GET_STRING_FROM_ENV_)
10789 return GTEST_GET_STRING_FROM_ENV_(flag, default_value);
10790#else
10791 const std::string env_var = FlagToEnvVar(flag);
10792 const char* const value = posix::GetEnv(env_var.c_str());
10793 return value == NULL ? default_value : value;
10794#endif // defined(GTEST_GET_STRING_FROM_ENV_)
10795}

10830//
10831// This file implements a universal value printer that can print a
10832// value of any type T:
10833//
10834// void ::testing::internal::UniversalPrinter<T>::Print(value, ostream_ptr);
10835//
10836// It uses the << operator when possible, and prints the bytes in the
10837// object otherwise. A user can override its behavior for a class
10838// type Foo by defining either operator<<(::std::ostream&, const Foo&)
10839// or void PrintTo(const Foo&, ::std::ostream*) in the namespace that
10840// defines Foo.

10853
10854// Prints a segment of bytes in the given object.
10855GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_MEMORY_
10856GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS_
10857GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_NO_SANITIZE_THREAD_
10858void PrintByteSegmentInObjectTo(const unsigned char* obj_bytes, size_t start,
10859 size_t count, ostream* os) {
10860 char text[5] = "";
10861 for (size_t i = 0; i != count; i++) {
10862 const size_t j = start + i;
10863 if (i != 0) {
10864 // Organizes the bytes into groups of 2 for easy parsing by
10865 // human.
10866 if ((j % 2) == 0)
10867 *os << ' ';
10868 else
10869 *os << '-';
10870 }
10871 GTEST_SNPRINTF_(text, sizeof(text), "%02X", obj_bytes[j]);
10872 *os << text;
10873 }
10874}
10875
10876// Prints the bytes in the given value to the given ostream.
10877void PrintBytesInObjectToImpl(const unsigned char* obj_bytes, size_t count,
10878 ostream* os) {
10879 // Tells the user how big the object is.
10880 *os << count << "-byte object <";
10881
10882 const size_t kThreshold = 132;
10883 const size_t kChunkSize = 64;
10884 // If the object size is bigger than kThreshold, we'll have to omit
10885 // some details by printing only the first and the last kChunkSize
10886 // bytes.
10887 // FIXME: let the user control the threshold using a flag.
10888 if (count < kThreshold) {
10889 PrintByteSegmentInObjectTo(obj_bytes, 0, count, os);
10890 } else {
10891 PrintByteSegmentInObjectTo(obj_bytes, 0, kChunkSize, os);
10892 *os << " ... ";
10893 // Rounds up to 2-byte boundary.
10894 const size_t resume_pos = (count - kChunkSize + 1)/2*2;
10895 PrintByteSegmentInObjectTo(obj_bytes, resume_pos, count - resume_pos, os);
10896 }
10897 *os << ">";
10898}

10904// Delegates to PrintBytesInObjectToImpl() to print the bytes in the
10905// given object. The delegation simplifies the implementation, which
10906// uses the << operator and thus is easier done outside of the
10907// ::testing::internal namespace, which contains a << operator that
10908// sometimes conflicts with the one in STL.
10909void PrintBytesInObjectTo(const unsigned char* obj_bytes, size_t count,
10910 ostream* os) {
10911 PrintBytesInObjectToImpl(obj_bytes, count, os);
10912}
